packetInstructions: Note the October 1, 2027 gate in product copy from day one.

Motion content, § 16-806(c)(1): the motion must state all of the movant's unsealed and unexpunged citations, arrests, charges, and convictions as reasonably known, the grounds for eligibility, and facts in support. If the motion does not comply, the movant has 30 days after notice to amend, or the motion is dismissed without prejudice.

Scope relief, § 16-806(h): the movant need not satisfy the waiting periods for all records and need not seek relief for every eligible record. Packets can be scoped to what the person actually wants cleared.

The prosecutor is not required to respond. Under § 16-806(d) the motion is served on the prosecutor, but the prosecutor need not respond unless the court orders it. Do not tell users to expect an opposition by default.

Repeat-motion limits: under § 16-806(i)(6), after a denial the court entertains a second motion no sooner than one year, and a third and final motion no sooner than one year after that. A temporary provision, § 16-806(i)(7), exempts motions dismissed between March 1, 2025 and July 14, 2025 from the one-year wait.

Completion of the sentence, § 16-801(2), is unconditional discharge from incarceration, commitment, probation, parole, or supervised release, whichever is latest, and nonpayment of fines, restitution, or other monetary assessments does not prevent completion.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.
The certificate of service must name both the arresting law enforcement agency and the prosecuting attorney. This notice set is broader than the other § 35-3-37(j) routes.
The packet must say that the relief restricts the felony charge only and does not reach the misdemeanour conviction.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.
The packet must say that the case is still pending and has not been resolved. A participant who believes a dead docket is the same as a dismissal is wrong, and the copy must say so.
The participant obtains the docket showing the date the charge was placed on the dead docket, which is what starts the 12 months.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.
The participant obtains and attaches the order vacating or reversing the conviction and the record showing the decision became final through completion of the appellate process.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.
The packet must say that Georgia restriction reaches Georgia records only and does not touch the demanding state's records or the FBI Identity History Summary.
The certificate of service must name both the arresting law enforcement agency and the prosecuting attorney.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.
The packet must tell the participant to follow up at day 31, because the facility must restrict within 30 days of the request.
Offer this route as a standard follow-on step after the restriction and sealing routes. Restriction at GCIC and sealing at the clerk do not automatically reach the jail's own records.

Prior restriction is the statutory precondition of the request and is a required-before-submission item, not a condition of generating the request.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.
The packet must tell the participant to follow up at day 31, because the facility must restrict within 30 days of the request.
Offer this route as a standard follow-on step after the restriction and sealing routes. Restriction at GCIC and sealing at the clerk do not automatically reach the jail's own records.

The participant obtains and encloses proof that the offence is already restricted — the criminal history report showing the cycle as restricted, or the restricting order. Prior restriction is the statutory precondition of the request and is a required-before-submission item, not a condition of generating the request.

packetInstructions: The prosecuting attorney receives notice of the petition. Notice is not a request for consent, there is no advance-consent gate on this route, and the packet must not describe one.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

The packet must say that the court shall order restriction and sealing within 90 days of filing, that the clerk then seals every document in its custody within 60 days, and that law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers must restrict within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order.
The participant obtains and attaches the final disposition showing the First Offender sentence as Exhibit A.

packetInstructions: The prosecuting attorney receives notice of the petition. Notice is not a request for consent, there is no advance-consent gate on this route, and the packet must not describe one.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

The packet must say that the court shall order sealing within 90 days of filing, that the clerk then seals every document in its custody within 60 days, and that the court shall also order law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers to restrict, with 30 days to comply after they receive a copy.
The participant obtains and attaches the final disposition showing the First Offender sentence, and the discharge order where one was entered, as Exhibit A.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: Statewide staged Hawaii process: court order from the sentencing court, then HCJDC application.

rules.filing: Stage one: file a written motion in the existing penal case, in the court that entered the judgment. Stage two: submit the HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center with a copy of the signed order attached.
rules.fees: No fee is prescribed by the statute on any of the five stage-one routes, and the Judiciary publishes no filing fee for a motion filed in an existing penal case. What remains open is clerk cost practice, which is recorded as a release-level question rather than answered here. An HCJDC application fee applies at stage two.
rules.feeWaiver: None arises from the statute. Haw. R. Penal P. Form B, the Request to Proceed Without Paying Filing Fees, is the companion to the Rule 40 post-conviction petition and is not a component of an expungement packet.
rules.notice: No statutory notice. Not one of the five provisions requires notice to the prosecuting attorney, to a victim, to the Attorney General, to the Data Center or to any agency. The notice that exists is the service every filed document receives.
rules.service: Haw. R. Penal P. 49(a): all written submissions to the court shall be served upon each of the parties promptly after filing. The prosecuting attorney is a party to the underlying penal case and is served under that rule. Proof of service is required by Haw. R. Penal P. 49(c), so a certificate of service is part of the stage-one filing.
rules.participantSignature: The participant signs the motion personally, and signs the Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) declaration.
rules.notarization: None. Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) permits an unsworn declaration in lieu of an affidavit, subscribed as true under penalty of law and dated, which removes any notarization requirement from the stage-one filing.

rules.notice: Service is made in accordance with the Indiana Rules of Trial Procedure under I.C. 35-38-9-8(e). The prosecuting attorney must respond no later than 30 days after receipt and waives objection by failing to respond, under I.C. 35-38-9-8(g). rules.service: In accordance with the Indiana Rules of Trial Procedure, I.C. 35-38-9-8(e).

packetInstructions: The packet carries a hearing-preparation document putting the four K.S.A. 21-6614(h) findings in plain language and prompting the participant to assemble their own account of the intervening years and their own supporting documents. Three of the four findings are unpleaded by the official petition. LegalEase does not write the participant's account of their own life and does not predict the outcome.

The packet must tell the participant exactly who completes what and in what order: which documents are for the clerk, which are brought to the hearing for the judge, and which goes to the KBI. A packet that hands someone five documents without saying so fails at the counter.
The required number of copies varies by county and there is no statewide answer. The packet instructs the participant to confirm the copy count with the clerk before filing.

Consumer copy must carry the disclosure carve-outs. After expungement the participant is treated as not having been arrested, convicted or diverted and may say so, but K.S.A. 21-6614(i)(2) lists twelve contexts where the arrest, conviction or diversion must still be disclosed, including law enforcement employment, a commercial driver's licence, bar admission, private detective and private patrol work, KDADS institutions, the Kansas lottery, racing and gaming, expanded lottery act positions, state and tribal gaming, securities registration, bail enforcement licensure, and insurance producer or public adjuster licensure for a fraudulent insurance act. Subsection (l) lists eighteen categories of requestor to whom the custodian may still disclose.

Always offer the fee-waiver request. K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3) is the only fee waiver in the section and it must be asked for. LegalEase prepares the request from the participant's own facts and does not argue it.

On this lane the court need only find that no felony proceeding is presently pending or being instituted. The two-year no-felony-conviction lookback does not apply, and the packet must not ask for or plead it as though it did.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: The court with trial jurisdiction over the offence in the parish of arrest, under Article 972.1: district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts.

rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

packetInstructions: Route every participant through Art. 988 before filing. The fee waiver certification goes to the district attorney first and comes back in 15 days. Filing without it costs $550 that is nonrefundable even on denial. This is the highest-dollar sequencing rule in any jurisdiction reviewed.
Build the sixty-day background check clock into the packet sequence, and the thirty-day feel of it: order the check, assemble certifications, file while it is fresh.
Capture the original arrest charge, not the amended charge, plus arrest number, SID, agency item number, and every count. Louisiana State Police names these as the common fatal errors.

rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

rules.filing: File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. Since 1 August 2015 the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information is on the same sixty-day period as everyone else. Article 980(C) lets the court grant one extension of not more than thirty days beyond the original sixty. A timely objection means a contradictory hearing, which the objecting party must ask to have set. Where an Affidavit of No Opposition executed by each named agency is attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order states that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte. On the Article 978(E) lane a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself, so the ex parte route is not available there and the objection window is not the operative constraint.
rules.service: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.
rules.participantSignature: The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.fees: Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles. On the first offender pardon route the participant must also have paid the underlying court costs of the conviction, which is a precondition of the pardon rather than an expungement fee.
rules.feeWaiver: Article 983(F) through the Article 988 form in principle, but Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony. On a felony conviction track the exemption will almost never be available, and the packet says so rather than implying a waiver that will be refused.

rules.notice: Under Article 980 any entity served under Article 979 may object by filing an affidavit of response, with reasons and with service on the defendant, within sixty days from the date of service of the motion. rules.filing: Nothing is filed on the base branch: § 703(2) confidentiality is automatic and no court has any role. On the correction branch the participant sends the § 709 request in writing to the criminal justice agency that holds the record, principally the State Bureau of Identification, in person or by mail. There is no official form and the statute prescribes none.
rules.fees: None for the confidentiality itself and none for a § 709 request. The Bureau charges a fee for the participant's own criminal history record search and a higher fee for a notarised background check; confirm current amounts with the Bureau rather than publishing a figure.

rules.notice: None. There is no opposing party, no objection period and no hearing. Under § 709(2) the agency has fifteen days to investigate and notify the requester of its decision, with reasons for any refusal.
rules.service: Not applicable. The participant sends the request directly to the agency and serves no one else.
rules.participantSignature: The participant signs the § 709 request. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.notarization: none for the § 709 request. A notarised Bureau background check is a separate, optional record product.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: Not applicable at the dispute stage. The letter goes to the screening service's own dispute address, wherever the service is located; § 1500-EE deems a foreign-corporation service that disseminates Maine criminal history record information, or obtains records from a Maine government entity or court, to consent to service and jurisdiction in Maine.

rules.filing: Nothing is filed with any court. The participant sends the signed dispute letter, with its enclosures, to the business screening service's published dispute address, in a way that lets receipt be evidenced. Send copies of enclosures and keep the originals.
rules.fees: None. § 1500-CC requires the business screening service to investigate the disputed record without charge. The participant may pay a Bureau fee for their own criminal history record and a clerk's copy fee for the sealing order; neither is a fee for this route.
rules.feeWaiver: none — there is no fee to waive.
rules.notice: The service must notify the subject of the results of the investigation within thirty days from the date it receives notice of the dispute, stating whether the investigation was completed or terminated and what records were corrected or deleted (§ 1500-CC(4)). A service may terminate an investigation it reasonably determines is frivolous, but must then state the specific reasons and describe the information it requires (§ 1500-CC(3)).
rules.service: Not applicable. There is no opposing party to serve. The participant sends the letter to the vendor and to no one else.
rules.participantSignature: The participant signs the dispute letter. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: The court in which the person pled guilty or was sentenced (§ 610.130.1). This is the court of plea or sentence, which for an ordinance violation will often be a municipal division and for a state misdemeanor an associate circuit division. It is not the county of arrest and it is not a freely chosen circuit court.
authority: S.S. v. Mitchell, 289 S.W.3d 797 (Mo. App. E.D. 2009)

rules.filing: An application filed with the clerk of the court in which the participant pled guilty or was sentenced (§ 610.130.1). Whether that court opens a new case or accepts the application under the original case number is local practice and is confirmed with the clerk. No Office of the State Courts Administrator form exists for this section, so the application and proposed order are LegalEase-drafted against the statutory contents and the track carries a local-form override for any circuit or municipal division that publishes its own.
rules.fees: Not fixed by the section and county-variable. The participant confirms the filing fee and costs with the clerk of the court of plea before filing. No fee figure is published on this track. The participant separately pays for the driver record, the certified docket and the Highway Patrol search.
rules.feeWaiver: GN10 under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040 where the filing court accepts the statewide form. Municipal divisions vary, and the participant confirms with the clerk.
rules.notice: Not prescribed by § 610.130, which requires a hearing but names no notice recipients. In practice the respondents named in the application — the prosecuting or city attorney, the arresting agency, the Highway Patrol and the Department of Revenue — are the entities whose records the order would reach, and the packet directs the participant to ask the clerk how that court notices them. Whether the participant or the clerk gives notice is a local-practice question the packet does not answer for them.
rules.service: Not prescribed by the section. The packet includes a certificate of service the participant may complete if the clerk directs that the applicant serve the named respondents, and leaves it blank otherwise.
rules.participantSignature: The applicant signs the application beneath a declaration under penalty of perjury. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.notarization: none prescribed by § 610.130. A declaration under penalty of perjury is used. Where a local court requires an acknowledgment before a notary the participant is told to ask the clerk.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What was the offense? Was it a drink- or drug-driving offense, or a boating offense?
Was it charged as a state misdemeanor, or as a county or city ordinance violation? A felony is not eligible under this section.
On what date did you plead guilty or were you sentenced? The ten-year period runs from then.
Which court took your plea or sentenced you — the municipal division, the associate circuit division, or the circuit court — and in which county? That is where this application is filed.
What was the case number?
Was this your first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, anywhere? The section reaches a first offense only.
Since that plea or conviction, have you been convicted of any other drink- or drug-driving offense or intoxication-related boating offense, in Missouri or any other state?

Since then, has your driving licence been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it is the question people most often answer wrongly.
Do you have any drink- or drug-driving charge, boating offense, or licence suspension or revocation proceeding pending right now?

Have you ever been issued a commercial driver's licence, in Missouri or in any other state, or are you required to hold one for your work? This bars the whole section, whether or not it had anything to do with the offense.
Were you driving a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offense?
Have you ever had an expungement under this section before? You are entitled to only one, ever, and it cannot be undone.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this matter? Include the court, the arresting agency, the prosecuting or city attorney, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division and the Missouri Department of Revenue.
Have you checked your driver record and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

packetInstructions: Once in a lifetime, and the warning goes above the signature block. § 610.130.3 entitles a person to only one expungement under the section and lets the director keep records sufficient to enforce the limit. There is no second application.

This section and § 610.140 do not overlap and a drink-driving matter must never be routed through the general track. § 610.140.3(7) excludes offenses eligible under § 610.130 and § 610.140.3(8) excludes intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses generally.

Relief is mandatory on the findings. § 610.130.2 says the court shall enter an order of expungement where the three conditions are met after hearing. The packet must not describe the outcome as discretionary, and a required hearing is not a reason to withhold the packet.

The definition of alcohol-related enforcement contact is reproduced verbatim from § 302.525.3 in the participant materials, because a participant asked whether they have had one will otherwise answer from memory of convictions and miss an administrative suspension entirely.

The Department of Revenue driver record, any out-of-state driver records, the certified docket and the Highway Patrol criminal record are obtained by the participant before filing. None of them delays generation.

manualCompletionItems.item: The FI-05 case type code, where a cover sheet is required
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: FI-05, case type code and description
manualCompletionItems.why: The official Case Types List publishes no code for a § 610.130 expungement. Rather than guess a code from a similar track name, the packet leaves the field blank and instructs the participant to ask the clerk which code that court uses.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number in the caption
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Application, proposed order and cover-sheet captions
manualCompletionItems.why: Assigned by the clerk if a new case is opened; supplied by the participant from the certified docket if the application is filed under the original number.

manualCompletionItems.item: The applicant's signature and date
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Application, below the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own sworn statement.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.130.2 makes the findings the court's to make after hearing. The proposed order offers them for adoption; it does not make them.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets the hearing and supplies the details after filing.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that a particular licence suspension was or was not an alcohol-related enforcement contact
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: § 302.525.3 defines the term, and applying that definition to a particular entry on a driver record — especially an out-of-state one — is individualized legal judgment. The packet reproduces the definition, asks the participant what their record shows, and refers out where it is arguable.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that the offense was the participant's first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recited on the application only as the participant's own sworn allegation
manualCompletionItems.why: Firstness is the whole eligibility question and it is the participant's to swear to. The once-in-a-lifetime consequence makes a machine-generated guess unacceptable.

manualCompletionItems.item: The FI-05 case type code is left blank where a cover sheet is required, because the official Case Types List publishes no code for this section. The participant asks the clerk rather than the packet guessing.
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Missouri Department of Revenue driver record. Order your Missouri driver record from the Department of Revenue. It is the document that shows administrative suspensions and revocations under §§ 302.500 to 302.540 and chemical-test refusals, which are alcohol-related enforcement contacts under § 302.525.3 even where no conviction followed. A participant who answers the enforcement-contact question from memory will very often be wrong.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Since then, has your driving licence been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it is the question people most often answer wrongly." against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Out-of-state driver records. Request your driver record from each state where you have been licensed. § 302.525.3 counts a suspension, revocation or conviction in any other state, and § 610.130.4 bars anyone issued or required to hold a commercial driver's licence in any state.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The licensing authority of each other state where the participant has held a licence
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the participant has held a driving licence in any state other than Missouri.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have you ever been issued a commercial driver's licence, in Missouri or in any other state, or are you required to hold one for your work? This bars the whole section, whether or not it had anything to do with the offense." against Out-of-state driver records, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the participant has held a driving licence in any state other than Missouri.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "On what date did you plead guilty or were you sentenced? The ten-year period runs from then." against Certified docket sheet and judgment from the court of plea or sentence, and correct the packet if they disagree.

packetInstructions: Once in a lifetime, and the warning goes above the signature block. § 610.130.3 entitles a person to only one expungement under the section and lets the director keep records sufficient to enforce the limit. There is no second application.

This section and § 610.140 do not overlap and a drink-driving matter must never be routed through the general track. § 610.140.3(7) excludes offenses eligible under § 610.130 and § 610.140.3(8) excludes intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses generally.

Relief is mandatory on the findings. § 610.130.2 says the court shall enter an order of expungement where the three conditions are met after hearing. The packet must not describe the outcome as discretionary, and a required hearing is not a reason to withhold the packet.

The definition of alcohol-related enforcement contact is reproduced verbatim from § 302.525.3 in the participant materials, because a participant asked whether they have had one will otherwise answer from memory of convictions and miss an administrative suspension entirely.

The Department of Revenue driver record, any out-of-state driver records, the certified docket and the Highway Patrol criminal record are obtained by the participant before filing. None of them delays generation.

packetInstructions: Once in a lifetime. § 311.326 entitles a person to only one expungement under the section and lets courts and other state officials keep records necessary to enforce the limit. The warning goes above the signature block.
The waiting period runs from the participant's twenty-first birthday, not from the offense or the conviction. The earliest possible application is at twenty-two, however long ago the case was.
Relief is mandatory on the findings: the court shall enter an order of expungement. The packet must not describe the outcome as discretionary.

The § 302.525.3 definition of alcohol-related enforcement contacts is reproduced verbatim in the participant materials, because a participant asked whether they have had one will otherwise think only of convictions and miss an administrative licence suspension that disqualifies them outright.

The Department of Revenue driver record, any out-of-state driver records, the certified docket and the Highway Patrol criminal record are obtained by the participant before filing. None of them delays generation.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: The justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the case was pending or in which the arrest record originated. Circuit court for a felony charge dismissed after indictment; justice or municipal court for a citation or lower-court misdemeanour. All 82 counties, 22 circuit court districts, and every municipal and justice court.

rules.filing: File the petition with the proposed order and certificate of service with the clerk of the justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the case was pending. Mississippi has no statewide form; the petition is drafted to the statute and the court, county and prosecuting authority are participant data. Call the clerk before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.
rules.fees: No amount is published here. Section 99-19-72 sets a fee for a petition to expunge an offence under § 99-19-71, and subsection (4) sits inside § 99-19-71, but charging a person whose case was dismissed is a contested result and county practice differs. The participant is instructed to confirm the filing fee with the clerk before filing. See the unresolved fee question.
rules.feeWaiver: A pauper's affidavit under general Mississippi practice. Not verified for expungement specifically; the participant asks the clerk.
rules.notice: The prosecuting authority receives a copy. The ten days' written notice to the district attorney is imposed by § 99-19-71(2)(b), which sits inside the felony conviction subsection, and it is NOT imported into this subsection without textual support; the packet nonetheless tells the participant that some districts expect notice and prosecutor approval as a matter of local practice. No response or objection period is stated for this track and no hearing is required by subsection (4).
rules.service: United States mail or hand delivery by the petitioner to the prosecuting authority, contemporaneous with filing, evidenced by the certificate of service.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank and does not use the archived models' 'by and through his attorney' recital.
rules.notarization: None on the archived models. Whether any district requires verification or notarization is unresolved; the petition carries a simple truth statement rather than a notarized verification.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?

How did the case end? Choose the one that matches: you were arrested and released and the case was dismissed; the charges were dropped; there was never any disposition; or you were found not guilty at trial.
On what date did that happen?
Was the case ever presented to a grand jury and indicted? Many cases are not, and the petition only pleads an indictment where one exists.
What exactly does your paperwork say about how the case ended? Copy the wording. Phrases like 'passed to the file' or 'retired to the file' need a closer look before we go further.
Was this a nonadjudication, a pretrial intervention programme, or an intervention or drug court? Those end differently and route differently.
Was anyone charged with you whose case is still open?

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The order directs every person and agency keeping official records to expunge them EXCEPT fingerprint records, and the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings. Participant-facing copy must not say the record is erased everywhere.

Section 99-19-71(3) expressly provides that the existence of an order of expunction does not preclude an employer from asking a prospective employee whether an order of expunction has been entered on their behalf. This is a real and unusual limitation and participants must be told about it. A person called as a prospective juror must also, on request, advise the court in camera of the previous conviction and expunction.

A participant who uses this track has not spent their one felony expungement. The one-felony-per-lifetime cap sits in § 99-19-71(2)(a) and applies to conviction expungement, not to subsection (4). That is an important thing to tell people and to encode.
Relief is mandatory. The statute says the court "shall expunge", which is one of very few mandatory record-clearing provisions in the country and should be the headline of the Mississippi product.
The disposition order is obtained by the participant from the clerk and attached as an exhibit. It never delays generation of the petition.

manualCompletionItems.why: Both archived Fourth District orders carry this block, which is the clearest evidence that Mississippi practice runs through prosecutor sign-off. The block is retained because it costs nothing where it is not expected, and it is never pre-signed or pre-filled.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any characterization that a dismissal was 'with prejudice'
manualCompletionItems.why: The Fourth District dismissal model recites that the charge 'was dismissed with prejudice', which is a legal characterization and is NARROWER than § 99-19-71(4) requires. The statute reaches dismissals, dropped charges, no disposition and acquittals without any prejudice qualifier. LegalEase pleads the statutory category and does not add the qualifier unless the order itself says so.

manualCompletionItems.item: LegalEase must not generate: that the petitioner meets the criteria for expungement, which is the court's finding; that the offence is an 'Expungeable Offense', which appears in the Fourth District caption block as though it were a data field but is a legal conclusion; that the petitioner is a first offender; that the petitioner is rehabilitated; that a dismissal was 'with prejudice' unless the order says so; any statement about immigration, firearms, federal records or professional licensing consequences; or any assertion that the record will be erased everywhere.

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?
On what date were you convicted of the felony?
What felony were you convicted of, and under which Mississippi Code section?
What did your sentence include — incarceration, probation, supervised release, fines, costs, restitution, treatment, or a combination?
On what date did you successfully complete the LAST of all those terms and conditions? Not the conviction date and not your release date.
Are all criminal fines and costs of court imposed in the sentence paid in full? This is a separate statutory condition.

Is your conviction any of these: a crime of violence under § 97-3-2; first-degree arson; trafficking in controlled substances; a third or subsequent DUI; felon in possession of a firearm; failure to register as a sex offender; voyeurism; witness intimidation; abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable person; embezzlement; felony procuring prostitution; or promoting prostitution?

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The order directs every person and agency keeping official records to expunge them EXCEPT fingerprint records, and the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings. This is a real and unusual limitation and participants must be told about it. A person called as a prospective juror must also, on request, advise the court in camera of the previous conviction and expunction.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?
Were these convictions in a justice court or a municipal court? That decides which statute the petition is brought under.
List every misdemeanour conviction in THAT court that you want expunged: the charge, the cause number and the conviction date. This route reaches any or all misdemeanours in that one court.
When were you last convicted of anything, in ANY court anywhere? The two-year good-conduct period runs from that date, not from the convictions you are trying to clear.
Do you have misdemeanour convictions in any OTHER justice or municipal court? Each court only clears its own, so those need their own separate petitions.
In your own words, what have you done since these convictions? You will have to make this showing in open court, and a lawyer or advocate should help you prepare it.
Are you hoping this will clear your driving record? It will not — the order has no effect on the driving record kept under Title 63.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.
The order does not apply to the confidential records of law enforcement agencies and has no effect on the driving record maintained under Title 63.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

Do not conflate § 99-15-26 and § 99-19-71. They are separate tracks with different eligibility, different completion requirements and different proof, and a petition that pleads both invites a denial on whichever one does not fit. Do not copy the Fourth District form's dual citation.
The nonadjudication order, the dismissal order and proof of completion of all conditions are obtained by the participant and attached. None delays generation.

Section 67-3-70 contains no restoration-of-status clause, no perjury-protection clause and no Title 63 carve-out, so participant-facing copy must not import those effects from § 99-19-71.
Instruct the participant to confirm the current waiting period, the correct court and any fee with the clerk before filing.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The one-year waiting period is retained ONLY because § 67-3-70(6) was read from primary authority on this pass — enrolled HB 917 § 34, Laws 2020 ch. 314 — and not because a secondary clearinghouse source reported it. The clock runs from the later of dismissal and discharge or completion of any sentence and payment of any fine.

Relief is mandatory on the statutory findings — 'it shall enter such order' — unlike the discretionary lower-court misdemeanour route. Section 67-3-70 contains no restoration-of-status clause, no perjury-protection clause and no Title 63 carve-out, so participant-facing copy must not import those effects from § 99-19-71.
Instruct the participant to confirm the current waiting period, the correct court and any fee with the clerk before filing.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: A Montana district court in a judicial district where at least one of the convictions occurred (§ 46-18-1105). The underlying convictions will usually have been entered in Justice, Municipal or City Court, but the expungement petition goes to District Court. Where convictions span several districts the participant chooses among them, and the choice has strategic consequences and is never auto-selected.

rules.filing: Unit 1 is a civil petition filed on paper with the clerk of a district court in a judicial district where at least one conviction occurred (§ 46-18-1105). Local district court filing rules apply and the Office of the Court Administrator Court Locator is the published route to local rules and contact information; confirm with the clerk before filing. Unit 2 is a mailed submission to DOJ CRISS after the order issues. Whether any district permits or requires self-represented e-filing for this petition type is unresolved.
rules.fees: $120 for civil commencement of an action by a petitioner, per the Montana Clerks of District Courts civil fee schedule updated May 2024 and issued under §§ 25-1-201, 25-1-202, 3-1-317, 50-15-301 and 25-9-506. The base statutory figure in § 25-1-201(1)(a) is $90; use the published schedule total for the participant-facing number. No fee is charged for the CRISS request. The participant pays for the background check, court document copies and the fingerprinting.
rules.feeWaiver: By statement of inability to pay court costs and fees. The judiciary and Montana Legal Services Association route participants to the MLSA interactive Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees plus a proposed order. That form carries the same non-commercial-use restriction as ER-100 and ER-200, so LegalEase links the participant to the published form and does not reproduce it. Whether a court-approved statewide fee-waiver form exists is unresolved.
rules.notice: § 46-18-1106(1) requires notice to every prosecution office that prosecuted an offence for which expungement is requested. § 46-18-1106(2) gives that office fourteen days from receiving the petition to attempt to notify any victim and to document the attempt. There is no statutory deadline for the prosecution office to respond to the petition itself. § 46-18-1107(1) additionally places on the prosecution office the duty to verify that the petitioner is not detained, charged or subject to pending charges.
rules.service: Mail, hand delivery or email of a file-stamped copy of the petition to each prosecuting office, after filing. Montana files first and then serves; do not reverse it. Victims are notified by the prosecution office, not by the participant.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition under a declaration under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of Montana, giving the city and state where signed, and separately signs the CRISS form. LegalEase leaves both blank.
rules.notarization: none. A declaration under penalty of perjury is used instead.

What is your date of birth?

List EVERY Montana misdemeanour conviction you want expunged: the crime, the case number, the conviction date and the court for each. This petition can only be filed once in your lifetime, so anything left off cannot be added later.
You have listed the convictions above. Do you confirm this is your complete Montana misdemeanour record, having checked the CRISS background check and BOTH Montana Public Access Portals?
Which county attorney or city attorney office prosecuted each of those cases?
Your convictions occurred in more than one judicial district. Which district do you want to file in? You may file in any district where at least one conviction occurred.

generationRequirements.question: Have you completed every sentencing term for each of those convictions, including paying every fine, fee and restitution in full and finishing any court-ordered treatment?
On what date did you complete the last of those sentencing terms?
Since that date, have you been convicted of ANY offence in Montana, in another state, or in a federal court?
Are you currently detained for an offence, charged with an offence, or do you have charges pending for a new offence?
Have you ever petitioned for expungement under Montana's misdemeanour expungement law before, or had records expunged under it?
Are you applying to a United States military academy, applying to enlist in the armed forces or national guard, or currently serving and being held back because of a prior conviction?

Is any conviction on your list for assault, partner or family member assault, stalking, sexual assault, violation of a protective order, DUI, or any offence whose penalty was increased because of driving under the influence?

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.
LegalEase drafts its own petition, certificate of service, and proposed order. It must not reproduce ER-100, ER-200, or the MLSA fee-waiver forms.
Do not promise that the court order alone completes expungement. The participant must complete the DOJ CRISS stage under § 46-18-1110(2)(b).

The FD-258 fingerprint step must appear at the front of the participant's task list, not at the end. It is a physical dependency of the CRISS submission and is never a condition of generating the court packet.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.

A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.

Stage 1, the call to the clerk, is a required packet step with a script. The published guidance says courts may have their own procedures or forms and that the case may already have been dismissed and sealed.
LegalEase drafts its own motion, certificate of service, and proposed order. It must not reproduce DS-100 or DS-200.

Participant-facing copy must say "sealed and treated as confidential criminal justice information," never "destroyed" or "erased." Agencies listed in § 44-5-103 retain access to the sealed record in its entirety, and DOJ specifically names law enforcement including the military and Border Patrol.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.

A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.

Stage 1, the call to the clerk, is a required packet step with a script. The published guidance says courts may have their own procedures or forms and that the case may already have been dismissed and sealed.
LegalEase drafts its own motion, certificate of service, and proposed order. It must not reproduce DS-100 or DS-200.

Participant-facing copy must say "sealed and treated as confidential criminal justice information," never "destroyed" or "erased." Agencies listed in § 44-5-103 retain access to the sealed record in its entirety, and DOJ specifically names law enforcement including the military and Border Patrol.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: The existing criminal case for the offence, under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03(1). There is no separate civil action. District court or municipal court, whichever holds the case.

rules.filing: Serve the prosecuting attorney, then file the petition, the mandatory proposed order and the proof of service with the clerk of the criminal case.
rules.fees: Not established. The statewide court fee schedule effective 1 July 2025 carries no line item for a Chapter 12-60.1 petition or for a motion within an existing criminal case, and the official research guide directs the participant to ask the clerk what the fee is, if any.
rules.feeWaiver: Not established for this petition. N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-04(6) expressly makes a municipal-to-district-court appeal fee-free, which implies a fee may attach at first instance.
rules.notice: The prosecutor must, so far as practicable, notify and seek input from law enforcement, witnesses, victims and correctional authorities under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-04(4).
rules.service: On the prosecuting attorney, under N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03(4) through N.D.R.Crim.P. 49 and N.D.R.Civ.P. 5(b). The participant serves and files proof.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03 imposes no verification requirement, so no sworn form of signature is required.
rules.notarization: none required. The chapter contains no verification clause.

packetInstructions: Sealing under Chapter 12-60.1 does not reach BCI criminal history record information or the criminal justice data system, and it does not reach federal, tribal, military, out-of-state or private-database records. The order also states that the petitioner remains subject to N.D.C.C. § 12.1-33-02.1 and that the information is released where an entity has a statutory obligation to run a background check.
The proposed order is filed with the petition, not after it. N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-03(3) makes it mandatory and a petition without one is incomplete.
Service on the prosecuting attorney precedes filing, and proof of service is filed with the petition.

packetInstructions: Say set aside, never expunge, clear or erase. Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2264(5) nullifies the conviction and removes civil disabilities and disqualifications; it does not seal, erase or remove the record, and § 29-2264(6) lists the many purposes for which the conviction still counts.

A set-aside does not restore firearm rights. Section 29-2264(6) preserves the conviction for the firearm statute, and § 29-2264(5)(c) requires the order itself to tell the participant to consult an attorney about firearm effects. A pardon is the only route.
One petition per conviction. A participant with several convictions needs a separate packet for each, and the fee position for each is a clerk-level question.

rules.filing: Prepare the petition, declaration and proposed order, submit them to the district attorney or city attorney with the repository record and attachments, and file with the clerk of the convicting court once the prosecutor stipulates.
rules.fees: County-dependent. Reno Municipal Court charges a filing fee; the repository criminal history and fingerprinting carry their own costs; certified copies are charged. Every one of those is waived for a victim of sex trafficking or involuntary servitude under NRS 179.245(9).
rules.feeWaiver: NRS 179.245(9) for a victim of sex trafficking or involuntary servitude, which zeroes every fee in the process. County fee-waiver applications otherwise.
rules.notice: The prosecuting agency receives the packet before filing. If the prosecutor stipulates, or fails to object within 30 days, the court may seal without a hearing.
rules.service: The signed order is served on every agency named in it, and goes to the Central Repository under NRS 179.275.
rules.participantSignature: The participant signs the petition and the declaration or affidavit by hand. Typed signatures are cause for immediate denial in Las Vegas Municipal Court.
rules.notarization: County-dependent; the declaration and verification is required in every county reviewed.
