generationRequirements.question: What category was the offence — category A, B, C, D or E felony, gross misdemeanour, or misdemeanour?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the category sets the waiting period and is taken from the official record, not from recollection. It drives a one-year versus ten-year answer.

generationRequirements.question: When were you released from custody, and when were you discharged from parole or probation?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because paragraphs (a) to (d) run from the later of those two events.

generationRequirements.question: Were you given a suspended sentence, and if so when did it end?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because paragraphs (e) to (g) run from release from actual custody or the end of a suspended sentence, whichever is later, which is a different trigger from the felony paragraphs.

generationRequirements.question: If this was a DUI, which subsection were you punished under, and did you take part in the statewide sobriety and drug monitoring programme?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because NRS 179.245(7) preserves eligibility for a DUI punished under NRS 484C.400(1)(b), and for one punished under (1)(c) where judgment was entered under (1)(b) because of participation in the NRS 484C.392 programme. A blanket rule that felony DUI is never sealable will wrongly reject eligible people.

generationRequirements.question: Do you still owe any fines, jail fees, probation fees or house arrest costs on this case?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the statute keys on release and discharge rather than payment, but outstanding fees are widely reported to stall petitions in practice. This is a practical prerequisite to verify, not a statutory one.

generationRequirements.question: Were you dishonourably discharged from probation?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because NRS 179.2445 withholds the rebuttable presumption from a defendant dishonourably discharged from probation under NRS 176A.850, which changes what the packet can tell the participant to expect.

generationRequirements.question: Have you asked a Nevada court to seal any record before, and was it denied? If so, when?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because NRS 179.265 bars a rehearing for a period after a denial, which the internal reference omits entirely.

packetInstructions: The petition is not the first step. The district attorney is. The state's own instructions direct the petitioner to prepare the petition and order, submit them to the DA's office with attachments, and only file with the court clerk after the DA stipulates.

NRS 179.245(7) preserves eligibility for a DUI punished under NRS 484C.400(1)(b), and for one punished under (1)(c) where judgment was entered under (1)(b) because of participation in the statewide sobriety and drug monitoring program. The sex trafficking fee waiver under NRS 179.245(9) is not a separate track but a cross-cutting entitlement that zeroes out every fee in the process, including fingerprints, criminal history and certified copies. It must be surfaced wherever a fee is mentioned.
Everything runs off a current verified criminal history from the Central Repository. NRS 179.245(2)(a) and 179.255(3)(a) make it a statutory attachment requirement. No repository record, no packet.

What is your date of birth?
In which Nevada county did the case happen, and which court handled it — district, justice or municipal?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the court level decides the venue and because the stipulation practice differs between district attorneys and city attorneys.

generationRequirements.question: What is the case number?
What was the offence called, which NRS section was cited, and on what date did it happen?
What other Nevada arrests, charges or convictions do you have, in any county and any court?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because Nevada practice is to seal a county's records as one package, and because a later case interacts with the clean-period requirement on an earlier one.

generationRequirements.question: Is any charge pending against you now, anywhere?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because NRS 179.245(5) requires the court to find that during the prescribed period the petitioner has not been charged with any offence for which charges are pending and has not been convicted of any offence, except minor moving or standing traffic violations.

generationRequirements.question: Were you a victim of sex trafficking or involuntary servitude in connection with this record?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because NRS 179.245(9) waives every fee in the process for a victim of sex trafficking or involuntary servitude, including fingerprints, the criminal history and certified copies, and because a separate vacatur route under NRS 179.247 may be better than sealing.

generationRequirements.question: What category was the offence — category A, B, C, D or E felony, gross misdemeanour, or misdemeanour?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the category sets the waiting period and is taken from the official record, not from recollection. It drives a one-year versus ten-year answer.

generationRequirements.question: When were you released from custody, and when were you discharged from parole or probation?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because paragraphs (a) to (d) run from the later of those two events.

generationRequirements.question: Were you given a suspended sentence, and if so when did it end?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because paragraphs (e) to (g) run from release from actual custody or the end of a suspended sentence, whichever is later, which is a different trigger from the felony paragraphs.

generationRequirements.question: If this was a DUI, which subsection were you punished under, and did you take part in the statewide sobriety and drug monitoring programme?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because NRS 179.245(7) preserves eligibility for a DUI punished under NRS 484C.400(1)(b), and for one punished under (1)(c) where judgment was entered under (1)(b) because of participation in the NRS 484C.392 programme. A blanket rule that felony DUI is never sealable will wrongly reject eligible people.

generationRequirements.question: Do you still owe any fines, jail fees, probation fees or house arrest costs on this case?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the statute keys on release and discharge rather than payment, but outstanding fees are widely reported to stall petitions in practice. This is a practical prerequisite to verify, not a statutory one.

generationRequirements.question: Were you dishonourably discharged from probation?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because NRS 179.2445 withholds the rebuttable presumption from a defendant dishonourably discharged from probation under NRS 176A.850, which changes what the packet can tell the participant to expect.

generationRequirements.question: Have you asked a Nevada court to seal any record before, and was it denied? If so, when?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because NRS 179.265 bars a rehearing for a period after a denial, which the internal reference omits entirely.

rules.filing: Two mechanisms in one track. On the subsection 1 branch nothing is filed by the participant: the justice court, municipal court or district court orders the sealing itself after the discharge or dismissal, without a hearing, unless the Division petitions for good cause not to seal. On the subsection 2 branch the defendant files a petition in the court that handled the case, and not sooner than seven years after the conditional dismissal or the setting aside of the judgment.
rules.fees: None is prescribed. Neither NRS 176A.245, NRS 176A.265 nor NRS 176A.295 imposes, authorises or mentions a fee, on either branch. Whether a particular clerk charges a filing fee for the subsection 2 petition is not established by the sections and is recorded as an open question rather than asserted either way. The NRS 179.245(9) sex-trafficking fee waiver is confined by its own words to a petition for sealing under NRS 179.245 and does not by its terms reach these sections.
rules.feeWaiver: None prescribed by these sections. NRS 179.245(9) waives fees related to a petition for sealing under NRS 179.245 where the petitioner was being sex trafficked when the crime was committed; its text is confined to that section and it is not authority for a waiver here.
rules.notice: No notice duty falls on the participant on either branch. Under subsection 4 the court sends a copy of any sealing order to each agency or officer named in it and each must notify the court in writing of compliance, and under NRS 179.275 a copy also goes to the Central Repository and each named custodian.
rules.service: The sections prescribe none. On the subsection 1 branch there is nothing to serve. On the subsection 2 branch the sections require only "the filing of a petition by the defendant" and name no person to be served; the Division is the body given the right to object, and whether the petition must be served on it or on the prosecutor is not established by the text and is recorded as an open question.
rules.participantSignature: On the subsection 2 branch the petitioner signs the petition and the declaration personally. On the subsection 1 branch nothing is generated for the participant to sign.
rules.notarization: None required. The sections prescribe no verification or notarization.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: The court with jurisdiction over the offence for which the person was arrested, per § 40-32-109(a). The section states that forum inside the eligibility clause rather than as a standalone filing directive, and supplies it by implication: it is the court whose records the clerk searches under (c) and whose clerk serves the district attorney general under (a). Service is on the district attorney general for that judicial district, which is the only express geographic anchor. There is no residence-based venue and no alternative forum.

rules.filing: A petition filed by the participant with the court with jurisdiction over the offence for which the person was arrested, through that court's clerk. Section 40-32-109(a) uses the permissive may petition, where § 40-32-108(a) uses shall petition. There is no residence-based venue and no alternative forum.
rules.fees: A clerk's fee applies and is mandatory. Section 40-32-109(e) provides that a person petitioning the court for expunction pursuant to the section must be charged the appropriate clerk's fee pursuant to T.C.A. § 8-21-401. The amount is set by § 8-21-401, whose current text sits in the licensed Tennessee Code and was not retrievable from an official Tennessee source, so no figure is quoted. This is the material difference from the § 40-32-106 route, which is free.
rules.feeWaiver: None established. Section 40-32-109 contains no indigency, waiver or without-cost provision, in express contrast to § 40-32-106(a)(1). Whether any general court-cost waiver reaches it was not established and none is asserted.
rules.notice: The clerk serves the petition on the district attorney general for that judicial district on filing. Both the petitioner and the district attorney general may file evidence with the court under § 40-32-109(b).
rules.service: Through the clerk. The participant does not effect service.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. On this route the petition is the participant's own operative filing.
rules.notarization: Not prescribed. Section 40-32-109 requires no verification and no affidavit.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: Statewide statute with originating-court venue and prosecutor-office routing. The request goes to the office of the district attorney general for the judicial district of the convicting court, because § 40-32-108(e) makes that office the preparer of the petition. The petition, once prepared, is filed by the petitioner with the clerk of the convicting court under § 40-32-108(a). A person with convictions in several judicial districts deals with each separately.

rules.filing: Two steps with different actors. The participant requests the packet from the office of the district attorney general for the judicial district of the convicting court. That office prepares the petition and the proposed order under § 40-32-108(e) and gives them to the petitioner, who files them with the clerk of the convicting court under § 40-32-108(a). A person with convictions in more than one judicial district deals with each separately.
rules.fees: A clerk's fee applies. Section 40-32-108(a) provides that a person applying for expunction of records under the section must be charged the appropriate court clerk's fee pursuant to T.C.A. § 8-21-401. The amount is set by § 8-21-401, whose current text sits in the licensed code and could not be retrieved from an official Tennessee source on 2026-08-06, so no figure is quoted. The widely circulated $180 figure appears only on a superseded AOC-hosted page and appears nowhere in the enacted text of Public Chapter 268. Public Chapter 719 did not change any fee provision.
rules.feeWaiver: No indigency or fee-waiver provision appears anywhere in the reorganized §§ 40-32-106 through 40-32-110. None is asserted.
rules.notice: The clerk serves the petition on the district attorney general, who may submit recommendations within 60 days with a copy to the petitioner, and who may file evidence under seal which is confidential and not a public record. The court may not order sooner than 61 days after service.
rules.service: Through the clerk. The participant does not effect service.
rules.participantSignature: The participant signs the request to the district attorney general and, once the office prepares it, the petition it supplies.

Mapping the offence to its exact T.C.A. section and checking it against the current eligible list is not something an offence label or class can settle. The eligible lists at T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a)(1) are enumerated section by section — Class C, Class D and Class E felony lists and a misdemeanour category with a long exclusion list — and the legislature has expanded them repeatedly, most recently by Public Chapter 930. The packet checks the current list rather than assuming, and any borderline offence goes to review.

Under T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e) the petition and proposed order must be prepared by the office of the district attorney general and given to the petitioner to be filed with the clerk of the court. The petition is therefore a prosecutor instrument, and LegalEase does not generate it. What LegalEase generates is the participant's own written request to the district attorney general's office for the conviction-expunction packet, with the supporting eligibility record. Both the Tennessee AOC and the TBI direct participants to request a conviction expungement packet from the district attorney's office, which is the practical face of that provision.

packetInstructions: Where the eligibility requirements are satisfied there is a rebuttable presumption that the petition should be granted, which shifts the practical burden to the district attorney general to object. Public Chapter 719, effective 2026-04-14, rewrote T.C.A. § 40-32-108(d)(2) and preserved that presumption for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), while providing that the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety. The packet may describe the presumption; it may not state that the petition will be granted.

Confirm the statutory citation with the county clerk or district attorney general before every filing. Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608, the 2026 Code Bill, effective 2026-03-25. Clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering: the Tennessee AOC's own expunction page is titled to say updated information is coming to reflect changes to T.C.A. § 40-32-101 and still reasons from that section, which since 2025-04-24 has been nothing but a definitions section. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing.

Routing added by the integrated Tennessee 2026 route inventory decision, without any change to this route's own eligibility rules. A participant refused here because the conviction is outside the § 40-32-107(a)(1) lists but who holds a gubernatorial pardon is evaluated under tn_post_pardon. A participant refused here only by the § 40-32-107(a)(3)(A) predating condition because of a DUI conviction, who completed a certified recovery court programme with a ten-year interval, is evaluated under tn_recovery_court. The exclusion list is unchanged in both cases.

Mapping the offence to its exact T.C.A. section and checking it against the current eligible list is not something an offence label or class can settle. The eligible lists at T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a)(1) are enumerated section by section — Class C, Class D and Class E felony lists and a misdemeanour category with a long exclusion list — and the legislature has expanded them repeatedly, most recently by Public Chapter 930. The packet checks the current list rather than assuming, and any borderline offence goes to review.

The two-offence pathway is once per lifetime, and the reciprocal bars across § 40-32-107(a), (b) and (c) mean a single earlier grant closes it. A participant with two eligible offences now and a third that becomes eligible later should be told that using it now closes the door.

Under T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e) the petition and proposed order must be prepared by the office of the district attorney general and given to the petitioner to be filed with the clerk of the court. The petition is therefore a prosecutor instrument, and LegalEase does not generate it. What LegalEase generates is the participant's own written request to the district attorney general's office for the conviction-expunction packet, with the supporting eligibility record. Both the Tennessee AOC and the TBI direct participants to request a conviction expungement packet from the district attorney's office, which is the practical face of that provision.

List every other conviction you have anywhere, including federal and out-of-state.
Are you asking about this because of immigration, federal employment or a security clearance? Tennessee expunction does not reach federal records.
What is the exact T.C.A. section you were convicted under? The offence name and class are not enough — Tennessee's eligible lists are section by section.
On what date was the offence committed? This matters independently of the conviction date, because a 2026 change applies only to offences committed on or after 1 July 2026.
Did the conviction occur on or after 1 November 1989?
On what date did you finish the entire sentence — including any imprisonment or probation, all release conditions, and every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment?
Is every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid in full? Anything outstanding means the sentence is not complete and the clock has not started.

Have you ever had a conviction expunged in Tennessee before under T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a), (b), (c) or (e)? This route is available once in a lifetime and a previous grant under (a), (b) or (c) closes it. A grant under (e) is recorded because the statute is asymmetric on the point, and no bar is applied against you that the subsection does not state.
Did you hold a commercial driver licence at the time, and did the offence involve a controlled substance or a commercial motor vehicle?
Did your sentence require a period free from dependency on or abuse of alcohol or a controlled substance? If so, have you met at least one year of it?
How many offences are you asking to clear? The limit is two.
Are the two offences both misdemeanours, or one felony and one misdemeanour? Two felonies cannot be done on this route.
Did the offences happen at the same time and place as part of one continuous incident with a single intent? If so they may count as one, leaving your second slot open.
This pathway can be used once in your life. Do you have any other conviction that might become eligible later? Using it now closes the door on that.
Have you received a pardon from the Governor for this conviction? If you have, a different route may reach it even where this one cannot.

If a DUI conviction is what is standing in the way: have you successfully completed a certified recovery court programme, and did the offence you want cleared happen at least ten years after that DUI conviction?

packetInstructions: Where the eligibility requirements are satisfied there is a rebuttable presumption that the petition should be granted, which shifts the practical burden to the district attorney general to object. Public Chapter 719, effective 2026-04-14, rewrote T.C.A. § 40-32-108(d)(2) and preserved that presumption for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), while providing that the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety. The packet may describe the presumption; it may not state that the petition will be granted.

Confirm the statutory citation with the county clerk or district attorney general before every filing. Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608, the 2026 Code Bill, effective 2026-03-25. Clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering: the Tennessee AOC's own expunction page is titled to say updated information is coming to reflect changes to T.C.A. § 40-32-101 and still reasons from that section, which since 2025-04-24 has been nothing but a definitions section. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing.

Routing added by the integrated Tennessee 2026 route inventory decision, without any change to this route's own eligibility rules. A participant refused here because the conviction is outside the § 40-32-107(a)(1) lists but who holds a gubernatorial pardon is evaluated under tn_post_pardon. A participant refused here only by the § 40-32-107(a)(3)(A) predating condition because of a DUI conviction, who completed a certified recovery court programme with a ten-year interval, is evaluated under tn_recovery_court. The exclusion list is unchanged in both cases.

What is the docket or case number?
What is the exact T.C.A. section you were convicted under? It is tested against a closed list of seven excluded felonies.
Have you received a pardon from the Governor, and on what date?
Did the board of parole return a positive vote to receive a pardon, and on what date?
Was the conviction for an attempt, conspiracy, facilitation or solicitation to commit an offence? The exclusion list reaches those forms expressly.
Was the offence a sexual offence requiring registration as a sexual offender or violent sexual offender, or any sexual offence involving a minor?

In your own words, is there anything you want the court to know about whether the offence was violent? After the 2026 amendment this is something the court weighs rather than a bar, and it is your account to give.
Have you ever been granted an expunction before under T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a), (b), (c) or (e)? Subsection (d) states no bar of its own, so this is recorded rather than applied against you.
What is the state control number on your TBI criminal history?

Public Chapter 719 Section 3 rewrote § 40-32-108(d)(2) so that the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety; the rebuttable presumption that the petition should be granted is preserved only for petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E). A subsection (d) petitioner therefore gets no presumption, and the court instead considers whether the offence sought to be expunged was violent and any other relevant factors presented by the petitioner and the district attorney general. Violence moved from a jurisdictional bar to a merits consideration.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

rules.filing: An ex parte petition, verified, filed with the district clerk of the county of arrest or of the alleged offence, through eFileTexas, in person, or by mail where the clerk allows. The matter is a new civil action and receives a new cause number. Justice court or municipal court of record is available under art. 55A.252 only where the arrest was for a fine-only offence.
rules.fees: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.
rules.feeWaiver: A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
rules.notice: The court sets a hearing not earlier than the 30th day after the petition is filed and gives a copy of the petition and the notice of hearing to each official, agency or other entity listed in the petition, other than central federal depositories. On receipt, DPS notifies the central federal depositories, so the filer does not chase the FBI.
rules.service: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. A state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service. The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and the petition must be verified under art. 55A.253. Both a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury are provided, and county practice chooses between them.
rules.notarization: Verification is required by statute. Whether an unsworn declaration satisfies it is accepted in practice by some clerks and not others, which is why both blocks ship.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

Where entitlement rests on the expiry of an art. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) period without prosecutor certification, art. 55A.302(c) requires the court to allow the law enforcement agency and the prosecutor to retain the records. That is partial rather than full expunction and the participant must understand it before filing.

Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
The engine must not treat dismissed as sufficient. It must capture the documented dismissal reason and must hard-stop where the reason is not one of the five statutory grounds.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

manualCompletionItems.item: Petition may not list an agency twice or list divisions separately (55A.253(b), 55A.256(c-1)).
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
The engine must not treat dismissed as sufficient. It must capture the documented dismissal reason and must hard-stop where the reason is not one of the five statutory grounds.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.
rules.feeWaiver: A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
rules.notice: The court sets a hearing not earlier than the 30th day after the petition is filed and gives a copy of the petition and the notice of hearing to each official, agency or other entity listed in the petition, other than central federal depositories. On receipt, DPS notifies the central federal depositories, so the filer does not chase the FBI.
rules.service: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. A state or local agency with a listed e-mail address must accept electronic service. The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs and the petition must be verified under art. 55A.253. Both a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury are provided, and county practice chooses between them.
rules.notarization: Verification is required by statute. Whether an unsworn declaration satisfies it is accepted in practice by some clerks and not others, which is why both blocks ship.

What is the date of the arrest?
Which agency arrested you?

Were you ever placed on court-ordered community supervision for this offence, other than for a Class C misdemeanour?

After you were released on bond, did you ever fail to appear or leave the jurisdiction?

On what date is the offence alleged to have been committed?

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

manualCompletionItems.item: Petition may not list an agency twice or list divisions separately (55A.253(b), 55A.256(c-1)).
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district clerk of the county where the petition will be filed

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Which agencies and entities are likely to hold records of this arrest? Obtain Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution. Ask the clerk for the court file and cause number. Some counties also want a certified disposition attached; ask when you call about the agency list.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district or county clerk in that county
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where a charge was filed.

stopConditions: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
The limitations period itself, including tolling. This is a legal conclusion rather than a lookup, and the packet does not compute it.
Any question whether the limitations clock was tolled by absence from the state, a pending indictment, or anything else.
Limitations-period computation.

LegalEase may prepare the pleading, but the limitations conclusion must be either supplied by the participant from a documented source or reviewed. Do not auto-compute limitations across the Penal Code.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: In-window: the trial court if it is a district, justice or municipal court of record, or a district court in the county where the trial court sits (art. 55A.201(a)). Out-of-window: a district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence under art. 55A.251, or a justice or municipal court of record under art. 55A.252 for a fine-only arrest. Statewide across all 254 counties.

rules.filing: In-window: a request to the trial court under art. 55A.201, with notice to the state, accompanied by the art. 55A.253 information package. Out-of-window: a verified ex parte petition filed with the district clerk of the county of arrest or of the alleged offence.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district clerk of the county where the petition will be filed

Obtain Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution. Ask the clerk for the court file and cause number. Some counties also want a certified disposition attached; ask when you call about the agency list.

Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable. On this track specifically, art. 102.0061(c) requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.

Obtain Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution. Ask the clerk for the court file and cause number. Some counties also want a certified disposition attached; ask when you call about the agency list.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
The document is not a pardon, or its type cannot be confirmed.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Which agency arrested you?

After you were released on bond, did you ever fail to appear or leave the jurisdiction?

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
Requires the conviction date and the pre-2021 statutory subsection to be confirmed from court records, not from the participant's memory.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

manualCompletionItems.item: Petition may not list an agency twice or list divisions separately (55A.253(b), 55A.256(c-1)).
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Were you ever placed on court-ordered community supervision for this offence, other than for a Class C misdemeanour?

After you were released on bond, did you ever fail to appear or leave the jurisdiction?

Which agencies and entities are likely to hold records of this arrest? Your district clerk publishes a list with e-mail addresses on the clerk's website, and using the e-mail addresses is free while paper service costs you 25 dollars per agency at each of two stages.
Do you know of any background-check company that has reported this arrest? Those are listed separately from the government agencies, never merged in.

Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?
In which county do you live? The application goes to that county's felony prosecutor, not to a court.
Why is this arrest on your record — was your information written down wrong by mistake, or did someone else give your name when they were arrested?

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

The relief is narrower than ordinary expunction. Under art. 55A.354 agencies obliterate the applicant's identifying information and substitute the arrested person's information. They do not return or destroy the file and do not delete index references.
Authenticated fingerprint records are mandatory. Route the participant to a DPS FAST location.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

manualCompletionItems.item: Petition may not list an agency twice or list divisions separately (55A.253(b), 55A.256(c-1)).
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district clerk of the county where the petition will be filed

Obtain Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution. Ask the clerk for the court file and cause number. Some counties also want a certified disposition attached; ask when you call about the agency list.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district or county clerk in that county
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where a charge was filed.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What is the case number and which court handled it, if a case was filed?" against Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution, and correct the packet if they disagree.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Authenticated fingerprint records. Book an appointment at a DPS FAST location and obtain authenticated fingerprint records. LegalEase never receives or inspects them; the applicant submits them with the application.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. The participant does not serve in the ordinary case; a certificate of service is included only where local practice requires the filer to serve the prosecutor directly.

stopConditions: The state opposes the petition, or seeks retention of records under art. 55A.302.

The arrest produced multiple charges with mixed outcomes. State v. T.S.N. and Ex parte R.P.G.P. govern whether individual offences from one arrest can be expunged separately, and that analysis is not automated.
A felony from the same transaction is present or arguable, which moves the wait to three years and can defeat the petition.
The applicable limitations period is contested, or the participant wants full rather than partial expunction and the limitations analysis is not clear.

There is any absconding or bail-jumping history. Article 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible under arts. 55A.052(a)(1) to (3) and 55A.054, and a participant may not self-identify the fact.
The arrest may have been made on a community-supervision violation warrant under art. 42A.751(b), which art. 55A.153 bars.
Venue is unclear because the arrest and the alleged offence occurred in different counties.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying case rather than clear it.
Any dispute about whether the applicant is in fact the arrested person.
The prosecutor declines to verify the application, which stops the matter before it reaches any court.
The applicant cannot obtain authenticated fingerprint records.

The prosecutor verifies the allegations, supplements arrest information the applicant did not know, attaches the agency list, forwards the application to the district court and requests the order. LegalEase cannot complete that stage and the packet says so. If the prosecutor does not verify and forward, nothing reaches the court.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: Statewide in scope with county-level filing. An ex parte petition is filed in a district court for the county in which the petitioner was arrested or in which the offence was alleged to have occurred (art. 55A.251) — not the county of residence. Where the arrest was for a fine-only offence, art. 55A.252 also allows a justice court or municipal court of record in either county. All 254 counties.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.

The relief is narrower than ordinary expunction. Under art. 55A.354 agencies obliterate the applicant's identifying information and substitute the arrested person's information. They do not return or destroy the file and do not delete index references.
Authenticated fingerprint records are mandatory. Route the participant to a DPS FAST location.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).
