generationRequirements.question: Did any felony charge arise from the same incident, even against someone else or even if it was never filed against you?
Were you ever placed on court-ordered community supervision for this offence, other than for a Class C misdemeanour?
Was this arrest made on a warrant for violating probation or community supervision?
After you were released on bond, did you ever fail to appear or leave the jurisdiction?

Which agencies and entities are likely to hold records of this arrest? Your district clerk publishes a list with e-mail addresses on the clerk's website, and using the e-mail addresses is free while paper service costs you 25 dollars per agency at each of two stages.
Do you know of any background-check company that has reported this arrest? Those are listed separately from the government agencies, never merged in.
Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order.
Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?
Was it a veterans treatment court programme or a mental health court programme?
On what date was the case dismissed after you completed the programme?
Have you ever had an expunction before on this same ground? Each ground is available once in a lifetime.
Has the prosecutor's office been asked whether it consents? LegalEase does not ask on your behalf and cannot obtain consent.

packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
No fee may be charged. Article 55A.203(c) provides that a court entering an order under the article may not charge any fee or assess any cost for the expunction.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

manualCompletionItems.item: Petition may not list an agency twice or list divisions separately (55A.253(b), 55A.256(c-1)).
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.

Obtain Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution. Ask the clerk for the court file and cause number. Some counties also want a certified disposition attached; ask when you call about the agency list.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: Statewide in scope with court-level filing. The petition is filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision — not the county of arrest. This is the single biggest venue difference from expunction, and it matters because a person with both an expunction and a nondisclosure may be filing in two different courts.

rules.filing: A petition filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, who forwards it to the court. Under Gov't Code 411.0745(a) it may be filed in person, electronically or by mail. OCA instructions state that in most courts a proposed order must be submitted with the petition. An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence, so multiple offences require multiple orders.
rules.fees: Under Gov't Code 411.0745(b) the petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee that generally applies to the filing of a civil case. Read at source on 2026-08-06: the subsection sets the type of fee, not an amount, so county civil filing fee schedules govern and no flat statutory figure exists for a petition-based nondisclosure. OCA instructions describe the total as typically about $280, varying by county, and direct the filer to call the clerk. packetInstructions: The OCA nondisclosure documents are statewide MODEL forms, not mandatory and not promulgated. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 from the Texas Judicial Branch nondisclosure forms page and from the document footers themselves, which read OCA MODEL PETITION and are dated February 2022, with the Overview dated February 2024. Gov't Code 411.0745(c) and (d) do direct OCA to prescribe and publish a form for petitions filed electronically or by mail, and every county and district clerk website must link to it, so these sit closer to a statutorily authorised statewide model than to a sample. Nothing in Subchapter E-1 makes the OCA form mandatory or forbids a differently drafted petition, and the packet does not assert that it is mandatory.
An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence. Multiple offences require multiple orders, and that is a cost and packet multiplier the participant must be told about before paying.

Nondisclosure seals rather than destroys. The record remains available to the criminal justice and noncriminal justice agencies listed in Gov't Code 411.0765, which include school districts, charter and private schools, education service centres and commercial transportation companies, and the person may not deny the matter in those contexts.
The petition must include evidence showing entitlement to file. The section says so expressly, so the packet carries the supporting record rather than relying on the petition's assertions alone.

Source correction recorded with provenance. This section carries a three-year wait with a six-month-or-longer interlock condition and five years otherwise. The internal reference's two-or-five framing is correct only for Gov't Code 411.0731. Confirmed at source on 2026-08-06.
Interlock duration of six months or longer under 411.0731 and 411.0736 is a supporting document the participant obtains. The judgment and conditions of community supervision are what establish it.

packetInstructions: Subsection (h) requires VCIC to retain a confidential special index of deferred sentences for sex offences requiring registration, listing name, date of birth, offence and docket number, accessible only by the VCIC director and one designated staff person for presentence investigation purposes. The participant should be told the index survives the expungement.

After 2025-07-01 Vermont is a sealing state, not an expungement state. Participant-facing copy must not use expungement as the umbrella term: expungement removes records from any accessible database and destroys the paper file, sealing moves them into a confidential file without destroying them, and after Act 60 expungement survives only for conduct that is no longer criminal.

Expunged and sealed records may still appear in a federal criminal background check. Vermont relief does not reach federal records even though VCIC notifies the FBI's National Crime Information Center.
The record is not expunged until restitution has been paid in full. This is a statutory bar on the relief, not merely a document the participant gathers.

packetInstructions: Written notice to the prosecuting attorney is a DV eligibility condition, not a courtesy.

Where the current application covers more than one conviction arising out of a single incident, none of those convictions counts as a previous DV conviction. That is a favorable rule and it changes how a packet should be bundled.

RCW 9.96.060(8)(b) states that a vacated DV conviction is not considered a conviction of such an offense for the purposes of 27 C.F.R. 478.11, and bars the state from using it in a later prosecution except for three enumerated categories. It should be stated precisely, because it is one of the few concrete wins vacation delivers.
Vacation does not make the court record private, or remove the case from court indexes and public court websites. Never call Washington vacation expungement.
Vacation does not restore firearm rights, which run through RCW 9.41.041.

Vacated convictions still count for recidivist charging. RCW 9.96.060(8)(c) provides that a conviction vacated on or after 2019-07-28 qualifies as a prior conviction for the purpose of charging a present recidivist offense committed on or after that date.
Local county superior court rules may require additional documents. Every packet carries a local-check instruction rather than assuming the pattern form set is complete.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: A qualified court, and RCW 9.97.010(2) closes the set: a Washington superior court in the county where the applicant resides, or the superior court of the county that sentenced or adjudicated them. Where the sentencing or adjudicating court was a court of limited jurisdiction, the qualified court is the superior court of that county of conviction or adjudication; the district or municipal court that convicted the applicant is never itself a qualified court. Because the set is closed and statutory, one statewide packet serves the whole state as to venue and the county is a participant answer rather than a routing branch. The packet routes to the superior court of the county of the applicant's conviction or adjudication, because RCW 9.97.020(8) provides that court may not decline to consider the application.

rules.filing: File the application, the proposed certificate and order, and the notice package with the superior court clerk of a qualified county under RCW 9.97.010(2), as a civil action under RCW 9.97.020(7). The packet routes to the county of conviction or adjudication, whose superior court may not decline to consider the application under RCW 9.97.020(8). Confirming intake with the clerk is prudent practice, not a legal prerequisite, and not a condition of generation.
rules.fees: A superior court civil filing fee applies. rules.feeWaiver: A participant who cannot afford the filing fee may ask the court for a waiver by GR 34 motion, which is the route the Administrative Office of the Courts' instructions name.

rules.service: The applicant sends the notice to each prosecuting attorney RCW 9.97.020(6) names and files proof of service with the petition; the Administrative Office of the Courts publishes CRO 01.0300 as the pattern proof of service and its instructions direct the applicant to bring the notices to the clerk with the petition.

packetInstructions: The waiting period is decided from the Revised Statutes section of conviction and from nothing else. One year applies where the section of conviction is W.S. 6-4-305(b), which § 6-4-305(e) expressly labels a status offense under § 7-1-107(b)(iii). Five years applies to every other offense the section reaches, including an under-twenty-one alcohol conviction under W.S. 12-6-101(c), which § 7-1-107(b)(iii) expressly excludes from the definition, and including W.S. 6-4-305(c) and (d), which § 6-4-305(f) makes ordinary misdemeanors. Both branches run from the expiration of the terms of sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation and the completion of any program ordered by the court. Never route the branch on the participant's age at the time, on the case having been in juvenile court, or on the offense sounding minor.

The misdemeanor packet may not promise that any right is restored, and firearm rights in particular: § 7-13-1501 restores none by its own terms, the legislature removed the provision that once did, and § 7-13-1502(m) may not be read across. It may not promise an entitlement to answer an inquiry as though the conviction did not occur, because W.S. 7-13-1401(f) is confined to its own section. It may not describe the record as destroyed, erased or gone. It may say that the court file is placed under seal, that the Division of Criminal Investigation record is reclassified out of general dissemination, and that relief is discretionary.
Disclose before payment that Wyoming allows one misdemeanor expungement under § 7-13-1501 in a lifetime, and that the felony statute carries a separate once-per-lifetime limit.

packetInstructions: The waiting period is decided from the Revised Statutes section of conviction and from nothing else. One year applies where the section of conviction is W.S. 6-4-305(b), which § 6-4-305(e) expressly labels a status offense under § 7-1-107(b)(iii). Five years applies to every other offense the section reaches, including an under-twenty-one alcohol conviction under W.S. 12-6-101(c), which § 7-1-107(b)(iii) expressly excludes from the definition, and including W.S. 6-4-305(c) and (d), which § 6-4-305(f) makes ordinary misdemeanors. Both branches run from the expiration of the terms of sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation and the completion of any program ordered by the court. Never route the branch on the participant's age at the time, on the case having been in juvenile court, or on the offense sounding minor.

The misdemeanor packet may not promise that any right is restored, and firearm rights in particular: § 7-13-1501 restores none by its own terms, the legislature removed the provision that once did, and § 7-13-1502(m) may not be read across. It may not promise an entitlement to answer an inquiry as though the conviction did not occur, because W.S. 7-13-1401(f) is confined to its own section. It may not describe the record as destroyed, erased or gone. It may say that the court file is placed under seal, that the Division of Criminal Investigation record is reclassified out of general dissemination, and that relief is discretionary.
Disclose before payment that Wyoming allows one misdemeanor expungement under § 7-13-1501 in a lifetime, and that the felony statute carries a separate once-per-lifetime limit.

No order may issue before 30 days after service on the prosecuting attorney. State that timing in the packet instructions rather than in the pleading.

packetInstructions: The waiting period is decided from the Revised Statutes section of conviction and from nothing else. One year applies where the section of conviction is W.S. 6-4-305(b), which § 6-4-305(e) expressly labels a status offense under § 7-1-107(b)(iii). Five years applies to every other offense the section reaches, including an under-twenty-one alcohol conviction under W.S. 12-6-101(c), which § 7-1-107(b)(iii) expressly excludes from the definition, and including W.S. 6-4-305(c) and (d), which § 6-4-305(f) makes ordinary misdemeanors. Both branches run from the expiration of the terms of sentence imposed by the court, including any period of probation and the completion of any program ordered by the court. The misdemeanor packet may not promise that any right is restored, and firearm rights in particular: § 7-13-1501 restores none by its own terms, the legislature removed the provision that once did, and § 7-13-1502(m) may not be read across. File the verified Petition for Expungement of Records of Conviction and the proposed Order for Expungement with the clerk of the convicting court. Wyoming publishes no statewide petition form and no statewide proposed-order template, so both documents are drafted and are complete as drafted. Call that clerk about that court's own filing mechanics — cover sheet, copy count, electronic or paper filing, whether a chambers copy is wanted, and whether the proposed order is submitted with the initial filing or brought later — not about whether the document itself is right.

stopConditions: The felony may appear on the § 7-13-1502 exclusion list. The list is long and statute-specific and is not encoded; route to attorney review.
The participant has any other felony plea, nolo plea or conviction anywhere, since the other-felony bar looks at the entire record.
Any firearm use or attempted use, including where the participant believes a Title 23 carve-out applies.
Any offense subject to sex offender registration under §§ 7-19-302(g) through (j).
The participant has already received one expungement under § 7-13-1502; the statute allows one in a lifetime.

A completed felony deferral rather than a conviction. There is no Wyoming route: § 7-13-1401(a)(i) is barred by the deferral disposition itself, § 7-13-1502 requires a conviction the participant does not have, § 7-13-301 contains no record-clearing provision and § 7-13-307 forbids construing §§ 7-13-301 through 7-13-306 to authorize expunging the record. Stop and say so plainly rather than offering either section. Where the Division of Criminal Investigation record misdescribes the disposition, a W.S. 7-19-109 application to purge, modify or supplement inaccurate or incomplete criminal history record information is the only thing available — it corrects the record to say what actually happened and is not expungement, and it is not a track this packet offers.
The prosecuting attorney files an objection, or the court sets a contested hearing.
An identifiable victim is likely to object.
Facts indicating human trafficking or coercion, which route to the § 6-2-708 vacatur outside this track.
Immigration consequences.
Federal, tribal or out-of-state records.

A completed felony deferral has no Wyoming route, and the packet says so plainly rather than guessing. Section 7-13-1401(a)(i) is barred by the deferral disposition itself, § 7-13-1502 requires a conviction the participant does not have, § 7-13-301 carries no record-clearing provision, and § 7-13-307 forbids construing §§ 7-13-301 through 7-13-306 to authorize expunging the record. Neither conviction section may be offered to that participant. Stop and refer.

Penal P. 49(c), so a certificate of service is part of the stage-one filing.

Stage one: file a written motion in the existing penal case, in the court that entered the judgment. Stage two: submit the HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center with a copy of the signed order attached.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Court order granting expungement. Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application.
Check your answer to "What was the conviction — which court, and on what date?" against Court order granting expungement, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Signature and date on the motion and declaration. — Stage-one motion, declaration and proposed order.
The case number and the judgment date. — Stage-one motion, declaration and proposed order.
Court-order number and date, and the attached copy of the signed order — HCJDC 159(b) application, order reference fields.
The participant signs the motion personally, and signs the Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) declaration.

None. Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) permits an unsworn declaration in lieu of an affidavit, subscribed as true under penalty of law and dated, which removes any notarization requirement from the stage-one filing.

No fee is prescribed by the statute on any of the five stage-one routes, and the Judiciary publishes no filing fee for a motion filed in an existing penal case. What remains open is clerk cost practice, which is recorded as a release-level question rather than answered here. An HCJDC application fee applies at stage two.

None arises from the statute. Haw. R. Penal P. Form B, the Request to Proceed Without Paying Filing Fees, is the companion to the Rule 40 post-conviction petition and is not a component of an expungement packet.

A circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected. ISP charges nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order. County totals commonly run from roughly $60 to $235; McLean County publishes $136, comprising a $60 filing fee, a $60 state police fee and $16 for four certified copies. Treat every figure as county-specific.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name?
What was your full name at the time of the arrest, conviction or diversion, if different from your name now?
What sex, race and date of birth should the petition state?
In which Kansas county and which court was the case, and what is the case number?
Which law enforcement agency arrested you?
What offence were you convicted of, and under which Kansas statute?
On what date was the offence committed? This is not the same as the conviction date, and it decides which version of the law applies to you.
On what date were you convicted?
How was the offence classified — a traffic, cigarette or tobacco infraction, a misdemeanour, or a felony? If a felony, what class or grid severity level?
Was the conviction for driving under the influence under K.S.A. 8-1567, and if so was it a first violation or a second or subsequent violation?
On what date did you satisfy the sentence imposed?
On what date were you discharged from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence?
Have you been convicted of a felony in the past two years, or is any felony proceeding pending or being instituted against you?
Are you currently required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act?
Having read the list of offences that cannot be expunged, do you assert that your conviction is not one of them and is not comparable to one of them under a pre-July-2011 offence definition?
In your own words: what has changed in your circumstances and behaviour since the case, and why does expungement matter to you now?
What documents do you have that show what you have been doing since the case — employment, education, treatment, service, letters of support?

Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.

Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.

Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.

What is your date of birth?
What are the last four digits of your Social Security number?
What is your driver's license number?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the participant holds or held a Louisiana driver's licence; the Article 989 form provides a field for it.

generationRequirements.question: Which judicial district or court handled the case?
In which parish were you arrested or convicted?
What is the docket or case number?
What division of the court is the case assigned to?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant's paperwork shows a division; the caption provides a field for it.

generationRequirements.question: Which law-enforcement agency arrested you?
On what date were you arrested? Use the arrest and booking date shown on your Louisiana State Police rap sheet, not the date of the offence.
What was each charge at the time of arrest? Give the original arrest charge and statute for every count, not the charge you were finally convicted of or the amended charge.
How many separate charges or counts are on this arrest?
What is your SID number, if your rap sheet shows one?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the Article 989 form provides the field; Louisiana State Police lists a missing or wrong identifier among its common fatal errors.

generationRequirements.question: What is the arrest number (ATN) shown on the rap sheet?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the Article 989 form provides the field and Louisiana State Police matches the motion to the rap sheet on it.

generationRequirements.question: What is the arresting agency's item number?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the Article 989 form provides the field.

generationRequirements.question: How did each charge on this arrest end — never prosecuted and the time limit ran out, the district attorney refused the charges, you completed a pretrial diversion programme, the case was dismissed, a motion to quash was sustained, you were acquitted, or a court found you factually innocent?
On what date did each charge end that way?
Did any charge on this arrest end in a misdemeanour or felony conviction?
Was this arrest for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, or for a parish or city ordinance version of that offence?
Did you enter a pretrial diversion programme on that vehicle-while-intoxicated arrest?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the arrest was vehicle-while-intoxicated, because it triggers the Article 976(B) five-year bar.

generationRequirements.question: Have you ever been convicted of a felony, in Louisiana or anywhere else, including a felony that was later expunged?
Is any felony charge pending against you now under a bill of information or indictment?
Has a court determined you to be factually innocent and entitled to compensation for a wrongful conviction?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the participant selects the factual-innocence ground, which is both an eligibility ground under Art. 976(A)(4) and a fee-exemption ground under Art. 983(F).

generationRequirements.question: Does the record of this arrest name anyone besides you?
Are you now in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour?

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification verifying no conviction of any other criminal offence during the ten-year period and no pending criminal charge. Article 978(A)(2) requires it and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request naming the exact certification and the ten-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it, and its absence is a filing requirement rather than a generation blocker.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(2) ten-year route and on the Article 978(E) lane.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution. Ask the clerk for a certified copy. Where no such order exists and Article 893 relief appears available, obtain it first on the separate Article 987 track and then return here.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Has a court already signed an order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution under Article 893(E)?" against Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the first offender pardon. Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Under R.S. 15:572 the pardon is automatic for a first offender on completion of sentence, but it does not issue while court costs for the conviction remain unpaid. If costs are outstanding, pay them and then request the pardon; this is the most common and most fixable obstacle on this route.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole, or the Department of Public Safety and Corrections
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(3) first offender pardon route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984. Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the order waiving the sex offender registration and notification requirements under R.S. 15:542(F). Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Article 978(B)(2)(b) makes such an order sufficient to meet the mover's burden of showing that a pre-15-August-2001 carnal knowledge conviction would today be misdemeanour carnal knowledge of a juvenile.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The court that issued the waiver
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to the narrow Article 978(B)(2)(b) carnal-knowledge exception.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency. The agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Optional, and not available on the Article 978(E) lane, where a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles. On the first offender pardon route the participant must also have paid the underlying court costs of the conviction, which is a precondition of the pardon rather than an expungement fee.

Article 983(F) through the Article 988 form in principle, but Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony. On a felony conviction track the exemption will almost never be available, and the packet says so rather than implying a waiver that will be refused.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name as it appears on the arrest record — last, first, middle initial?
What is your date of birth?
What are the last four digits of your Social Security number?
What is your driver's license number?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the participant holds or held a Louisiana driver's licence; the Article 989 form provides a field for it.

generationRequirements.question: Which judicial district or court handled the case?
In which parish were you arrested or convicted?
What is the docket or case number?
What division of the court is the case assigned to?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant's paperwork shows a division; the caption provides a field for it.

generationRequirements.question: Which law-enforcement agency arrested you?
On what date were you arrested? Use the arrest and booking date shown on your Louisiana State Police rap sheet, not the date of the offence.
What was each charge at the time of arrest? Give the original arrest charge and statute for every count, not the charge you were finally convicted of or the amended charge.
How many separate charges or counts are on this arrest?
What is your SID number, if your rap sheet shows one?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the Article 989 form provides the field; Louisiana State Police lists a missing or wrong identifier among its common fatal errors.

generationRequirements.question: What is the arrest number (ATN) shown on the rap sheet?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the Article 989 form provides the field and Louisiana State Police matches the motion to the rap sheet on it.

generationRequirements.question: What is the arresting agency's item number?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the Article 989 form provides the field.

generationRequirements.question: What felony offence were you convicted of, and under what statute?
On what date were you convicted?

Which applies to you — the conviction was set aside and the prosecution dismissed under Article 893(E); more than ten years have passed since you finished your sentence, probation or parole; you are entitled to a first offender pardon; or the offence is one of the six in Article 978(E)?
Has a court already signed an order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution under Article 893(E)?
Were you placed on probation under Article 893 with a deferred sentence, and did you complete the probation terms?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where no Article 893(E) order exists, because it decides whether the participant should be routed to the Article 987 set-aside track first.

generationRequirements.question: On what date did you finish your sentence, deferred adjudication, probation or parole for this conviction?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked on the ten-year and Article 978(E) routes, because it starts the clean period.

generationRequirements.question: Since that date, have you been convicted of ANY other criminal offence — felony or misdemeanour, in any state?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked on the ten-year and Article 978(E) routes. Unlike the misdemeanour track, any criminal offence breaks this clean period, not only a felony.

generationRequirements.question: Is any criminal charge pending against you now?
Had you ever been convicted of a felony before this one?
Have all court costs for this conviction been paid?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked on the first offender pardon route. No pardon issues while court costs remain unpaid, and this is the common, fixable failure point.

generationRequirements.question: Is the offence a crime of violence under R.S. 14:2(B)?

Is the offence one of these six — aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the offence is or may be a crime of violence, because Article 978(E) is the only lane that reaches those six.

generationRequirements.question: Is the offence a sex offence, or a criminal offence against a victim who is a minor, as defined by R.S. 15:541?
Is the offence a violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law?

If it is a drug offence, which of these fits — simple possession under R.S. 40:966(C), 967(C), 968(C), 969(C) or 970(C); possession with intent to distribute; an offence punishable by not more than five years; an offence eligible under Article 893(E); or an offence for which you are entitled to a first offender pardon?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the offence is a controlled dangerous substance violation, because Article 978(B)(3) bars the class and then names five exceptions.

generationRequirements.question: Was the conviction for domestic abuse battery?
Was this conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated?
Does the record of this arrest name anyone besides you?
Are you now in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour?

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 3 of CR-218 — the assertion of no other adult criminal convictions in Maine
manualCompletionItems.why: Paragraph 3 of CR-218 Rev. 7/24 reads in full: 'Defendant has no other adult criminal convictions in Maine and has not had a case dismissed as the result of a deferred disposition since completing their sentence for this offense.' The trailing time limit governs the deferred-disposition clause but not the convictions clause, so the form asks the participant to swear to an unbounded absence of Maine convictions while § 2262(3) bars only a conviction SINCE the person fully satisfied the sentence for their most recent eligible criminal conviction. A participant with an old prior that predates the completion date is not disqualified by the statute but reads as disqualified on the form. LegalEase does not answer this paragraph either way: it prints it blank, sets out both readings in plain terms, and tells the participant to complete it themselves and to take advice before filing if they have an older prior.

generationRequirements.question: If there is a hearing, would you want to take part remotely?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because § 2264(4-A)(A) provides for remote participation unless the court finds the person resides in Maine and the interests of justice require attendance in person.

manualCompletionItems.item: The substance behind CR-307 paragraph 2 — the survivor's account and the causal connection between the trafficking or exploitation and the offence
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR-307, numbered paragraph 2, and any supporting material
manualCompletionItems.why: This is the whole case and it belongs to the participant and their advocate. LegalEase prints the statutory paragraph as the form supplies it and never generates, elicits, characterises or embellishes the underlying account, never writes the causal argument, and never determines whether the participant meets the statutory victim status or the substantial-result test.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 1's recital that the crimes are eligible for sealing under 15 M.R.S.A. § 2261(6)(C) and § 2262-B
manualCompletionItems.why: The eligibility recital is a legal assertion. Because § 2261(6)(C) reaches any current or former crime it is far less contentious than on the general track, but it remains the participant's assertion to make.

manualCompletionItems.item: Every checkbox, finding of fact, date and the judge or justice signature on CR-308
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR-308, the outcome checkboxes, findings lines and signature block
manualCompletionItems.why: CR-308 is the court's order. The three outcome checkboxes — grant on consent without hearing, grant after hearing, deny after hearing — are judicial determinations and are never pre-selected.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time and courtroom, where a hearing is set
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Participant instructions, filing and hearing section
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk sets any hearing. Under § 2264(5) the court may dispense with one entirely if the State consents.

manualCompletionItems.item: The participant's signature and the date of signing
manualCompletionItems.why: LegalEase never signs for the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Notice to the prosecutorial office
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only
manualCompletionItems.why: § 2264(3) places notice on the court rather than the movant, and CR-307 carries no certificate-of-service block.

manualCompletionItems.item: Never elicit graphic detail. A single gentle screening question is the limit. Do not generate the participant's factual narrative, characterize their victimization, or draft the causal argument.
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Official documentation of victim status, if the participant already holds any. § 2264(4-A)(B) is explicit that official documentation is NOT required. If it is presented it creates a presumption that participation in the offence was a substantial result of the trafficking or exploitation. Qualifying documentation includes an official record, certification or eligibility letter from a federal, state, tribal or local proceeding, including an approval notice or certification generated in a federal immigration proceeding. Your lawyer or advocate decides whether to present anything; LegalEase never asks you to produce proof and never assesses what you have.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The federal, state, tribal or local proceeding that issued it, including a federal immigration proceeding
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Entirely optional. Whether to obtain or present documentation is a strategy decision for the participant's attorney or advocate.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Affidavit or sworn testimony from clergy, a medical professional, victim services staff, or another professional from whom the person sought counsel or assistance. § 2264(4-A)(C)(2) names this as qualifying documentation. It is prepared by the professional, not by LegalEase and not by the participant, and whether to seek one is a decision for the attorney or advocate.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The professional concerned
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Optional and strategically significant. Not obtained or drafted by LegalEase.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name a Missouri case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.

List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition.
Were all of the cases you listed charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in the same Missouri county? If they were in different counties, one petition cannot reach them all.
For each case, was the offense a felony, a misdemeanor, a municipal or ordinance violation, or an infraction?

For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date.
Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?
Since the date you finished each case, have you been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any criminal charges pending right now, anywhere?

Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction.

Were any of the cases you listed part of the same course of criminal conduct, or charged as counts in the same indictment or information? If so they can go in one petition and count only once, at the highest offense level.

Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Work from your own paperwork: the circuit court division, any municipal division, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county, the Missouri Department of Revenue, and anyone else. Add every agency whose name appears on any document you have.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Case.net printouts, your court paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?

The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Missouri Supreme Court Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and the number is not published through Case.net. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

Is any case on your list a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for unlawful use or possession of drug paraphernalia? From 1 January 2027 at the latest, Missouri will expunge some of those automatically and free of charge, and an automatic expungement uses up the same lifetime slots as this petition.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 5 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to the public safety of the state
manualCompletionItems.why: It is a conclusion about the participant, sworn under penalty of perjury, and § 610.140.6(5) makes it one of the two criteria that create the rebuttable presumption. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own facts and never asserts the conclusion. The review lists it first among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 7 — that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it
manualCompletionItems.why: The same reason. § 610.140.6(6) makes it the second presumption criterion, and it is a legal conclusion about the public interest rather than a fact about the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection and the court and case number of any prior expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether prior expungements have exhausted the § 610.140.13 caps is a legal judgment the review lists among the questions requiring individualized legal judgment. LegalEase asks for the participant's history, records their answer, and does not decide whether the caps remain available.

manualCompletionItems.item: Final verification of the defendant agency list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 1, defendant selections and the Other lines
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.140.8 and the CR360 text both say the court's order of expungement shall not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant. A named agency closes its record; an unnamed agency keeps its copy, and the participant usually discovers that only when a later background check comes back. LegalEase builds the best list it can from the participant's own records because doing it badly is the most common way Missouri relief half-works, but the list is an assertion under oath about where records exist and the participant confirms it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number in the caption
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360, FI-05, CR370 and GN10 captions
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk assigns it when the petition is filed.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and the date
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, below the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own sworn statement. LegalEase never signs it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR370, Judgment and Order of Expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: The judgment is the court's. LegalEase supplies the caption and the recital of what was requested, nothing more.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time, division and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets a hearing only after the objection window, and supplies the details. The packet is generated long before they exist.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any statement that a particular offense is or is not on the § 610.140.3 exclusion list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: Several exclusions turn on classification rather than on the offense name — whether a felony is a dangerous felony under § 556.061, whether an ordinance violation is substantially equivalent to an excluded offense, whether a § 571.030 weapons offense falls in a statutory exception. The review makes never auto-screening the eleven categories from self-report an express limitation, and it is a self-help boundary.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraphs 5 and 7, paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection, the participant's signature and date, the case number, the hearing details, and the judge's findings and signature on CR370 are all left blank by design.
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Case.net printout for each case. generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name a Missouri case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.

List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition.
Were all of the cases you listed charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in the same Missouri county? If they were in different counties, one petition cannot reach them all.
For each case, was the offense a felony, a misdemeanor, a municipal or ordinance violation, or an infraction?

For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date.
Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?
Since the date you finished each case, have you been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any criminal charges pending right now, anywhere?

Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction.

Were any of the cases you listed part of the same course of criminal conduct, or charged as counts in the same indictment or information? If so they can go in one petition and count only once, at the highest offense level.

Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Work from your own paperwork: the circuit court division, any municipal division, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county, the Missouri Department of Revenue, and anyone else. Add every agency whose name appears on any document you have.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Case.net printouts, your court paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?

The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Missouri Supreme Court Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and the number is not published through Case.net. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

Is any case on your list a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for unlawful use or possession of drug paraphernalia? From 1 January 2027 at the latest, Missouri will expunge some of those automatically and free of charge, and an automatic expungement uses up the same lifetime slots as this petition.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 5 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to the public safety of the state
manualCompletionItems.why: It is a conclusion about the participant, sworn under penalty of perjury, and § 610.140.6(5) makes it one of the two criteria that create the rebuttable presumption. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own facts and never asserts the conclusion. The review lists it first among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 7 — that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it
manualCompletionItems.why: The same reason. § 610.140.6(6) makes it the second presumption criterion, and it is a legal conclusion about the public interest rather than a fact about the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection and the court and case number of any prior expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether prior expungements have exhausted the § 610.140.13 caps is a legal judgment the review lists among the questions requiring individualized legal judgment. LegalEase asks for the participant's history, records their answer, and does not decide whether the caps remain available.

manualCompletionItems.item: Final verification of the defendant agency list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 1, defendant selections and the Other lines
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.140.8 and the CR360 text both say the court's order of expungement shall not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant. A named agency closes its record; an unnamed agency keeps its copy, and the participant usually discovers that only when a later background check comes back. LegalEase builds the best list it can from the participant's own records because doing it badly is the most common way Missouri relief half-works, but the list is an assertion under oath about where records exist and the participant confirms it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number in the caption
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360, FI-05, CR370 and GN10 captions
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk assigns it when the petition is filed.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and the date
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, below the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own sworn statement. LegalEase never signs it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR370, Judgment and Order of Expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: The judgment is the court's. LegalEase supplies the caption and the recital of what was requested, nothing more.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time, division and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets a hearing only after the objection window, and supplies the details. The packet is generated long before they exist.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any statement that a particular offense is or is not on the § 610.140.3 exclusion list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: Several exclusions turn on classification rather than on the offense name — whether a felony is a dangerous felony under § 556.061, whether an ordinance violation is substantially equivalent to an excluded offense, whether a § 571.030 weapons offense falls in a statutory exception. The review makes never auto-screening the eleven categories from self-report an express limitation, and it is a self-help boundary.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraphs 5 and 7, paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection, the participant's signature and date, the case number, the hearing details, and the judge's findings and signature on CR370 are all left blank by design.
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name a Missouri case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.

List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition.
Were all of the cases you listed charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in the same Missouri county? If they were in different counties, one petition cannot reach them all.
For each case, was the offense a felony, a misdemeanor, a municipal or ordinance violation, or an infraction?

For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date.
Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?
Since the date you finished each case, have you been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any criminal charges pending right now, anywhere?

Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction.

Were any of the cases you listed part of the same course of criminal conduct, or charged as counts in the same indictment or information? If so they can go in one petition and count only once, at the highest offense level.

Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Work from your own paperwork: the circuit court division, any municipal division, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county, the Missouri Department of Revenue, and anyone else. Add every agency whose name appears on any document you have.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Case.net printouts, your court paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?

The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Missouri Supreme Court Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and the number is not published through Case.net. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

Is any case on your list a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for unlawful use or possession of drug paraphernalia? From 1 January 2027 at the latest, Missouri will expunge some of those automatically and free of charge, and an automatic expungement uses up the same lifetime slots as this petition.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 5 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to the public safety of the state
manualCompletionItems.why: It is a conclusion about the participant, sworn under penalty of perjury, and § 610.140.6(5) makes it one of the two criteria that create the rebuttable presumption. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own facts and never asserts the conclusion. The review lists it first among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 7 — that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it
manualCompletionItems.why: The same reason. § 610.140.6(6) makes it the second presumption criterion, and it is a legal conclusion about the public interest rather than a fact about the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection and the court and case number of any prior expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether prior expungements have exhausted the § 610.140.13 caps is a legal judgment the review lists among the questions requiring individualized legal judgment. LegalEase asks for the participant's history, records their answer, and does not decide whether the caps remain available.

manualCompletionItems.item: Final verification of the defendant agency list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 1, defendant selections and the Other lines
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.140.8 and the CR360 text both say the court's order of expungement shall not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant. A named agency closes its record; an unnamed agency keeps its copy, and the participant usually discovers that only when a later background check comes back. LegalEase builds the best list it can from the participant's own records because doing it badly is the most common way Missouri relief half-works, but the list is an assertion under oath about where records exist and the participant confirms it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number in the caption
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360, FI-05, CR370 and GN10 captions
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk assigns it when the petition is filed.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and the date
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, below the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own sworn statement. LegalEase never signs it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR370, Judgment and Order of Expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: The judgment is the court's. LegalEase supplies the caption and the recital of what was requested, nothing more.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time, division and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets a hearing only after the objection window, and supplies the details. The packet is generated long before they exist.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any statement that a particular offense is or is not on the § 610.140.3 exclusion list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: Several exclusions turn on classification rather than on the offense name — whether a felony is a dangerous felony under § 556.061, whether an ordinance violation is substantially equivalent to an excluded offense, whether a § 571.030 weapons offense falls in a statutory exception. The review makes never auto-screening the eleven categories from self-report an express limitation, and it is a self-help boundary.

manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR145 page 1, the two checkbox paragraphs
manualCompletionItems.why: The review is right that the choice between the two grounds is the whole eligibility determination. LegalEase asks the factual questions and shows the participant which ground their answers point to, but the selection is sworn and is theirs.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that the arrest was based on false information
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR145 page 1, first ground — recited only from the participant's own words
manualCompletionItems.why: The review lists this third among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track. It is a factual showing about someone else's conduct and it is the participant's to make.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that there is no probable cause to believe the petitioner committed the offense
manualCompletionItems.why: Fourth on the same list. It is a present-tense legal conclusion about the state of the evidence, which is exactly what § 610.122.1(1)(a) makes the court determine.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that the participant is not a commercial driver licence holder
manualCompletionItems.why: Fifth on the same list: never assert commercial licence status without confirming it. The participant answers, and the driver record confirms their answer.

manualCompletionItems.item: The notarial block — the date, the notary's commission expiry and the signature of the notary, judge or clerk
manualCompletionItems.why: A third party administers the oath. CR145 must be subscribed and sworn before a notary public, a judge or a clerk, unlike CR360, which uses an unnotarized declaration. The two must not be conflated in participant copy.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.

manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR145 page 1, the two checkbox paragraphs
manualCompletionItems.why: The review is right that the choice between the two grounds is the whole eligibility determination. LegalEase asks the factual questions and shows the participant which ground their answers point to, but the selection is sworn and is theirs.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that the arrest was based on false information
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR145 page 1, first ground — recited only from the participant's own words
manualCompletionItems.why: The review lists this third among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track. It is a factual showing about someone else's conduct and it is the participant's to make.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that there is no probable cause to believe the petitioner committed the offense
manualCompletionItems.why: Fourth on the same list. It is a present-tense legal conclusion about the state of the evidence, which is exactly what § 610.122.1(1)(a) makes the court determine.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that the participant is not a commercial driver licence holder

manualCompletionItems.why: A third party administers the oath. CR145 must be subscribed and sworn before a notary public, a judge or a clerk, unlike CR360, which uses an unnotarized declaration. The two must not be conflated in participant copy.

manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR145 page 2, above the notarial block
manualCompletionItems.why: The petition is sworn by the participant in the presence of the officer administering the oath.

manualCompletionItems.why: Both are assigned by the clerk at filing.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets the hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing and supplies the details afterwards.
