participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.

What is your date of birth?
CR145 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What was the offense? Was it a drink- or drug-driving offense, or a boating offense?
Was it charged as a state misdemeanor, or as a county or city ordinance violation? A felony is not eligible under this section.
On what date did you plead guilty or were you sentenced? The ten-year period runs from then.
Which court took your plea or sentenced you — the municipal division, the associate circuit division, or the circuit court — and in which county? That is where this application is filed.
What was the case number?
Was this your first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, anywhere? The section reaches a first offense only.
Since that plea or conviction, have you been convicted of any other drink- or drug-driving offense or intoxication-related boating offense, in Missouri or any other state?

Since then, has your driving licence been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it is the question people most often answer wrongly.

generationRequirements.question: Right now, are you in prison, jail or a halfway house for this marijuana case; on probation or parole for it; or have you finished the sentence completely? Missouri treats those three situations differently under the constitution.
What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What year were you born? CR375 asks only for the year, not the full date.
CR375 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.
What is your current mailing address, or the address of the facility where you are held?
List each marijuana case: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county where it was charged, and the number and description of the charge.
In which Missouri county was each case charged, or the finding of guilt entered? That is where the petition is filed.
For each case, was the offense a misdemeanor, a class E felony, a class D felony, a class A, B or C felony, or a city or county ordinance violation?
For each case, how much marijuana was involved? Three pounds is the line for a class D felony.
Did any of these cases involve giving or selling marijuana to someone under 21, any violence, or driving while under the influence of marijuana? Any of those is outside this route.

Have you checked Case.net and your Highway Patrol record to see whether this case has already been expunged? Missouri courts were directed by the constitution to clear many of these cases without anyone asking, and filing for something you already have wastes your money.

If the case was already expunged, would you like help asking the court for the certificate of expungement? The constitution requires the court to issue one and it is the document you can show an employer.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where verification indicates expungement has already been ordered.

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Include the circuit court division, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division and the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county.
Have you checked your paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and is not published through Case.net. What is it?

Would what you did still be a crime today under Missouri's marijuana amendment, and if so would it be a lesser offense than what you were convicted of? This is the eligibility test and it is about current law, not about what the charge was called at the time.

generationRequirements.question: How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything.

Which happened? Did somebody else use your name, date of birth, Social Security number or other identifying information? Or was it a mistake — a witness or an officer misidentified you, was confused about who committed the offense, or was given wrong information about who it was?
In your own words, what happened? How did your name come to be on this case, and how did you find out?
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR301 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? CR301 asks for it on the face of the petition.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest or apprehension?
What offense were you named in?
What was the date of the arrest or apprehension?
Which court was the charge last pending in, and in which county? If the case moved courts, it is the last one that matters.
What was the case number, and was it in the circuit, associate or municipal division?
Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports the charge was dismissed rather than tried.

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records naming you on this case? § 610.145 lets you identify them and the order reaches every one you name — law enforcement agencies, the Department of Corrections, the Department of Revenue and any other state or local government agency.

Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost.

Did your insurance premium go up because of insurance points from this matter? If so, the insurer has to refund the extra premium for the three years before the expungement once you notify and verify it.

What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it.

generationRequirements.question: How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything.

Which happened? Did somebody else use your name, date of birth, Social Security number or other identifying information? Or was it a mistake — a witness or an officer misidentified you, was confused about who committed the offense, or was given wrong information about who it was?
In your own words, what happened? How did your name come to be on this case, and how did you find out?
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR301 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? CR301 asks for it on the face of the petition.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest or apprehension?
What offense were you named in?
What was the date of the arrest or apprehension?
Which court was the charge last pending in, and in which county? If the case moved courts, it is the last one that matters.
What was the case number, and was it in the circuit, associate or municipal division?
Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports the charge was dismissed rather than tried.

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records naming you on this case? § 610.145 lets you identify them and the order reaches every one you name — law enforcement agencies, the Department of Corrections, the Department of Revenue and any other state or local government agency.

Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost.

Did your insurance premium go up because of insurance points from this matter? If so, the insurer has to refund the extra premium for the three years before the expungement once you notify and verify it.

What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it.

What offense is recorded against your name?
What is the date of the arrest recorded against your name?

Which agency made the arrest?
What is the arrest citation number, if you know it?

Obtain Montana Public Access Portal searches — District Courts AND Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Run TWO separate searches, one on the District Courts portal and one on the Courts of Limited Jurisdiction portal, under SEARCHES, then Case Searches, then By Party. This is not optional: the judiciary packet warns that some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check, and Montana has no centralised court records system.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Montana Judicial Branch public access portals

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "You have listed the convictions above. Do you confirm this is your complete Montana misdemeanour record, having checked the CRISS background check and BOTH Montana Public Access Portals?" against Montana Public Access Portal searches — District Courts AND Courts of Limited Jurisdiction, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Copy of the final judgment from each convicting court. Ask the clerk of each court that entered a conviction for a copy of the final judgment. A per-document fee may apply. Obtain certified copies for the DOJ stage.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of each convicting court

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "List EVERY Montana misdemeanour conviction you want expunged: the crime, the case number, the conviction date and the court for each. This petition can only be filed once in your lifetime, so anything left off cannot be added later." against Copy of the final judgment from each convicting court, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain FD-258 blue applicant fingerprint card, with prints taken. Request the free FD-258 blue applicant fingerprint card from DOJ CRISS and have your prints taken by local law enforcement or a private company, expecting a fee for the printing. Section 46-18-1104(3) requires fingerprinting to validate identity and the CRISS form requires the card. Start this early: it is a physical-world dependency that people discover too late. It is needed before you mail the CRISS request, NOT before your court packet is prepared.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Card free from Montana DOJ CRISS; prints taken by local law enforcement or a private vendor

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified copy of the district court expungement order. After the court grants the petition, ask the clerk for a certified copy of the expungement order. You need it for the CRISS submission and for the copies you send to the arresting agency, the prosecutor and the clerk of each convicting court.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the district court that granted the petition
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Obtained after the court order issues, for the DOJ stage.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Filing fee, or a statement of inability to pay court costs and fees. LegalEase links you to that published form and does not reproduce it, because it carries a non-commercial-use restriction.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the district court; the fee-waiver form is published by Montana Legal Services Association

$120 for civil commencement of an action by a petitioner, per the Montana Clerks of District Courts civil fee schedule updated May 2024 and issued under §§ 25-1-201, 25-1-202, 3-1-317, 50-15-301 and 25-9-506. The participant pays for the background check, court document copies and the fingerprinting.

Whether a court-approved statewide fee-waiver form exists is unresolved.

participantActionRequired.description: Mail, hand delivery or email of a file-stamped copy of the petition to each prosecuting office, after filing. Montana files first and then serves; do not reverse it. Victims are notified by the prosecution office, not by the participant.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the conviction is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your mailing address, phone number and email?
Which court sentenced you for this conviction — a Montana district court, a justice court, or a municipal or city court?
In which county was that court?
What is the case number for the conviction?

Which offence were you convicted of? Choose from the list: criminal distribution of dangerous drugs (marijuana); criminal possession of dangerous drugs (marijuana); criminal possession with intent to distribute (marijuana); criminal production or manufacture of dangerous drugs (marijuana); criminal possession of drug paraphernalia (marijuana); manufacture or delivery of drug paraphernalia (marijuana); or another offence you will name.
If your offence is not on that list, what was it?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the participant selects the free-text path, which is an attorney-handoff trigger rather than a completion path.

generationRequirements.question: On what date were you convicted, or approximately when?
Which county will you file in? The county attorney for that county must be served.
Do you want to ask the court for a hearing? Under § 16-12-113(7) no hearing is necessary unless you request one.
Have you completed the entire sentence for this conviction?

Which outcome are you asking the court for — expungement of the conviction, redesignation as a misdemeanour, or redesignation as a civil infraction? These are different outcomes with different consequences and the choice is yours to make.
In your own words, why is this conviction eligible — what makes the conduct something that is now allowed under Montana's marijuana law, or something that would now carry a lesser sentence?
Do you have more than one marijuana conviction you want to address? Each one needs its own complete set of forms, even if they happened at the same time.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that no revocation petition was filed, where the participant has not confirmed it with the clerk
manualCompletionItems.why: This is dispositive on the felony limb and LegalEase will not assert it from the participant's recollection. The field stays blank until the clerk confirms.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that a suspended sentence qualifies
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: The published guidance states expressly that this route does not apply to suspended sentences. Where the participant's order shows a suspended sentence the packet is not generated.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any characterization of the outcome as expungement, destruction or erasure
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: The legal effect is sealing: records become confidential criminal justice information under § 44-5-103, accessible to the public only by district court order upon good cause shown, and agencies listed in § 44-5-103 retain access in full. Participant-facing copy says sealed, never destroyed.

manualCompletionItems.why: Section 46-18-204 provides no perjury shield and the point is unresolved.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any statement about immigration consequences
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: A dismissal after deferred imposition may still be a conviction for federal immigration purposes. The packet carries a warning to seek immigration advice and makes no representation of its own.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
Where should the court write to you?
Which court disposed of the charge, and where is it?
What is the case number and, if you have it, the charge ID?
For the charge you want annulled: what was the offence called, which RSA was violated, and on what date did it happen?
Was the offence a violation, a class B misdemeanor, a class A misdemeanor, or a felony — and if a felony, what class?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because each level carries a different waiting period under RSA 651:5, III and misclassification either wastes a filing or triggers a paragraph VIII dismissal and a three-year lockout. Answered from the court record, not recollection.

generationRequirements.question: On what date were you convicted?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the January 1, 2019 line selects the form and, for a violation or class B misdemeanor, may route to the streamlined mandatory route instead.

generationRequirements.question: What sentence was imposed?
On what date did you finish every term and condition of the sentence, including probation or parole, fines, fees and restitution?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the waiting period runs from the day after all terms and conditions are complete, and because sentence completion is one of only two grounds on which a prosecutor may object to a streamlined petition.

generationRequirements.question: List every other conviction you have anywhere, with what it was, where, when, and when you finished that sentence.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because RSA 651:5, VI makes eligibility a whole-record question: no annulment may be granted until the time requirements for all offenses of record have been met, and none may be granted if any part of the record is barred.

generationRequirements.question: Do any of those convictions come from outside New Hampshire, and if so what was the conduct?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because RSA 651:5, VI-a excludes an out-of-state conviction for conduct that would not be an offense under New Hampshire law, which can unfreeze a record that otherwise looks blocked.

generationRequirements.question: Have you been convicted of anything since you finished that sentence, apart from a motor vehicle violation?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because RSA 651:5, III requires a clean period, excepting motor vehicle violations other than DWI under RSA 265-A:2, I, RSA 265:82 or RSA 265:82-a.

generationRequirements.question: Is any charge pending against you now, anywhere?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because RSA 651:5, VII stops the court acting on the petition until the pending charge is disposed of.

generationRequirements.question: Were you sentenced to an extended term of imprisonment on any of these convictions?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked as a routing screen, because RSA 651:5, V bars annulment outright. A yes or an unclear answer stops the track.

generationRequirements.question: Have you asked a New Hampshire court to annul any record before, and was it denied? If so, when?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because RSA 651:5, IV bars a further petition more frequently than every 3 years after a denial.

generationRequirements.question: Do you need to ask the court to waive the $125.00 filing fee, or to be excused from the $100 investigation fee?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked so NHJB-2311 and NHJB-2328 are included where they are needed. RSA 651:5, IX excuses the investigation fee on a demonstration of indigency.

generationRequirements.question: Do you want to ask the court for a hearing? The court can decide without one.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because RSA 651:5, I lets the court grant or deny without a hearing unless the petitioner requests one.

generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(c)(3) permits expungement of certain such crimes on a showing of compelling circumstances, and the Judiciary kit has a dedicated checkbox for it. The showing itself is not template output.

generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because missing case identifiers are the leading cause of rejected petitions.

generationRequirements.question: List every conviction you have anywhere, including other states and federal court, with the grading and the date.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because out-of-state and federal convictions cannot be expunged here but do count toward eligibility and toward the offence counts.

generationRequirements.question: Is any charge pending against you now, anywhere?
Have you ever had a New Jersey record expunged before?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because N.J.S.A. 2C:52-14(e) bars a further petition after a previous criminal conviction expungement, except on the Clean Slate route.

generationRequirements.question: Were any of these matters resolved through pretrial intervention, conditional discharge or another diversion programme?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because a dismissal after diversion is treated differently from an ordinary dismissal and the participant will describe both as a dismissal.

generationRequirements.question: Were any of these matters motor vehicle charges, including DWI?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked as a hard screen: N.J.S.A. 2C:52-28 puts Title 39 motor vehicle matters outside the expungement chapter entirely, so a DWI cannot be expunged and the participant must be told so rather than sold a petition.

generationRequirements.question: Have you paid every fine, fee, penalty and restitution ordered in these cases, and if not, why not?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the waiting period runs from final payment, and because an unpaid assessment that is unpaid for reasons other than willful noncompliance does not necessarily stop the application.

generationRequirements.question: When did you finish probation or parole, or get released from custody, on each matter?
For each conviction, was it an indictable offence, a disorderly persons offence, or a petty disorderly persons offence?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the count drives the route, and answered from the official record rather than recollection.

generationRequirements.question: Were any of these convictions entered in a single judgment of conviction, or on the same day?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because that route carries no numeric cap.

generationRequirements.question: Did any of these offences happen as part of one connected sequence of events over a short period?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the interdependent-or-closely-related route also carries no numeric cap, and characterising it is where the largest eligibility payoff sits.

generationRequirements.question: Did any conviction involve marijuana or hashish, or drug paraphernalia used with them?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the regrading rules in the statute treat specified marijuana and hashish convictions as disorderly persons offences rather than crimes, and treat specified possession, use, under-the-influence and paraphernalia convictions as not convictions at all, which can move the participant between routes or from ineligible to eligible.

generationRequirements.question: Was any conviction a third or fourth degree controlled dangerous substance crime?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2(c)(3) permits expungement of certain such crimes on a showing of compelling circumstances, and the Judiciary kit has a dedicated checkbox for it. The showing itself is not template output.

participantActionRequired.description: Required. Service of the petition and all attachments is by first-class United States mail on the district attorney for the county in which the arrest was made or the criminal charge or proceeding was filed, and on the New Mexico Department of Public Safety. A certificate of service on Form 4-955 NMRA is then filed with the district court. Subsequent pleadings are served under Rules 1-005, 1-005.1 or 1-005.2 NMRA.

File a civil petition on Form 4-952 NMRA under seal with the clerk of the district court for the county where the charges originated or the arrest occurred, with the DPS RAP sheet and the disposition records attached. Bring copies for yourself and for the judge and a self-addressed stamped envelope. Then mail the petition and attachments to the two responding parties and file Form 4-955 NMRA. After the sixty-day objection window closes, file Form 4-959 NMRA with Form 4-960.2 NMRA attached and serve it on any party that objected.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the participant has served any other sentence, including in another state.

generationRequirements.question: For each conviction: the county, court, docket or indictment number, the charge with its Penal Law citation and class, the sentencing date, and any incarceration and release dates?
How many New York convictions do you have in total, and how many are felonies?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the cap is two convictions with no more than one felony.

generationRequirements.question: Did any of these convictions arise from a single incident or a single criminal transaction?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because crimes arising from a single criminal transaction may be treated as one conviction, which is the difference between eligible and over the cap.

generationRequirements.question: Do you have any marijuana convictions that were expunged?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because expunged marijuana convictions do not count toward the two-conviction limit, which can move a participant from ineligible to eligible.

generationRequirements.question: For the conviction you want sealed, what is the later of the sentencing date and your release date, and have you been incarcerated at all since then?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the ten years runs from the later of sentencing or release, and later incarceration extends it by an equivalent period.

generationRequirements.question: Was any conviction a sex offence, an offence requiring registration, a child pornography or sexual performance offence, a felony homicide, a violent felony, or a class A felony?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked as a routing screen only. A yes or an unclear answer stops the track. The exclusion list here is not the Clean Slate list and the difference on class A drug felonies is deliberate.

generationRequirements.question: Was any conviction for an attempt or a conspiracy, and if so what was the offence you were accused of attempting or conspiring to commit?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because a felony conspiracy or attempt is ineligible where the underlying target offence is itself ineligible.

generationRequirements.question: Is any criminal charge open or pending against you?
Which courts decided each conviction, and which offence was the most serious?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because venue is the court where the most serious offence was decided, or, where the offences are of equal class, where the person was last convicted.

generationRequirements.question: What have you done since, and what is this record costing you now?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because rehabilitation and the interests of justice are what the court weighs. The answers are the participant's own account and are the substance of the application; LegalEase never asserts the conclusion.

generationRequirements.question: Have you filed, or do you intend to file, any other sealing application?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because a sworn statement on this, with copies of any such applications, must accompany the motion.

generationRequirements.question: Did any of these convictions arise from a single incident or a single criminal transaction?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because crimes arising from a single criminal transaction may be treated as one conviction, which is the difference between eligible and over the cap.

generationRequirements.question: Do you have any marijuana convictions that were expunged?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because expunged marijuana convictions do not count toward the two-conviction limit, which can move a participant from ineligible to eligible.

generationRequirements.question: For the conviction you want sealed, what is the later of the sentencing date and your release date, and have you been incarcerated at all since then?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the ten years runs from the later of sentencing or release, and later incarceration extends it by an equivalent period.

generationRequirements.question: Was any conviction a sex offence, an offence requiring registration, a child pornography or sexual performance offence, a felony homicide, a violent felony, or a class A felony?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked as a routing screen only. A yes or an unclear answer stops the track. The exclusion list here is not the Clean Slate list and the difference on class A drug felonies is deliberate.

generationRequirements.question: Was any conviction for an attempt or a conspiracy, and if so what was the offence you were accused of attempting or conspiring to commit?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because a felony conspiracy or attempt is ineligible where the underlying target offence is itself ineligible.

generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the degree and the chapter drive both the exclusions and the waiting period, and both are taken from the official record.

generationRequirements.question: When did you finish the sentence, including any parole, all fines and all restitution?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the waiting period runs from final discharge. Court costs are not part of the sentence for this purpose, so unpaid court costs do not delay eligibility.

generationRequirements.question: Do you still owe court costs, as opposed to fines or restitution?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked so the participant is told the useful thing: unpaid court costs do not delay eligibility, which is a common and expensive misunderstanding.

generationRequirements.question: What every charge was that came out of the same incident, and how each one ended.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because ORC 2953.61 generally prevents clearing only part of a record where charges from the same act ended differently.

generationRequirements.question: What other convictions do you have, in Ohio or anywhere else, with the degree and the date?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the same-act and same-proceeding counting rules can collapse several convictions into one, and because the third-degree-felony counting rule can bar relief.

generationRequirements.question: Have you ever had to register under Chapter 2950?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because a sexually oriented offence committed while subject to registration is excluded, and a person formerly subject to registration has a five-year clock that runs from the end of the requirement.

generationRequirements.question: Was the offence a traffic or OVI matter, a felony of violence, a sexually oriented offence, an offence against a child under 13, theft in office, a first or second degree felony, or first or second degree domestic violence?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked as a routing screen only. A yes or an unclear answer stops the track.

generationRequirements.question: Is any criminal case pending against you now, anywhere?

generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because Ohio common pleas courts can reach out-of-state and federal convictions for sealing purposes, which changes the venue and complicates the analysis.

generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) disqualifies a person convicted of another offence within the applicable look-back period, with carve-outs for motor vehicle violations, a single non-motor-vehicle violation and certain drug enforcement misdemeanours.

generationRequirements.question: Did any other conviction come from the same incident or the same course of conduct as the one you want set aside?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the controlling review and the enacted statutory text disagree on whether a same-episode conviction counts as disqualifying. No eligibility statement is made where this is in play.

generationRequirements.question: Is any criminal charge pending against you now, or any contempt proceeding for violating a restraining or protective order?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because ORS 137.225(7)(a)(C) bars relief while such a charge or proceeding is pending.

generationRequirements.question: Was the offence a traffic offence or DUII, a sex crime, a Class A felony, a person felony, criminal mistreatment, endangering the welfare of a minor, criminally negligent homicide or assault in the third degree?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked as a routing screen only. A yes or an unclear answer stops the track, because ORS 137.225(5), (6) and (7)(a)(A) exclude these categorically and the lists are offence-specific.

generationRequirements.question: Do you have Oregon cases in more than one county?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because a separate motion is filed in each county, although only one State Police record-check fee is charged where only one check is performed.

generationRequirements.question: Were you imprisoned for this, and if so when were you released?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because each tier runs from the date of conviction or the release from imprisonment, whichever is later.

generationRequirements.question: Have you finished everything the sentence required — incarceration, probation, post-prison supervision, restitution, fines and fees — and when?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because ORS 137.225(1)(a) requires full compliance with and performance of the sentence, and provides that a person still under supervision as part of that sentence has not fully complied.

generationRequirements.question: Was your probation ever revoked on this case, and if so when?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because ORS 137.225(1)(e) bars an application for three years from the date of revocation, or until the person becomes eligible under the ordinary tier, whichever is later.

generationRequirements.question: Do you still owe any fine, fee or restitution on this case, and roughly how old is the judgment?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because Oregon Laws 2025 chapter 395 treats monetary obligations whose judgment remedies have expired as satisfied for sentence-completion purposes, on the narrow terms recorded in the unresolved questions.

generationRequirements.question: Have you been convicted of anything else, anywhere, and when?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because ORS 137.225(7)(a)(B) disqualifies a person convicted of another offence within the applicable look-back period, with carve-outs for motor vehicle violations, a single non-motor-vehicle violation and certain drug enforcement misdemeanours.

generationRequirements.question: Did any other conviction come from the same incident or the same course of conduct as the one you want set aside?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because the controlling review and the enacted statutory text disagree on whether a same-episode conviction counts as disqualifying. No eligibility statement is made where this is in play.

generationRequirements.question: Is any criminal charge pending against you now, or any contempt proceeding for violating a restraining or protective order?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because ORS 137.225(7)(a)(C) bars relief while such a charge or proceeding is pending.

generationRequirements.question: Do you have Oregon cases in more than one county?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because a separate motion is filed in each county, although only one State Police record-check fee is charged where only one check is performed.

generationRequirements.question: What kind of court order were you found to have violated — a restraining or protective order, a family abuse prevention order, an elder abuse order, a stalking order, or something else?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because this is the whole tier question. ORS 137.225(13)(b) defines an order related to abuse or a person crime by reference to specific statutes, and a finding for violating one of those sits in the five-year tier rather than the one-year tier.

generationRequirements.question: Did the order come out of a criminal case, and if so what was that case about?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because an order arising from a criminal case involving a sex crime, stalking, or a person felony or person Class A misdemeanor against a family or household member is also an order related to abuse or a person crime.

manualCompletionItems.item: Signature on the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own oath. ORS 137.225(13)(a) allows a declaration under penalty of perjury in place of an affidavit.

manualCompletionItems.why: The affidavit must be sworn in person before a notary or a clerk. LegalEase cannot supply that.

manualCompletionItems.item: Hearing date and time
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk fills in the hearing date when the motion is filed, and it must be at least ten days out.

manualCompletionItems.item: Judge's signature and date of entry
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is proposed. Only the judge signs it, and only after the hearing.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion of good moral character or rehabilitation
manualCompletionItems.why: Good moral character, rehabilitation and consistency with the public interest are the court's findings. LegalEase must not assert them.

manualCompletionItems.item: The agency and entity list, deduplicated
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(b) forbids listing any state or local agency more than once and forbids multiple contacts or addresses for different divisions of the same agency. The list is assembled from the participant's answers and the clerk's published list, and the participant confirms it before filing because the clerk bears no completeness duty.

manualCompletionItems.item: Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253(a)(8)(C) treats private compilers separately from government agencies, and merging them breaks the no-duplicate rule and the service model.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: Article 55A.253 requires the petition to be verified. Both a notarial block and an unsworn declaration are provided; the participant executes whichever the county accepts.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

manualCompletionItems.item: Petition may not list an agency twice or list divisions separately (55A.253(b), 55A.256(c-1)).
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.
manualCompletionItems.why: Counsel classified this as an item the participant completes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.

Obtain Court file and cause number from the county of arrest or prosecution. Ask the clerk for the court file and cause number. Some counties also want a certified disposition attached; ask when you call about the agency list.

participantActionRequired.description: The agency and entity list, deduplicated — Petition, the art. 55A.253(a)(8) list.
Private entities, listed separately and never merged into the agency list — Petition, the separate private-entity attachment.
The petitioner's verification, and the signature and date — Petition, verification and signature block.
The judge's signature on the proposed Order of Expunction — Proposed order, signature block.

The petitioner signs and the petition must be verified under art. 55A.253. Both a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury are provided, and county practice chooses between them.
Verification is required by statute. Whether an unsworn declaration satisfies it is accepted in practice by some clerks and not others, which is why both blocks ship.

generationRequirements.question: In which county were you arrested, and in which county did the alleged offence happen? The petition is filed in one of those, not where you live.
What is the date of the arrest?
Which agency arrested you?
What offence were you arrested for, and what level was it — Class C, Class A or B misdemeanour, or felony?
What is the case number and which court handled it, if a case was filed?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Not asked where no charge was ever filed.

generationRequirements.question: Did any felony charge arise from the same incident, even against someone else or even if it was never filed against you?
Were you ever placed on court-ordered community supervision for this offence, other than for a Class C misdemeanour?
Was this arrest made on a warrant for violating probation or community supervision?
After you were released on bond, did you ever fail to appear or leave the jurisdiction?

Which agencies and entities are likely to hold records of this arrest? Your district clerk publishes a list with e-mail addresses on the clerk's website, and using the e-mail addresses is free while paper service costs you 25 dollars per agency at each of two stages.
Do you know of any background-check company that has reported this arrest? Those are listed separately from the government agencies, never merged in.
Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order.
Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?
What does the dismissal order actually say about why the case was dismissed? The exact wording decides whether this route is open.
Was the case dismissed because you completed a veterans treatment court or a mental health court programme, or a formal pretrial intervention programme?
Have you ever had an expunction before on the veterans court ground or the mental health court ground? Each is available once only.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the ground is veterans treatment court or mental health court, because the one-time limit and the affidavit attach only there.

generationRequirements.question: Did the case end with you completing deferred adjudication? If so, this is usually not the right route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

After you were released on bond, did you ever fail to appear or leave the jurisdiction?

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable.

Under Gov't Code 411.0745(b) the petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee that generally applies to the filing of a civil case. Read at source on 2026-08-06: the subsection sets the type of fee, not an amount, so county civil filing fee schedules govern and no flat statutory figure exists for a petition-based nondisclosure. OCA instructions describe the total as typically about $280, varying by county, and direct the filer to call the clerk. The $28 figure belongs only to the no-petition route under Gov't Code 411.072(c) and is not a filing fee.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, on the statewide bilingual form approved by the Supreme Court of Texas in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, which the clerk must make available without charge or request.

generationRequirements.question: Which court sentenced you or placed you on community supervision? That is where this is filed — not the county where you were arrested.
What is the cause number?
What was the offence, and what level was it?
Were you placed on deferred adjudication, or were you convicted and placed on probation, or neither? Texas splits nearly every nondisclosure section on this line.
On what date did you complete everything the sentence or supervision required, including any confinement and all fines, costs and restitution?
Did the court ever make a finding that the offence involved family violence, or was family violence alleged anywhere in the case?
List every other conviction and every other deferred adjudication you have ever had, with dates, other than fine-only traffic offences.
Do you want to ask the court to waive the filing costs because you cannot afford them?

manualCompletionItems.item: The best-interest-of-justice assertion
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: OCA model petition, the best-interest paragraph
manualCompletionItems.why: The court must find that issuance of the order is in the best interest of justice. That is a judicial finding and the review lists the assertion among the fields that must not be auto-completed.

manualCompletionItems.item: The complete list of prior convictions and deferred adjudications
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: OCA model petition, the prior-record attachment
manualCompletionItems.why: The list is built from the participant's answers and their own DPS history. The review lists it among the fields requiring legal judgment, and an incomplete list defeats the petition under Gov't Code 411.074.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: The petition is a participant filing and must be signed by the petitioner.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's signature on the proposed order
manualCompletionItems.why: The order is prepared by the petitioner and signed by the court.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI. Submit the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History with the application fee, or with a fee waiver request. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases and may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction. If eligible, BCI issues the certificate on payment of the issuance fee. File the court packet within 180 days of issuance.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Utah Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Criminal Identification

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "If BCI has already issued your certificate of eligibility, what date did it issue? It is valid for 180 days and must still be valid on the day you file." against Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a current balance on the case, and check with the Office of State Debt Collection if any balance was entered as a civil judgment and transferred. An unpaid balance defeats the petition and will also defeat the BCI certificate.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that handled the case, and the Office of State Debt Collection where a criminal accounts receivable was transferred

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have all fines, fees, interest and restitution on this case been paid in full?" against Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The participant's own case history for every case in every state, including previously expunged cases. Assemble the full list before applying to BCI. BCI assesses eligibility against total criminal history in all states, including cases that were previously expunged, so an incomplete list produces a denial rather than a certificate.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Court clerks in each jurisdiction and state criminal history repositories

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "List every criminal case you have ever had, in any state, including cases that were already expunged. BCI reviews all of them when it decides your certificate." against The participant's own case history for every case in every state, including previously expunged cases, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Any written declination or no-file letter from the prosecutor. Ask the prosecuting attorney's office whether a written declination exists for the arrest. Where none does, the participant says so; BCI's certificate decision is the operative check on this fact.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The prosecuting attorney's office for the county where the arrest occurred
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where one exists. Many declinations are never documented, which is why the fact is asked as a participant question with an evidence prompt.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where one exists. Many declinations are never documented, which is why the fact is asked as a participant question with an evidence prompt.

The petitioner signs the petition. The proposed order is completed by the petitioner except for the judge's signature line, which is left blank. The Consent and Waiver of Hearing is presented by the petitioner and signed by the prosecuting attorney; LegalEase neither obtains that consent nor signs on anyone's behalf.
Not required by Chapter 40a or by the published Utah Courts expungement packet for the petition itself.

A court filing fee set by Utah Code 78A-2-301 applies. The Utah Courts page directs filers to the cover sheet for the current amount rather than publishing a figure, so the packet does not quote one. The exact current amount is an open release-blocking question.

The court fee waiver process applies to the filing fee, and the published packet includes the fee waiver route. BCI separately operates an indigency-linked waiver and will issue without the issuance fee where the court is likely to waive the filing fee; if the court then finds the petitioner not indigent, the BCI issuance fee must be paid before BCI will process the expungement order.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service. The Utah Courts general service-of-process page governs first papers in a new civil case and must not be wired to this track; doing so would import a summons, a process server and a 120-day deadline this track does not have.

Filed in the court that decided the case, district or justice court, under Utah Code 77-40a-305. The packet is the civil cover sheet, the petition, the proposed order and the BCI certificate of eligibility, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. The certificate must still be valid on the filing date. Certified copies of a granted order must be requested within 28 days after the order is granted (URCrP 42).

participantActionRequired.description: The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney. Obtain Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a current balance on the case, and check with the Office of State Debt Collection if any balance was entered as a civil judgment and transferred. An unpaid balance defeats the petition and will also defeat the BCI certificate.

Check your answer to "Have all fines, fees, interest and restitution on this case been paid in full?" against Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "What is the date of the acquittal?" against Certified copy of the judgment of acquittal, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "When you look the case up on My Court Case, does it still show, or does it show as expunged?" against My Court Case record showing whether the case has already been expunged, and correct the packet if they disagree.

The petitioner signs the petition. The proposed order is completed by the petitioner except for the judge's signature line, which is left blank. The Consent and Waiver of Hearing is presented by the petitioner and signed by the prosecuting attorney; LegalEase neither obtains that consent nor signs on anyone's behalf.
Not required by Chapter 40a or by the published Utah Courts expungement packet for the petition itself.

A court filing fee set by Utah Code 78A-2-301 applies. The Utah Courts page directs filers to the cover sheet for the current amount rather than publishing a figure, so the packet does not quote one. The exact current amount is an open release-blocking question.

What was the conviction, and what level was it — infraction, class C, class B or class A misdemeanour, or felony?
When did the case finish, when were you released from any incarceration, and when did probation or parole end? The clock runs from whichever is most recent.
Has all restitution been paid in full?

Was the conviction a drug possession offence as Utah defines it — possession of a controlled substance under 58-37-8(2), drug paraphernalia under 58-37a-5(1), or an imitation controlled substance under 58-37b-6?
In your own words, why is expunging this record not contrary to the public interest? Write this yourself — it is your explanation, and the court weighs it.
Have you already checked whether this conviction clears itself under Clean Slate at no cost?

manualCompletionItems.item: Public-interest showing on the conviction petition.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI. Submit the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History with the application fee, or with a fee waiver request. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases and may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction. If eligible, BCI issues the certificate on payment of the issuance fee. File the court packet within 180 days of issuance.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Utah Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Criminal Identification

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "If BCI has already issued your certificate of eligibility, what date did it issue? It is valid for 180 days and must still be valid on the day you file." against Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a current balance on the case, and check with the Office of State Debt Collection if any balance was entered as a civil judgment and transferred. An unpaid balance defeats the petition and will also defeat the BCI certificate.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that handled the case, and the Office of State Debt Collection where a criminal accounts receivable was transferred

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have all fines, fees, interest and restitution on this case been paid in full?" against Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The participant's own case history for every case in every state, including previously expunged cases. Assemble the full list before applying to BCI. BCI assesses eligibility against total criminal history in all states, including cases that were previously expunged, so an incomplete list produces a denial rather than a certificate.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Court clerks in each jurisdiction and state criminal history repositories

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "List every criminal case you have ever had, in any state, including cases that were already expunged. A court filing fee set by Utah Code 78A-2-301 applies. The Utah Courts page directs filers to the cover sheet for the current amount rather than publishing a figure, so the packet does not quote one. The exact current amount is an open release-blocking question.

The court fee waiver process applies to the filing fee, and the published packet includes the fee waiver route. BCI separately operates an indigency-linked waiver and will issue without the issuance fee where the court is likely to waive the filing fee; if the court then finds the petitioner not indigent, the BCI issuance fee must be paid before BCI will process the expungement order.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service. The Utah Courts general service-of-process page governs first papers in a new civil case and must not be wired to this track; doing so would import a summons, a process server and a 120-day deadline this track does not have.

Filed in the court that decided the case, district or justice court, under Utah Code 77-40a-305. The packet is the civil cover sheet, the petition, the proposed order and the BCI certificate of eligibility, with the filing fee or a fee waiver request. The certificate must still be valid on the filing date. Certified copies of a granted order must be requested within 28 days after the order is granted (URCrP 42).

If eligible, BCI issues the certificate on payment of the issuance fee. File the court packet within 180 days of issuance.

Check your answer to "If BCI has already issued your certificate of eligibility, what date did it issue? It is valid for 180 days and must still be valid on the day you file." against Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a current balance on the case, and check with the Office of State Debt Collection if any balance was entered as a civil judgment and transferred. An unpaid balance defeats the petition and will also defeat the BCI certificate.

Check your answer to "Have all fines, fees, interest and restitution on this case been paid in full?" against Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "List every criminal case you have ever had, in any state, including cases that were already expunged. BCI reviews all of them when it decides your certificate." against The participant's own case history for every case in every state, including previously expunged cases, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The special certificate issued by BCI. BCI offers the special certificate per criminal episode after its research fails to establish disposition or eligibility. Pay the issuance fee, unless a fee waiver was requested, and attach the certificate to the petition.

Check your answer to "Did BCI offer you a special certificate rather than an ordinary certificate of eligibility?" against The special certificate issued by BCI, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Whatever records the participant can obtain about the incomplete episode. Ask each court clerk and arresting agency for whatever remains of the file. LegalEase does not receive, inspect or authenticate any of these records and does not judge whether they are sufficient.

Check your answer to "What does the record not show — a missing disposition, an old case with no file, or something else BCI could not confirm?" against Whatever records the participant can obtain about the incomplete episode, and correct the packet if they disagree.
The judge's signature line, the findings the court makes, and the date on the proposed order — Proposed order 1021EX, signature and findings block.
The prosecuting attorney's signature on the Consent and Waiver of Hearing — Consent and Waiver of Hearing (1148XX), prosecutor signature block.
The petitioner's signature and date on the petition — Petition, signature block.

The petitioner signs the petition. The proposed order is completed by the petitioner except for the judge's signature line, which is left blank. The Consent and Waiver of Hearing is presented by the petitioner and signed by the prosecuting attorney; LegalEase neither obtains that consent nor signs on anyone's behalf.
Not required by Chapter 40a or by the published Utah Courts expungement packet for the petition itself.

A court filing fee set by Utah Code 78A-2-301 applies. The Utah Courts page directs filers to the cover sheet for the current amount rather than publishing a figure, so the packet does not quote one. The exact current amount is an open release-blocking question.

The court fee waiver process applies to the filing fee, and the published packet includes the fee waiver route. BCI separately operates an indigency-linked waiver and will issue without the issuance fee where the court is likely to waive the filing fee; if the court then finds the petitioner not indigent, the BCI issuance fee must be paid before BCI will process the expungement order.

The Norfolk clerk's guidance is that the case is established with the court first and the State Police request comes second, so the sequence matters.
Check your answer to "How did the case end, and on what date?" against The participant's own Virginia criminal history record from the CCRE, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The circuit court case file, or the district court record held by that locality's circuit court. Ask the clerk of the circuit court of the locality where the case was disposed of for the case papers. District court charges are handled by that locality's circuit court, so that is where to ask even for a general district court charge.

Check your answer to "How did the case end, and on what date?" against The circuit court case file, or the district court record held by that locality's circuit court, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "Have you been convicted of anything since, anywhere? Virginia traffic infractions under Title 46.2 do not count." against FBI Identity History Summary, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that court-ordered restitution is paid in full. Ask the clerk or the collecting agency for a payoff or zero-balance statement. Section 19.2-392.12(F)(4) makes full payment a criterion, so an outstanding balance defeats the petition.

Check your answer to "Was court-ordered restitution ordered on any charge, conviction or ancillary matter you want sealed, and is it paid in full?" against Proof that court-ordered restitution is paid in full, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Signature — CC-1201 series petition, signature block.
Case number — CC-1201 series petition, caption.
The manifest injustice statement — CC-1201 series petition, the grounds paragraph.
Any rehabilitation showing where alcohol or drugs were involved — CC-1201 series petition, the rehabilitation paragraph.
Any assertion that the offence is not on the subsection L exclusion list — CC-1201 series petition, the eligibility recital.
Any assertion about the felony-history bars — CC-1201 series petition, the eligibility recital.
The petitioner signs the petition.
none stated in § 19.2-392.12 or § 19.2-392.12:1 for the petition.

none. Sections 19.2-392.12(B) and 19.2-392.12:1(C) provide that no court fees or costs are charged for a sealing petition, and the 2025 acts repealed the Sealing Fee Fund. The CCRE charges its own fee for the participant's own copy of their criminal history record, which is a separate cost.
none — no court fee is charged, so there is nothing to waive.

manualCompletionItems.item: The State's Attorney's or Attorney General's signature on the stipulation, and the entire order page
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Stipulation form, prosecutor signature block and the ORDER page
manualCompletionItems.why: The stipulation is a request, not an entitlement. The prosecutor signs it or does not, and the order page belongs to the judge. LegalEase never completes either, and the packet must not describe a stipulation as though the signature were a formality.

manualCompletionItems.item: The assertion that the underlying conduct is no longer prohibited by law, including the drug-amount showing
manualCompletionItems.why: The Judiciary's filing guide frames this as something the petitioner must prove. The review is explicit that the engine must capture the exact statute of conviction, the amount and the offence date, and must not conclude decriminalisation on its own.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and date
manualCompletionItems.why: The petition is a participant filing and must be signed by the petitioner.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Vermont Judiciary criminal record search result for each county. participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The Criminal Division of the Superior Court in each county where the participant had a case

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What is the docket number? A separate petition is needed for each unrelated offence and for each county." against Vermont Judiciary criminal record search result for each county, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Vermont Crime Information Center criminal conviction record. Request the statewide conviction record from VCIC online, by mail, by email or in person. participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Vermont Crime Information Center

No filing fee. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e) the $90 fee applies only to a motion to seal a criminal history record of a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a), and expressly does not apply to any other motion to seal or expunge under 13 V.S.A. § 7602, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) or other records-clearance provisions.

Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228 (revision 04/2026), the Vermont Judiciary's single statewide fee-waiver application. Use it only if you are asking the court to waive the filing fee; if you are paying the fee, you do not need it. It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve the prosecutor with process. Where a stipulation is used, the Judiciary directs the participant to take or send the stipulation form to the prosecutor and to ask whether the prosecutor will file it or return it signed for the participant to file. Under § 7602(a)(4) the respondent files the stipulation.

Filed with the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court in the county that handled the case. Offences arising from the same incident or occurrence may go on one petition. It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page.

generationRequirements.question: Which county handled the case?

packetInstructions: Automatic record relief is not a dismissal, sealing or expungement. The record stays on the state summary criminal history and a notation is added, which controls whether the record is disseminated to employers and agencies conducting fingerprint background checks under PC 11105(k) through (p).
The absence of a notation does not mean ineligibility. The DOJ evaluates millions of records monthly back to 1973 and says no additional action is needed to receive relief.

Commercial background check companies do not access DOJ records at all and may hold stale data. Law enforcement, the Commission on Teacher Credentialing, school districts and their contractors continue to see conviction history.

packetInstructions: The offense class and the maximum sentence that could have been imposed are determined based on the law in effect at the time the offense was committed, not current law. § 54-142a(e)(1)(B).

If a case has more than one count and any count is not erasable, nothing on that record is erased. The same rule appears at § 54-142a(i)(1), § 54-142u(b) and § 54-142v(b). This is the most common practical defeat in Connecticut.

DUI is not excluded from Clean Slate. § 14-227a is carved out of the seven-year misdemeanor bucket and placed in the ten-year bucket. The only DUI bar is a second § 14-227a conviction within the ten years following.
Firearms offenses are not a category exclusion. § 54-142a(e)(2)(C) is an enumerated list of statute sections and must be screened section by section, not by category label.

Erasure does not terminate the obligation to pay an unremitted fine imposed as part of the sentence, and it does not end sex offender, deadly weapon offender or felony-for-a-sexual-purpose registration obligations, or a standing criminal protective order. Nothing in the erasure provisions requires the DMV to erase criminal history information on a driving record, which matters to any CDL holder.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Confidentiality by operation of law — classification and verification, no filing
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The base branch. Where the disposition falls inside the 16 M.R.S. § 703(2) list the record is already confidential criminal history record information and there is nothing to file: no court has any role, no motion exists, and generating CR-218 for a non-conviction would be affirmatively wrong because § 2262 reaches a specific criminal conviction only. The unit classifies the disposition against the § 703(2) list, explains that the confidentiality is automatic, walks the participant through obtaining their own State Bureau of Identification record to see what the State actually holds, and states plainly where the disposition falls outside the list that Maine offers no relief for it rather than routing them to a motion that will be denied. It also separates the three problems that participants conflate: the Bureau record, the court docket, and a private vendor's database.
