processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Court-ordered and automatic Article XIV relief — verification, no participant filing
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The first branch, and it is a legally distinct mechanism rather than a preliminary check. Article XIV, section 2 directs the courts themselves to order expungement for people who have completed their sentences, on constitutional deadlines the courts were given, and automatically vacates the sentence and terminates supervision for a person on probation or parole without any petition at all. For both of those populations there is no participant filing, no application, no request and no form: the constitution puts the act on the court. CR375 confirms the design from the other direction — its two selectable postures are currently incarcerated and not currently incarcerated or on probation, so a participant presently on probation or parole for a marijuana offense fits neither box, because the constitution does not ask them to petition. The unit's output is therefore verification and explanation: identify the marijuana case and the sentencing county, check Case.net and the Highway Patrol record to see whether expungement was already ordered, and, where it was, help the participant ask the court for the certificate of expungement the constitution requires it to issue. Where relief was not entered the participant is routed to the second unit. What the unit must not do is promise that relief occurred: the constitution directed the courts to process these cases, and a direction is not a receipt.

destination.name: Clerk of the Missouri court where the charge was last pending
destination.detail: Unit 2 is filed with the clerk of the court where the charge was last pending, and the clerk gives notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney, which is the whole of CR301's printed instruction to the clerk. § 610.145.3 makes the clerk responsible for notifying state and local agencies of the court's order. Unit 1 has no filing destination: the prosecutor or judicial officer notifies the court and the court orders expungement of its own motion.

rules.filing: Unit 2 is a petition or written motion filed in the court where the charge was last pending, on a form approved by the office of state courts administrator and supplied by the clerk (§ 610.145.1(1)). That statutory requirement is why the strategy is official_pdf_fill and not a custom pleading: the form is prescribed, not merely available. Unit 1 involves no filing at all. Whether the petition opens a new case or proceeds under the original number is local practice confirmed with the clerk.
rules.fees: The costs of expunging the records, as provided in chapter 610, shall not be taxed against the person eligible for expungement under this section (§ 610.145.3). Any reinstatement fee for a licence or privilege is waived (§ 610.145.5). Whether a court nonetheless collects an opening filing fee where the petition commences a new case is not addressed by the section and is confirmed with the clerk. No fee figure is published on this track.
rules.feeWaiver: Ordinarily unnecessary, because § 610.145.3 provides that costs are not taxed against the eligible person. GN10 under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040 is available where a court nevertheless requires an opening fee the participant cannot pay.
rules.notice: The court provides notice to the prosecuting attorney and shall hold a hearing on the motion or petition (§ 610.145.1(1)). CR301's printed instruction to the clerk is that the clerk gives notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney. § 610.145.3 makes the clerk responsible for notifying state and local agencies of the court's order.
rules.service: None performed by the participant. CR301 carries no certificate of service.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner swears or affirms under penalty of perjury that the facts are true according to their best knowledge and belief, and signs. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.notarization: none prescribed by § 610.145 or by CR301, which uses a sworn or affirmed statement rather than a notarial acknowledgment.

generationRequirements.question: How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything.

Which happened? Did somebody else use your name, date of birth, Social Security number or other identifying information? Or was it a mistake — a witness or an officer misidentified you, was confused about who committed the offense, or was given wrong information about who it was?
In your own words, what happened? How did your name come to be on this case, and how did you find out?
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR301 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? CR301 asks for it on the face of the petition.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest or apprehension?
What offense were you named in?
What was the date of the arrest or apprehension?
Which court was the charge last pending in, and in which county? If the case moved courts, it is the last one that matters.
What was the case number, and was it in the circuit, associate or municipal division?
Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports the charge was dismissed rather than tried.

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records naming you on this case? § 610.145 lets you identify them and the order reaches every one you name — law enforcement agencies, the Department of Corrections, the Department of Revenue and any other state or local government agency.

Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost.

Did your insurance premium go up because of insurance points from this matter? If so, the insurer has to refund the extra premium for the three years before the expungement once you notify and verify it.

What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it.

packetInstructions: Automatic relief runs first. Where the charge was dismissed on identity grounds the packet checks whether the § 610.145.1(2) order was already entered before offering a petition, because a participant who files for relief the court was already obliged to enter pays for nothing.

The costs of expunging the records are not taxed against the person eligible for expungement (§ 610.145.3), and any licence or privilege reinstatement fee is waived (§ 610.145.5). The packet tells the participant so, and tells them to raise it with the clerk if a fee is demanded.

The ancillary relief in §§ 610.145.4 to 6 is set out in full, because it is unusually broad and participants do not know to ask for it: Department of Revenue expungement, reversal of administrative actions including licence points, suspensions and revocations, a certified corrected driver history at no cost, licence reinstatement at no cost, Department of Corrections and other-agency expungement and reversal, and an insurer's obligation to refund three years of additional premium charged on insurance points from the matter.
Venue is the court where the charge was last pending, which on a case that moved is not the court it started in. The packet says so and directs the participant to the docket.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Automatic expungement on prosecutor or judicial-officer notice — no participant filing
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The first branch, and the statute itself calls it automatic. Under § 610.145.1(2), where the participant was named in a charge because another person used their identifying information or because of mistaken identity and that charge is dismissed, the prosecutor or other judicial officer who ordered the dismissal shall notify the court and the court shall order the expungement. There is no petition, no motion, no application and no form: the duty is on the prosecutor or the judicial officer, and § 610.145.3 confirms it by describing the beneficiary as the person eligible for automatic expungement under subdivision (2) of subsection 1. That has a direct product consequence, which is why this is a unit rather than a footnote: generating CR301 for a participant whose charge was dismissed on exactly this ground asks a court for relief the law has already told it to enter, and may cost them a filing fee for nothing. The unit's output is verification and explanation — check Case.net and the Highway Patrol record, ask the clerk whether an expungement order was entered on the dismissal, and understand that the participant may still identify agencies for the order to reach, because § 610.145.3 extends that right to the automatic beneficiary as well as to a petitioner. Where the order was not entered, the participant moves to the second unit.

destination.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol central repository, with the Office of the State Courts Administrator
destination.detail: The central repository screens the statewide criminal history database on a rolling basis not less than once per week, expunges eligible offenses, reflects the change through the Missouri uniform law enforcement system, and notifies both the Supreme Court of Missouri and the Office of the State Courts Administrator; the Office of the State Courts Administrator then expunges the corresponding case records in the statewide court automation system. The participant submits nothing to either body. Where an eligible offense is not expunged, § 610.141.8 makes the filing of a § 610.140 petition the sole remedy, which is the mo-610-140-conviction track.

rules.filing: none. § 610.141 creates no petition, application, request or submission of any kind for the participant. The central repository screens and expunges of its own motion and the Office of the State Courts Administrator expunges the corresponding case records on the repository's designations. Where an eligible offense is not expunged, § 610.141.8 makes the filing of a § 610.140 petition the sole remedy.
rules.fees: none. The mechanism costs the participant nothing because nothing is filed. § 610.144 creates the Missouri Expungement Fund to pay for the technology from appropriations, gifts, donations, grants and bequests. The participant pays only for any record they choose to obtain to check the outcome.

rules.notice: none to the participant. generationRequirements.question: Is the conviction for possessing a controlled substance, or for drug paraphernalia? Missouri's automatic expungement law reaches only those four offenses — it does not reach trafficking, distribution, delivery or manufacture.
Was it a misdemeanor or a felony? And if a felony, was it a class A felony? A class A felony is excluded.
On what date did you finish everything the court ordered and were released from any custody or supervision? The law calls that final disposition, and the one-year or three-year clock runs from it.
Was this the only conviction in that case? If the same case included a conviction for something that is not one of the four covered offenses, the automatic law does not reach any of it.
Since that date, have you been convicted of any misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any outstanding arrest, warrant or pending criminal charge right now?

Have you had any Missouri expungement before, under any law? From the date the automatic law starts operating, automatic expungements and petition expungements share the same lifetime limits — three misdemeanors and two felonies between them.

Do you need this record cleared by a particular date — for a job, a licence, housing or an immigration matter? The automatic mechanism has no published start date beyond a 1 January 2027 outer limit and cannot be relied on for a deadline.

Knowing that a petition under § 610.140 is available now but costs a filing fee and uses one of your lifetime slots, and that automatic relief is free but not yet shown to be running and uses the same slot, would you like to talk through which makes sense for you?

packetInstructions: The scope is four offenses, not a category. § 610.141 reaches possession of a controlled substance under § 195.202 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, unlawful use of drug paraphernalia under § 195.233 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, possession or control of a controlled substance under § 579.015, and unlawful possession of drug paraphernalia under § 579.074. Trafficking, distribution, delivery and manufacture are outside it, and Missouri must never be described as a general clean-slate state.

Automatic expungement consumes a lifetime slot. § 610.141.6 limits an offender to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements under §§ 610.140 and 610.141 combined, counting only the highest-level offense where a case contains more than one. This closes the review's cap-coordination build blocker and belongs on the § 610.140 packet as well as this one.

The relief is closure of the record under § 610.120, which § 610.141.1(4) says in terms. It is the same legal effect as a § 610.140 order, not destruction, and the packet must not describe it as erasure.

The participant must be told the uncertainty and the alternative together. The section operates when technically feasible and no later than 1 January 2027, no implementation notice has been published, and a § 610.140 petition is available now. Telling a participant to wait for future relief without explaining both is not acceptable.

The sole remedy for a failure to expunge is a § 610.140 petition, which § 610.141.8 provides notwithstanding any other provision of law. There is no appeal to the Highway Patrol and no correction application, and the guidance routes a participant whose record was missed to the petition track rather than to an agency.

Secondary summaries of Missouri clean slate must not be used. The enacted § 610.141 is narrower than the press coverage and differs materially from SB 1494, the broader vehicle that did not become law but whose text is widely conflated with it — including a bulk-processing deadline that appears nowhere in the enacted section. Only the enrolled CCS SS SB 1421 text governs.

rules.filing: File the petition with the proposed order and certificate of service with the clerk of the justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the case was pending. Mississippi has no statewide form; the petition is drafted to the statute and the court, county and prosecuting authority are participant data. Call the clerk before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.
rules.fees: No amount is published here. Section 99-19-72 sets a fee for a petition to expunge an offence under § 99-19-71, and subsection (4) sits inside § 99-19-71, but charging a person whose case was dismissed is a contested result and county practice differs. The participant is instructed to confirm the filing fee with the clerk before filing. See the unresolved fee question.
rules.feeWaiver: A pauper's affidavit under general Mississippi practice. Not verified for expungement specifically; the participant asks the clerk.
rules.notice: The prosecuting authority receives a copy. The ten days' written notice to the district attorney is imposed by § 99-19-71(2)(b), which sits inside the felony conviction subsection, and it is NOT imported into this subsection without textual support; the packet nonetheless tells the participant that some districts expect notice and prosecutor approval as a matter of local practice. No response or objection period is stated for this track and no hearing is required by subsection (4).

rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank and does not use the archived models' 'by and through his attorney' recital.
rules.notarization: None on the archived models. Whether any district requires verification or notarization is unresolved; the petition carries a simple truth statement rather than a notarized verification.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?

How did the case end? Choose the one that matches: you were arrested and released and the case was dismissed; the charges were dropped; there was never any disposition; or you were found not guilty at trial.
On what date did that happen?
Was the case ever presented to a grand jury and indicted? Many cases are not, and the petition only pleads an indictment where one exists.
What exactly does your paperwork say about how the case ended? Copy the wording. Phrases like 'passed to the file' or 'retired to the file' need a closer look before we go further.
Was this a nonadjudication, a pretrial intervention programme, or an intervention or drug court? Those end differently and route differently.
Was anyone charged with you whose case is still open?

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The order directs every person and agency keeping official records to expunge them EXCEPT fingerprint records, and the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings. Participant-facing copy must not say the record is erased everywhere.

Section 99-19-71(3) expressly provides that the existence of an order of expunction does not preclude an employer from asking a prospective employee whether an order of expunction has been entered on their behalf. This is a real and unusual limitation and participants must be told about it. A person called as a prospective juror must also, on request, advise the court in camera of the previous conviction and expunction.

A participant who uses this track has not spent their one felony expungement. The one-felony-per-lifetime cap sits in § 99-19-71(2)(a) and applies to conviction expungement, not to subsection (4). That is an important thing to tell people and to encode.
Relief is mandatory. The statute says the court "shall expunge", which is one of very few mandatory record-clearing provisions in the country and should be the headline of the Mississippi product.
The disposition order is obtained by the participant from the clerk and attached as an exhibit. It never delays generation of the petition.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Intervention court — verification of the self-executing result, and routing
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The verification branch. Section 9-23-23 states a result rather than a procedure: on completion of all requirements the charge and prosecution 'shall be dismissed', and where the person was sentenced at the time of the guilty plea completion 'will result in the record of the criminal conviction or adjudication being expunged'. There is no petition language, no application, no fee, no hearing, no notice and no waiting period anywhere in the section — which is unique in the Mississippi scheme and is why no petition is generated on this branch. The section does not, however, direct any officer to enter or transmit an order, so whether an expungement order in fact issues without the participant asking is a matter of local practice and is preserved as an open question. The correct product output is therefore verification: establish from the clerk what was actually entered and when, obtain a certified copy of any dismissal or expungement order that already exists, and route onward only where the record shows relief did not issue. Implied consent violations are expressly barred from expunction here and route to the DUI track.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.
DOJ states that after July 1, 2017 CRISS will automatically remove all non-conviction arrest data per MCA 44-5-202 and no Record Removal Form is required. Do not generate a form for this route.

destination.detail: Two stages with two different answers. The vacatur, dismissal and expungement happen by operation of law under CPL § 160.50(5)(a): nothing is filed, nothing is generated and the participant does nothing, while under § 160.50(5)(b)(i) the chief administrator of the courts notifies the Division of Criminal Justice Services and the police, district attorney and other law enforcement agencies that hold the records. The destruction request is a participant submission to a court. The form directs "Submit your application to the Court where you were convicted", and the instructions page adds that an application sent to a different court cannot be processed and that a person with eligible convictions in more than one court must submit a separate application to each. The Office of Court Administration publishes the form; it does not receive it, and there is no statewide OCA address, mailbox or portal for this application. What happens after submission belongs to the court: it returns an Acknowledgement of Application to Destroy Expunged Marihuana Conviction Record and forwards the application to the prosecutor, the law enforcement agencies involved and, where the person was fingerprinted, DCJS, which then writes to confirm destruction. Those are the court's acts and none of them is the participant's to perform.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: The automatic vacatur, dismissal and expungement, and how to check it
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The default stage, and the one that runs first. Under CPL § 160.50(5)(a) a conviction for an offence described in § 160.50(3)(k) is vacated and dismissed and all records of it expunged, by operation of law. Nothing is filed, no motion is made, no fee is charged and the participant does nothing to obtain it: under § 160.50(5)(b)(i) the chief administrator of the courts notifies the Division of Criminal Justice Services and the heads of all appropriate police departments, district attorneys' offices and other law enforcement agencies, and those holders mark the record as expunged. No participant filing exists at this stage and none is generated. The guidance explains what expungement means, that the courts do not send a notice when it happens, how to check through a DCJS Record Review, why an absence in that report is consistent with expungement rather than proof of destruction, and the separate § 160.50(5)(b)(ii)(B) route where court records cannot be located or the expungement has not been reflected. Where the participant wants nothing beyond expungement, the route ends here.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The judgment stage. processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Notice to the Attorney General and charging police department, the hearing, and delivery of certified orders
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File with the clerk, who fills in the hearing date; the hearing must be at least ten days after filing because notice must reach the Attorney General and the charging police department. Sign the affidavit before a notary or clerk. Attend the hearing with the proposed order. On a grant the clerk prepares three certified copies after all conditions are satisfied, and the petitioner delivers one to the Attorney General's BCI unit and one to the charging police department — if that delivery does not happen, nothing changes on the record. Verify afterwards with a fresh BCI record.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Verify the automatic § 12-1.3-5 expungement
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The default stage, and the one that must run first. Section 12-1.3-5 entitles a person with a prior civil violation, misdemeanor conviction or felony conviction for possession only of a since-decriminalized marijuana offence to automatic expungement, and Rhode Island completed the initial statewide effort in June 2023 — more than 23,000 records, being 3,015 in Superior Court, 9,952 in the Traffic Tribunal and 10,650 in District Court — over a year ahead of the 1 July 2024 deadline. The participant pulls a BCI criminal history and checks whether the record has already cleared. Nothing is filed at this stage and no participant submission exists: the relief is automatic and, under § 12-1.3-5(f), the court rather than the participant distributes the order to the Attorney General, the arresting agency and any other agency known to hold records. Where the record has cleared, the route ends here and no motion is generated or sold.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The judgment stage, and the one that decides whether anything can be filed at all. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: The order the court owes automatically, and how to verify it issued
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The ordinary path, and the one that must be checked before anything is sold. The court determines eligibility when it grants discharge and dismissal and issues the order without any petition. LegalEase confirms the discharge and dismissal date is on or after 2017-09-01, confirms 180 days were served on deferred adjudication, screens the offence exclusions and the first-time-offender condition, and directs the participant to pull their DPS criminal history to see whether the record is already sealed. If it is sealed, there is nothing to buy and nothing to file. Automating a petition here would be the single most expensive error available in Texas, because it would sell a paid petition packet to someone entitled to a free automatic order.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: The expungement the court owes on discharge, and how to verify it happened
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The ordinary and intended path. Section 7041(e) makes expungement the court's duty on discharge from probation, absent a finding of good cause, and nothing is filed by the participant. LegalEase confirms that the person was discharged and the adjudication of guilt struck, confirms restitution is paid in full, and explains how to check whether the expungement order issued. Anyone who completed a deferred sentence should not be sold a petition packet, and this unit is why.

destination.name: Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court, in the county that handled the case
destination.detail: On the automatic route the court acts on its own within 60 days of final disposition and nothing is submitted. On the stipulated and petition routes the participant files in the same court, with the State's Attorney or Attorney General as respondent.

rules.filing: Filed with the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court in the county that handled the case. Offences arising from the same incident or occurrence may go on one petition. Offences not related to the same incident, or offences in more than one county, require a separate petition for each offence. That is a per-offence cost and packet multiplier, not a per-county one.
rules.fees: No filing fee. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e) the $90 fee applies only to a motion to seal a criminal history record of a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a), and expressly does not apply to any other motion to seal or expunge under 13 V.S.A. § 7602, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) or other records-clearance provisions.
rules.feeWaiver: Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228 (revision 04/2026), the Vermont Judiciary's single statewide fee-waiver application. Use it only if you are asking the court to waive the filing fee; if you are paying the fee, you do not need it. It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page.
rules.notice: The court notifies the prosecuting office. Under § 7608 the respondent, not the participant and not the court, must give notice of the petition to any victim of the offence known to the respondent, and the victim has the right to offer a statement to the respondent before any stipulation or to offer one to the court. The respondent's inability to locate a victim after reasonable effort — first-class mail, telephone and email to the last known contact details — is not a bar to granting the petition.
rules.service: The participant does not serve the prosecutor with process. Where a stipulation is used, the Judiciary directs the participant to take or send the stipulation form to the prosecutor and to ask whether the prosecutor will file it or return it signed for the participant to file. Under § 7602(a)(4) the respondent files the stipulation.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. On a stipulation form the petitioner signs and the State's Attorney signs separately; LegalEase neither obtains nor asserts the prosecutor's signature.
rules.notarization: Not required by chapter 230 or by the Judiciary's published petition forms.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Automatic court-initiated sealing within 60 days, and how to verify it happened
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The ordinary path and the one that must be checked before anything is sold. Under § 7603(a)(1) the court shall seal within 60 days of final disposition where there was no probable cause determination at arraignment, the charge was dismissed before trial with or without prejudice, or the defendant was acquitted, unless either party objects in the interests of justice. The participant files nothing: there is no petition, no form, no fee and no application step. LegalEase confirms the disposition is one of the three triggers, confirms 60 days have run, and explains how to check whether the record still appears.

packetInstructions: Conviction expungement under sections 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a is available once in a lifetime. That must be said before money changes hands, and it should drive bundling advice.
The circuit clerk civil filing fee applies, and a $100 State Police processing fee is due on grant, unless the petition is under section 61-11-26a.

Expunged convictions must still be disclosed for jobs involving the prevention, detection, investigation, prosecution, or incarceration of law violators, and legally required background checks may still reveal them.
The court has 60 days to act, agencies have 60 days to certify, and a victim or prosecutor may oppose within 30 days.

The complete section 61-11-26 exclusion list was read at source on 2026-08-06 and is recorded here verbatim in fifteen subdivisions, closing the review's build blocker for the exclusion screen. A DUI conviction does not automatically block expungement of an unrelated otherwise expungeable felony if the DUI conviction is at least five years old when the petition is filed.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction on the inventory. Ask the clerk of the county of disposition for a certified copy of the disposition, the judgment order and the sentencing order for each case. Most counties charge a per-copy fee. Ask for every case, not only the one you came in for, because the petition is once per lifetime.

Check your answer to "List every West Virginia conviction on your record, however old, including traffic citations — not just the one you came here about. What was each offence, in which county, and on what date were you convicted?" against Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction on the inventory, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof of supervision completion. Ask the probation office that supervised you for written confirmation of the date supervision ended, and the institution of confinement for the date of release. The waiting period runs from the later of conviction, release and end of supervision, so this date is usually the one that decides eligibility.

Check your answer to "For each conviction, on what date did you finish any jail or prison term and any probation, parole or other supervision?" against Proof of supervision completion, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Copy of any current restitution, protection, restraining or no-contact order. Ask the clerk of the court that entered the order for a copy. The statute requires a current order to be attached to the petition; a past order is disclosed but not attached.

generationRequirements.question: How old were you on the date of the offence?
What blood alcohol concentration was recorded, if you know it?
Was this your first charge of this kind — an under-21 alcohol driving offence?
Did you complete the Motor Vehicle Test and Lock Program, and on what date?
Which court was the charge in, and in which county?
Has the court told you the charge was dismissed, and have you seen the order?
Does the charge still appear on a court record search or a background check?

packetInstructions: Upon successful completion of the program, the court shall dismiss the charge against the person and expunge the person's record as it relates to the alleged offense. That is a mandatory expungement with no petition and no waiting period, sitting inside the DUI statute itself.
The DMV record is not expunged. The criminal record can be cleared; the driving record cannot.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the report and identify the arrest cycle for the fugitive warrant. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Any Georgia court record of the fugitive warrant proceeding
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the fugitive warrant matter was heard
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where a Georgia court record of the matter exists.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket or disposition of the fugitive warrant proceeding.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that the offence is already restricted — your Georgia criminal history report showing the cycle as restricted, or the court order restricting the record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC; or the clerk of the court that entered the order
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain your own criminal history report showing the cycle as restricted, or a copy of the restricting order from the clerk, and enclose it with the request. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: To confirm afterwards that the restriction was entered.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the report after sentencing and confirm the first offender cycle is restricted. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Final disposition showing the First Offender sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that sentenced you
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for the final disposition showing that you were sentenced under the First Offender Act, and attach it to the petition as Exhibit A. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Final disposition showing the First Offender sentence, and the discharge order where one was entered
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that sentenced you and granted the discharge
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the final disposition showing that you were sentenced under the First Offender Act, and for the discharge order if one was entered, and attach them to the petition as Exhibit A. A discharge frequently was never entered; where that is so, the petition says you were discharged as a matter of law. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates these records.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The sentencing record and plea paperwork from the original case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting court for the sentencing record, the plea transcript or plea paperwork, and the final disposition. These are what an attorney or legal-aid desk will need to assess the eligibility claim and approach the prosecuting attorney.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Photo identification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own documents
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Include a copy of your photo identification with the application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Money order for the application fee
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A post office, bank or store that issues money orders
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a money order for the HCJDC fee and enclose it with the application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Stamped self-addressed envelope
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A post office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope so HCJDC can return the result.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition showing discharge and dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the discharge and dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Photo identification, money order, and stamped self-addressed envelope
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own documents, a money order issuer, and a post office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Enclose a copy of your photo identification, a money order for the fee, and a stamped self-addressed envelope.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition showing discharge and dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the discharge and dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order granting expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court, at stage 1
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application. LegalEase does not review the court order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Photo identification, money order, and stamped self-addressed envelope
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own documents, a money order issuer, and a post office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Enclose these with the HCJDC application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order granting expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court, at stage 1
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application. LegalEase does not review the court order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order granting expungement

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Confirmation from the clerk that all financial obligations in this case are paid
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the Iowa District Court for the county of the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the balance in this case number. Rule 2.83(3) counts only obligations in the case or cases where expungement is sought, and room and board fees sought under a separate civil action under § 356.7 are not counted.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Official DCI Iowa criminal history record check, dated within the past 30 days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Iowa Department of Public Safety, Division of Criminal Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Submit form DCI-77 with a release authorization signature through the state portal. The Iowa Judicial Branch instructions state a request costs $15. The check must be dated within 30 days of filing, so obtain it and then file promptly.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Confirmation from the clerk that all financial obligations in this case are paid
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the Iowa District Court for the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the balance in this case number. Rule 2.83(3) counts only obligations in the case where expungement is sought.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Confirmation from the clerk of the balance in the case containing the deferred judgment
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the Iowa District Court for the county of the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the balance in that case number. An unpaid balance is the usual reason an expected automatic expungement did not happen.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Official DCI Iowa criminal history record check on form DCI-77, dated within the past 30 days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Iowa Department of Public Safety, Division of Criminal Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Submit form DCI-77 with a release authorization signature through the state portal. The Iowa Judicial Branch instructions state a request costs $15. Obtain it and then file the § 901C.3 application promptly, because it expires after 30 days.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified court order of acquittal stating not guilty of the charged crimes, or certified court order of dismissal showing which crimes were dismissed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that heard the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that heard the case for a certified copy of the order of acquittal or dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: One charging document: criminal citation, or criminal complaint and summons showing service by the sheriff's office, or an indictment, or an information
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that heard the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a copy from the court that heard the case.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Idaho State Police, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Not required as an attachment, but needed to build the petition accurately.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a criminal history report from the Idaho State Police Bureau of Criminal Identification.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case information from the iCourt Portal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: iCourt Portal at mycourts.idaho.gov, or the court where the case was filed
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant does not already know the case number, charges, statute sections, level, supervision end date, or completion date.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look the case up on the iCourt Portal at mycourts.idaho.gov, or ask the court where the case was filed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Illinois State Police statewide criminal history transcript
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Illinois State Police, Bureau of Identification, through the Access and Review process
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Attend an Illinois law enforcement or correctional facility or a licensed fingerprint vendor, submit fingerprints and identifying information, and receive the transcript. Access and Review is free on the ISP fee schedule.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Chicago Police Department RAP sheet
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Chicago Police Department
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where there were Chicago arrests; the statewide transcript does not always capture them.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the RAP sheet from the Chicago Police Department. A local fee applies.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition for each case

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: School, college or awarding body
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a copy of your high school diploma, GED, college diploma or transcripts.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Employers or tax records
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Provide W-2s, tax returns, paycheck stubs or a letter from your employers covering the last five years.

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant served in the military, and required for the military certificate branch.
