participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where restitution was ordered in the case.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for a payment history showing restitution paid in full.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certificate of pardon
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pardon Clerk, North Dakota Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a copy from the pardon clerk at pardonclerk@nd.gov. The certificate is the proof of eligibility on this ground, and whether the pardon is unconditional is read off its face.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Criminal judgment or disposition order in the DUI case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for the judgment. It establishes the conviction type and the violation date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The text of the municipal ordinance
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The municipality, through its website or its clerk
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant was charged under a city ordinance rather than the state statute.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the city for the text of the ordinance you were charged under. The petition has to show it is equivalent to N.D.C.C. § 39-08-01.

participantFilingRequirements.name: North Dakota BCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: North Dakota Attorney General, Bureau of Criminal Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history from the BCI. It evidences the clean period, which covers any criminal offence and not only impaired driving.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Criminal judgment
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for the judgment. It establishes the date judgment of guilt was entered.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Charging document showing the quantity
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the complaint or information. The quantity charged is an element of eligibility and recollection is not enough.

participantFilingRequirements.name: North Dakota BCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: North Dakota Attorney General, Bureau of Criminal Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant is unsure whether any further controlled-substance conviction exists.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history from the BCI.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Final order withdrawing the plea, setting aside the verdict and dismissing the case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for the final order. Until you have it, nothing can be said about whether the automatic term operated.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order deferring imposition of sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the deferral order. Its date decides which version of Rule 32.1 applies.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Probation discharge or final discharge from supervision
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court, or Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation Parole and Probation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or your probation officer for the discharge record. It fixes the date the sixty-one days run from.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Dismissal or acquittal order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court, or search the case at ndcourts.gov public access.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Official victim determination or documentation
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A federal, state, local or tribal agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has one. It is not required.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: If a government agency has made a determination about your victim status, ask for a copy. It is not required, but it creates a presumption in your favour.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Criminal judgment for each offence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of district court in the sentencing jurisdiction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Contact the clerk of district court where you were sentenced. These documents are not available to the public on the internet. The application is returned if they are missing.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Criminal information, complaint or citation for each offence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of district court in the sentencing jurisdiction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the same clerk. If you cannot obtain them, the form permits a written explanation of the attempts you made.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Photocopy of a driver's licence or state identification card
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own records
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Photocopy your licence or state identification card and attach it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Criminal judgment for each offence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of district court in the sentencing jurisdiction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Contact the clerk of district court where you were sentenced. An incomplete application is returned.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Photocopy of a driver's licence or state identification card
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own records
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Photocopy your licence or state identification card and attach it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Juvenile court file or final order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The juvenile court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant needs the case type or the closing date confirmed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the juvenile court that handled the case. Juvenile records are confidential and the court will tell you what it needs to release your own.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the sealing order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of district court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: After an order issues. It is what the laboratory acts on.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Once the court seals the record, ask the clerk for a certified copy and deliver it to the State Crime Laboratory.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Dismissal order or the decision overturning the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for the order. It establishes the disposition the route depends on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska State Patrol criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a limited criminal history search through nebraska.gov. A small fee applies. The judiciary recommends using more than one record source because no single one is complete.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska court case search result
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska Judicial Branch online case search
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Run a one-time case search on the Nebraska courts site. A small fee applies and it is incomplete on its own, which is why the judiciary recommends more than one source.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Probation discharge order or notice of set-aside eligibility
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court or the probation office
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where probation was imposed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or your probation officer. Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2263 requires the sentencing court and the probation officer to give notice of set-aside eligibility, so you may already have one.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska State Patrol criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a limited criminal history search through nebraska.gov. A small fee applies. The judiciary recommends using more than one record source because no single one is complete.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska court case search result
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska Judicial Branch online case search
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Run a one-time case search on the Nebraska courts site. A small fee applies and it is incomplete on its own, which is why the judiciary recommends more than one source.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Probation discharge order or notice of set-aside eligibility
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court or the probation office
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where probation was imposed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or your probation officer. Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2263 requires the sentencing court and the probation officer to give notice of set-aside eligibility, so you may already have one.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska State Patrol criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a limited criminal history search through nebraska.gov. This is how you check whether the record actually came off.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska court case search result
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska Judicial Branch online case search
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Run a case search on the Nebraska courts site to see whether the case is still publicly visible.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska State Patrol criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a limited criminal history search through nebraska.gov.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska court case search result
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska Judicial Branch online case search
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Run a case search on the Nebraska courts site to confirm the case number and the disposition date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court holding the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Useful where the dismissal reason is not clear from the online record.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the disposition. It is source data for the motion, not a filing requirement.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The pardon document
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska Board of Pardons
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Use your copy of the pardon, or ask the Board of Pardons for one. Bring it to the hearing. LegalEase never sees or checks it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska State Patrol criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a limited criminal history search through nebraska.gov.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska State Patrol criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a limited criminal history search through nebraska.gov to show the arrest still appears.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Agency records showing the error
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The arresting agency, or the participant's own papers
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant holds correction notices, agency correspondence or identification records.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Gather anything the agency sent you about the mistake. LegalEase names these; it does not collect, inspect or judge them.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska State Patrol criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a limited criminal history search through nebraska.gov. This is the evidence that the record is still public.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court case search result or courthouse terminal printout
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska Judicial Branch online case search, or the courthouse
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Run a case search or print from a courthouse public-access terminal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The order setting aside the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that granted the set-aside
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required before the sealing motion can be filed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the signed order. The sealing motion cannot be filed without the set-aside having been granted.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Nebraska State Patrol criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Nebraska State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a limited criminal history search through nebraska.gov.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Hampshire criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Hampshire State Police Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant wants to verify that the automatic annulment took effect.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete the Criminal Record Release Authorization, NHJB-2956, and send it to the State Police Criminal Records Unit with their fee. Nothing is filed with a court, so this is verification rather than an attachment.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court record showing the disposition and its date
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Circuit Court District Division or Superior Court that disposed of the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the disposing court for the docket or disposition record. The disposition date decides whether the relief is automatic and free or needs a paid petition, so it is checked against the record.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The order vacating the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that vacated the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that vacated the conviction for a copy of the order. Nothing is filed, but the order is what shows the annulment is owed, and its wording decides whether the case is within the subparagraph at all.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Hampshire criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Hampshire State Police Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant wants to verify that the annulment took effect.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete the Criminal Record Release Authorization, NHJB-2956, and send it to the State Police Criminal Records Unit with their fee.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court record showing the disposition and its date
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that disposed of the charge
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the disposing court for the docket or disposition record. The disposition date decides whether a petition is needed at all, so it is checked against the record rather than recollection.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Hampshire criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Hampshire State Police Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has more than one New Hampshire case and needs the complete list.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete the Criminal Record Release Authorization, NHJB-2956, and send it to the State Police Criminal Records Unit with their fee.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The order vacating the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that vacated the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that vacated the conviction for a copy of the order. Its wording decides whether the case is a vacatur at all, and the participant must already hold it before this track begins.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Hampshire criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Hampshire State Police Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete the Criminal Record Release Authorization, NHJB-2956, and send it to the State Police Criminal Records Unit with their fee. It is not a statutory attachment, because the Department of Corrections performs the court-ordered investigation, but it is the only practical way to build the complete record list that RSA 651:5, VI makes decisive.
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has other New Hampshire cases.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court records and dispositions for every New Hampshire case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Each Circuit Court District Division or Superior Court that disposed of a charge
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of each disposing court for the docket and disposition. You need the offence level and the disposition date for every entry, not just the one you are trying to clear.
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has other New Hampshire cases.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Hampshire criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Hampshire State Police Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete the Criminal Record Release Authorization, NHJB-2956, and send it to the State Police Criminal Records Unit with their fee. It is not a statutory attachment, because the Department of Corrections performs the court-ordered investigation, but RSA 651:5, VI makes eligibility a whole-record question and this is the only practical way to build the complete list.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court records and dispositions for every New Hampshire case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Each court that disposed of a charge
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of each disposing court for the docket and disposition. You need the offence level and the dates for every entry on the record, not only the one you are trying to clear.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that all terms and conditions of the sentence were completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court, probation or parole, and whoever collected fines, fees and restitution
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Gather the discharge from probation or parole, the release from incarceration, and receipts or zero-balance statements for fines, fees and restitution. Nothing is required as a statutory attachment, but sentence completion is where a prosecutor objection will land, so having the proof ready turns a possible objection into a short answer.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Hampshire criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Hampshire State Police Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete the Criminal Record Release Authorization, NHJB-2956, and send it to the State Police Criminal Records Unit with their fee. It is not a statutory attachment, because the Department of Corrections performs the court-ordered investigation, but RSA 651:5, VI makes eligibility a whole-record question and this is the only practical way to build the complete list.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court records and dispositions for every New Hampshire case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Each court that disposed of a charge
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of each disposing court for the docket and disposition. You need the offence level and the dates for every entry on the record, not only the one you are trying to clear.

Nothing is required as a statutory attachment, but sentence completion is where a prosecutor objection will land, so having the proof ready turns a possible objection into a short answer.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court or arrest record for the marijuana case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court of conviction, or the arresting agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant cannot supply the offence date or case number from memory.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case, or the arresting agency, for the docket or arrest record. You need the offence date, because the September 16, 2017 cutoff decides eligibility.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Jersey State Police State Bureau of Identification criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Jersey State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the fingerprint-based SBI criminal history and pay the State Police fee. It is not a statutory attachment, but it produces the offence count that decides the route, the case identifiers the petition needs, and the agency list the signed order must later be served on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court records and dispositions for any matter the SBI record does not show
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Superior Court or Municipal Court that handled the matter
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the SBI history is incomplete or a disposition is missing.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the matter for the disposition and the complaint, indictment or docket number.

participantFilingRequirements.name: FBI Identity History Summary
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Federal Bureau of Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where out-of-state or federal records may exist.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request an Identity History Summary from the FBI. Those records cannot be expunged in New Jersey, but they count toward eligibility and toward the offence counts, so the analysis is wrong without them.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Jersey State Police State Bureau of Identification criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Jersey State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the fingerprint-based SBI criminal history and pay the State Police fee. It is not a statutory attachment, but it produces the offence count that decides the route, the case identifiers the petition needs, and the agency list the signed order must later be served on.

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where out-of-state or federal records may exist.

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the SBI history is incomplete or a disposition is missing.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the fingerprint-based SBI criminal history and pay the State Police fee. It produces the offence count that decides the route, the case identifiers the petition needs, and the agency list the signed order must later be served on.

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the SBI history is incomplete or a disposition is missing.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the matter for the disposition and the complaint, indictment or docket number.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Superior Court or Municipal Court that handled the matter
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the SBI history is incomplete or a disposition is missing.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the matter for the disposition and the complaint, indictment or docket number.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that the record was created by identity theft
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own records, the police report of the identity theft, or the agency that resolved it
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Gather whatever shows the record is not yours: a police report of the identity theft, correspondence from the arresting agency or prosecutor, or a court document correcting the identification. New Mexico does not publish a list of what proof the court accepts, so bring everything you have.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Records showing the misidentified arrest or case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district court, metropolitan, magistrate or municipal court where the case was heard, and the arresting agency
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Use the New Mexico Courts "Find a Case" search to locate the case, then ask the clerk of the court that heard it for the docket sheet or arrest sheet. Court copies run about $0.35 per page.

participantFilingRequirements.name: New Mexico Department of Public Safety Record of Arrest and Prosecution (RAP) sheet
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Mexico Department of Public Safety
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete the DPS Authorization for Release of Information, have it notarized with an original signature, and send it to DPS with a $15.00 money order or cashier's check per record check. DPS must receive the form bearing the original signature. The sheet must be dated no earlier than ninety days before the petition is filed, so order it once the rest of the packet is nearly ready.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket sheet, arrest sheet or other record detailing the offenses
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district, metropolitan, magistrate or municipal court that handled the case, and the arresting agency
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Use the New Mexico Courts "Find a Case" search to locate the case, then ask the clerk of the court that heard it for the docket sheet or arrest sheet. Court copies run about $0.35 per page.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Record of the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the document showing how the case ended and the date it ended, so you can check your own answer about the disposition and the one-year date against the record.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that a preprosecution diversion or conditional discharge was completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's diversion programme or the court that ordered the conditional discharge
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the case ended in a referral to a preprosecution diversion program or an order of conditional discharge under Section 31-20-13.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the district attorney's office that ran the diversion programme, or the court that entered the conditional discharge, for a document confirming the case was discharged and when.

participantFilingRequirements.name: FBI Identity History Summary
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Federal Bureau of Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request an Identity History Summary from the FBI and pay the FBI's fee. participantFilingRequirements.name: New Mexico Department of Public Safety Record of Arrest and Prosecution (RAP) sheet
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: New Mexico Department of Public Safety
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete the DPS Authorization for Release of Information, have it notarized with an original signature, and send it to DPS with a $15.00 money order or cashier's check per record check. It must be dated no later than ninety days before filing.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Judgment and sentence, and proof that the sentence was completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that entered the conviction, and probation or parole
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered the conviction for the judgment and sentence, and ask probation or parole for a discharge document. Form 4-953 paragraph 17(a) asks for documentation showing completion of the sentences for the convictions you are seeking to expunge.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that sentences for any other convictions were completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Each court, probation or parole authority that handled those convictions, in any jurisdiction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has served any other sentence, including in another state.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Form 4-953 paragraph 17(b) asks for documentation showing completion of sentences for any other convictions served. Because the waiting period runs from the most recent sentence completed in any jurisdiction, gather this for out-of-state convictions too.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of final payment of fines and fees
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court or agency that collected them
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or the collections office for a receipt or a zero-balance statement for the conviction you want cleared. Form 4-953 paragraph 17(c) asks for it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that victim restitution was completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court or the agency that administered restitution
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where restitution was ordered in connection with the conviction.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the court or the restitution administrator for a document showing restitution was paid in full. Form 4-953 paragraph 17(d) asks for it and Section 29-3A-5(C)(3) makes it a finding the court must make.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket sheet or other record detailing the offenses
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Use the New Mexico Courts "Find a Case" search to locate the case, then ask the clerk for the docket sheet. Court copies run about $0.35 per page.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Picture identification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own documents
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The AOC's Application for Expungement of Court Records involving Cannabis asks the applicant to supply a picture ID with the request. LegalEase never collects, inspects or holds it; the participant supplies it directly to the AOC.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case documentation for the cannabis charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has it or can get it. The AOC application treats case documentation as optional.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Use the New Mexico Courts "Find a Case" search to locate the case, then ask the clerk for the docket sheet. If the record has already been expunged and destroyed you may not find it, which is itself the answer you were looking for.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Judgment and sentence for the cannabis conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that entered the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant is pursuing the referral and the lawyer or public defender asks for it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered the conviction for the judgment and sentence. Nothing generated by LegalEase depends on it; it is named because whoever takes the referral will want it.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting court for the judgment, and parole or probation for the discharge document. The discharge date is what the waiting period runs from, so it is checked against the record rather than recollection.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Named wherever the participant's criminal history or court paperwork does not already show the disposition and its finality on its face. NRS 179A.160 does not require any attachment, so this is never a gate on generation.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report from the Pennsylvania State Police. Rule 490 requires a current copy obtained within 60 days before filing to be attached. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Magisterial district court docket sheet
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The magisterial district court, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet showing every charge and its disposition, and confirm no misdemeanour or felony was filed with the summary offences.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket sheet showing the verdict on every count
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of courts, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet and confirm a not-guilty verdict on every count arising from the incident. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Used to verify whether the record actually cleared once twelve months have passed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report to check whether the acquitted cycle still appears.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report from the Pennsylvania State Police within 60 days before filing and attach it to the petition. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket sheet showing the ARD dismissal and any expungement order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of courts, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet and check whether an expungement order was entered with the dismissal. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the criminal history report within 60 days before filing and attach it. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Records showing final release from confinement or supervision
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising county probation department or the Pennsylvania Department of Corrections
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only on the age-70 ground, to establish when the ten-year clock began.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising agency for confirmation of the final release date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified death certificate
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania Department of Health, Division of Vital Records
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only on the deceased ground.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a certified death certificate from Vital Records.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that the driving-privilege suspension was completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where a licence suspension was imposed for the offence.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a driver history from PennDOT showing the suspension was served and restoration completed. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the criminal history report within 60 days before filing and attach it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the pardon
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania Board of Pardons
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a copy of the pardon showing whether it was unconditional. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required only where the fallback Rule 790 petition is filed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the criminal history report within 60 days before filing and attach it to the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report from the Pennsylvania State Police within 60 days before filing and attach it to the petition, unless the attorney for the Commonwealth agrees to waive it. Because of the 60-day window, order it late in packet assembly. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Complete docket sheet showing every charge on the docket and the sentence imposed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of courts, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet showing every count, the grading, the sentence imposed and the restitution status.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report to see whether the record has been given limited access. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Public docket sheet
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Check whether the docket is still publicly viewable, which indicates whether limited access has been applied.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Rhode Island BCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Rhode Island Department of Attorney General, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your criminal history from the Attorney General's BCI unit. This is where the BCI number the court form requires comes from, and it is also how you check whether the record has already cleared automatically. LegalEase cannot make this request for you.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket showing counts, charges and dispositions
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the District, Superior or Family Court where the case occurred
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court where the case occurred for the docket, which shows the case number, every count, the charges and the dispositions the form requires.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that sentence and probation are complete
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court, or the probation department
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or the probation department for documentation showing the sentence, including any probation, is complete. The waiting period runs from completion of sentence, not from conviction, and probation can push that date years out.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that financial obligations are paid, waived or reduced by court order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a record showing fines, fees, costs, assessments and restitution are satisfied, or the court order waiving or reducing them.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Rhode Island BCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Rhode Island Department of Attorney General, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your criminal history from the Attorney General's BCI unit. participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a record showing fines, fees, costs, assessments and restitution are satisfied, or the court order waiving or reducing them.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The deferral agreement and the order showing completion of the deferred sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered the deferred sentence
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the deferral agreement and the final order. Any participant who says 'it was deferred so it went away' needs the final order checked, because a deferred sentence is not an automatic expungement.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Rhode Island BCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Rhode Island Department of Attorney General, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your criminal history from the Attorney General's BCI unit. This is how you find out whether the record has already sealed, which decides whether anything needs to be filed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket showing the non-conviction disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the case occurred
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket and the dismissal or acquittal entry, which establishes which sealing route applies and whether it was a Rule 48(a) dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket showing the complaint was placed on file
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the complaint was filed
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket showing the complaint was placed on file and the filing date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Rhode Island BCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Rhode Island Department of Attorney General, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Used to confirm the automatic expungement took effect.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your criminal history from the Attorney General's BCI unit.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Rhode Island BCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Rhode Island Department of Attorney General, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your criminal history from the Attorney General's BCI unit. This is how you confirm the marijuana record has already been expunged.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Rhode Island BCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Rhode Island Department of Attorney General, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your criminal history from the Attorney General's BCI unit; the BCI number is required on the court form.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and judgment showing the conviction and the original sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the conviction occurred
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket and judgment, which show the offence charged and the conditions of the original sentence.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that fines, fees and costs are paid in full
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a record showing the balance is zero. The no-cost expungement is conditioned on this.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and judgment for the underlying matter
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the case occurred
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtained with the referral partner, not through LegalEase.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Your attorney or survivor legal service will advise what to obtain. Do not send documents to LegalEase.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket or disposition sheet
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the magistrate or municipal court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the summary court clerk for the docket or disposition sheet. It carries the disposition date the thirty-day and appeal-expiration clocks run from, and it will usually show whether you were fingerprinted.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified or raised-seal copy of the completed expungement order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The summary court that issued it
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Section 17-22-950(D) requires the summary court to give you a copy of the completed order, certified or marked with the court's raised seal. Ask for it and keep it; it is your proof, and you will need it if a background check still shows the charge.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and certified disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the magistrate, municipal or General Sessions court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for the docket and, where available, a certified disposition. The docket carries the warrant or indictment number, the court level and the disposition date the application needs.

participantFilingRequirements.name: SLED criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is not required for this route, but it is the only reliable way to see every charge on your record before you choose which to apply for.
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended rather than required on this route, because § 17-22-940(E) does not require SLED verification for a § 17-1-40 expungement.

participantFilingRequirements.name: SLED criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is the record the solicitor's office and SLED work from, and it is the only reliable way to see every charge and disposition on your record before you choose which one to spend an application on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and certified disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the magistrate, municipal or General Sessions court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for the docket and, where available, a certified disposition. The docket carries the warrant or indictment number, the court level and the disposition date the application needs.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pretrial Intervention completion certificate or letter
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Circuit Pretrial Intervention office that administered the programme
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the PTI office for written confirmation that you successfully completed the programme and the date you completed it. You will be dealing with the same office for the attestation, so ask for both at once.

participantFilingRequirements.name: SLED criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is the record the solicitor's office and SLED work from, and it is the only reliable way to see every charge and disposition on your record before you choose which one to spend an application on.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The circuit solicitor's Alcohol Education Program office or its contracted provider
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the programme office for written confirmation that you successfully completed the programme and the completion date. Ask for the attestation at the same time.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The governmental agency that administered the programme, being the circuit solicitor's office or the county or municipality it contracted with
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the administering agency for written confirmation that you successfully completed the programme and the completion date, and ask for the attestation at the same time.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order of discharge and dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the general sessions or summary court that entered it
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for the order discharging you and dismissing the proceedings. Section 44-53-450(B) makes the court's determination that you were dismissed and discharged the whole of the expungement standard, so this is the document the order turns on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Sentencing sheet or judgment showing the statutory penalty for the offence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the sentencing sheet or judgment. The statutory penalty ceiling, not the sentence you actually received, is what decides eligibility under § 22-5-910(A), and it must be taken from the record rather than from memory.

participantFilingRequirements.name: SLED criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is the record the solicitor's office and SLED work from, and it is the only reliable way to see every charge and disposition on your record before you choose which one to spend an application on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and certified disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the magistrate, municipal or General Sessions court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for the docket and, where available, a certified disposition. The docket carries the warrant or indictment number, the court level and the disposition date the application needs.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Sentencing sheet or judgment showing a Youthful Offender Act sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the General Sessions court that sentenced the participant
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the sentencing sheet or judgment and check that it records a sentence under the Youthful Offender Act, Chapter 19 of Title 24. Being eligible for a youthful offender sentence is not the same as having received one, and this route needs the second. Check the paperwork rather than your recollection.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Written confirmation that probation and parole ended
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The South Carolina Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the sentence included probation or parole, which the five-year clock runs from the completion of.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services for written confirmation of the date your supervision ended. The five-year clock runs from completion of the whole sentence including probation and parole, not from the conviction.

participantFilingRequirements.name: SLED criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is the record the solicitor's office and SLED work from, and it is the only reliable way to see every charge and disposition on your record before you choose which one to spend an application on.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for the docket and, where available, a certified disposition. The docket carries the warrant or indictment number, the court level and the disposition date the application needs.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Written confirmation that probation and parole ended
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The South Carolina Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the sentence included probation or parole, which both clocks run from the completion of.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services for written confirmation of the date your supervision ended. Both the three-year and the twenty-year clock run from completion of the sentence including probation and parole, not from the conviction date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: SLED criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is the record the solicitor's office and SLED work from, and it is the only reliable way to see every charge and disposition on your record before you choose which one to spend an application on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and certified disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the magistrate, municipal or General Sessions court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for the docket and, where available, a certified disposition. The docket carries the warrant or indictment number, the court level and the disposition date the application needs.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Sentencing sheet and proof that every term and condition was completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that sentenced the participant, and the supervising probation office where applicable
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the sentencing sheet, which shows the subsection you were convicted under and whether it was a felony, and for proof that fines, restitution and any other condition are satisfied. The three-year clock runs from the date the last of those was completed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: SLED criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is the record the solicitor's office and SLED work from, and it is the only reliable way to see every charge and disposition on your record before you choose which one to spend an application on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and certified disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the magistrate, municipal or General Sessions court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for the docket and, where available, a certified disposition. The docket carries the warrant or indictment number, the court level and the disposition date the application needs.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Sentencing sheet or judgment identifying the statute of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the General Sessions court that sentenced the participant
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the sentencing sheet or judgment and check that it names S.C. Code § 16-23-20 and that the conviction date is before 7 March 2024. Both are findings the order requires and neither can be taken from recollection.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order of dismissal, judgment of acquittal, or proof that no accusatory instrument was filed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of Courts for the court with jurisdiction over the arrest
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Clerk of Courts for a copy of the dismissal order or the judgment of acquittal. Where no charging document was ever filed, ask the clerk to confirm in writing that no case exists.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket for the underlying case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of Courts
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where a case was opened.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Clerk of Courts for the case docket, which shows whether every charge was dismissed or only some.

participantFilingRequirements.name: South Dakota criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Dakota Division of Criminal Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended where the participant is unsure how many separate arrest records exist.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a criminal history record from the DCI. LegalEase cannot make this request for you.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Diversion agreement and proof of successful completion
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The State's Attorney's office that administered the diversion program
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the State's Attorney's office for the diversion agreement and written confirmation that you completed the program, including the completion date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket for the diverted charges
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of Courts
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Used to check whether the dismissal and notice have been filed and whether the expungement has been granted.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Clerk of Courts for the case docket and look for the dismissal, the notice of completion and any expungement order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket showing the charges and the satisfaction of court-ordered conditions
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of Courts
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended where the participant is unsure of the highest charged offence or whether conditions were satisfied.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Clerk of Courts for the case docket, which shows every charge and whether fines, costs and other conditions were satisfied.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Suspended imposition of sentence order, and the discharge and dismissal order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of Courts

participantFilingRequirements.name: Texas DPS criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district clerk of the county where the petition will be filed
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant needs a document rather than a screen, for an employer or licensing body.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Current balance statement for any criminal accounts receivable or state debt

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant is unsure whether any balance remains outstanding.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the case balance and the Office of State Debt Collection whether a criminal accounts receivable was transferred to it. An outstanding balance is an express bar to clean slate expungement.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Utah Department of Public Safety, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Submit the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History with the application fee, or with a fee waiver request. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases and may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction. If eligible, BCI issues the certificate on payment of the issuance fee. File the court packet within 180 days of issuance.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that handled the case, and the Office of State Debt Collection where a criminal accounts receivable was transferred

An unpaid balance defeats the petition and will also defeat the BCI certificate.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own treating clinician or medical provider
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clinician who treated the condition for records covering the date of the arrest or citation. participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that entered the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the judgment. It carries the conviction date and the offence as charged.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order of dismissal in the criminal case

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a copy of the dismissal order. It carries the dismissal date the 30-day clock runs from and shows the charges, which is what the domestic violence screen turns on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the district court expungement order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the district court that granted the expungement
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a certified copy within 28 days after the order is granted, as URCrP 42 requires. Standing Order No. 12 requires the certified order to be filed with the appellate petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the district court expungement petition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own file, or the clerk of the district court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Standing Order No. 12 requires a copy of the district court petition to accompany the appellate petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the judgment showing the current conviction level
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that entered the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the judgment. It shows the offence level as it currently stands, and it will show a reduction if one has already been granted.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The participant's own Virginia criminal history record from the CCRE
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Virginia State Police, Central Criminal Records Exchange
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own copy from the CCRE for the fee they charge. This is a different thing from the court's copy: you must separately ask the CCRE to forward a copy electronically to the circuit court as part of the petition. The Norfolk clerk's guidance is that the case is established with the court first and the State Police request comes second, so the sequence matters.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the circuit court of the locality where the case was disposed of for the case papers. District court charges are handled by that locality's circuit court, so that is where to ask even for a general district court charge.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the warrant, summons or indictment
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Section 19.2-392.2(C) requires it to be filed with the petition where reasonably available.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a copy of the charging document. If it is not reasonably available, the petition states the reason for the unavailability instead.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the absolute pardon

participantFilingRequirements.name: Vermont Judiciary criminal record search result for each county
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Criminal Division of the Superior Court in each county where the participant had a case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Complete Form 200-00331, Request for Criminal Record Search, and email, mail or hand deliver it to the court in each county. A separate request is required for each county, and there is a fee. A free in-person search is available at a courthouse Public Access Terminal, with a charge to print.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Vermont Crime Information Center criminal conviction record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Vermont Crime Information Center
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the statewide conviction record from VCIC online, by mail, by email or in person. There is a fee, which moves and must be read from VCIC at intake rather than stored. The Judiciary record gives the docket and disposition detail the petition needs; the VCIC record gives the statewide picture the qualifying-crime and prior-conviction screens need.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that restitution and surcharges are paid in full on every conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Restitution Unit of the Vermont Center for Crime Victim Services, and the court that imposed each sentence
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Restitution Unit for a current balance and the sentencing court for any outstanding surcharge. The condition reaches restitution and surcharges on any crime of which the participant has been convicted, not only the offence being cleared.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the judgment of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Criminal Division of the Superior Court in the county that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the judgment. It carries the exact statute of conviction, which is what the decriminalisation showing turns on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order discharging the participant from probation and striking the adjudication of guilt
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Criminal Division of the Superior Court that entered the deferred sentence
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the discharge order. It establishes the date the § 7041(e) duty attached.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Restitution Unit statement showing restitution paid in full
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Restitution Unit of the Vermont Center for Crime Victim Services
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Restitution Unit for a current balance. Section 7041(e) bars expungement until restitution is paid in full, so this is the fact that most often explains a missing order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Washington State Patrol criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Washington State Patrol

It supplies the cause number, the exact RCW, the offence class, the sentencing date and the supervision and release dates. Every Washington waiting period runs from one of those dates and none of them is reliably on the $11 WATCH check.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Washington State Patrol criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Washington State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Get your WSP criminal history before anything is signed. On this route the declaration about previous domestic violence convictions is both an eligibility condition and a statement under penalty of perjury, and a forgotten out-of-state conviction turns a good-faith declaration into a false statement. The $11 WATCH check is the starting point; a fingerprint-based record is more complete.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of completion of any ordered treatment
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The treatment provider or the supervising agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the sentence ordered treatment, because the five-year clock runs from completion of the conditions including that treatment.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the treatment provider or the supervising agency for written confirmation of the completion date. That date, not the sentencing date and not the date fines were paid, usually starts the five-year clock.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Washington State Patrol criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Washington State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The $11 WATCH name and date-of-birth check online gives conviction information immediately and is enough to start routing. The non-conviction record is a different and slower product: it needs a fingerprint card plus $12, or an in-person record review at no fee with fingerprints and limited inspection time. Read the WSP fee table live rather than relying on a stored figure.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of completion of a substance use disorder programme, or the programme assessment with a written status update
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The substance use disorder programme, or the recovery navigator, arrest and jail alternative, or law enforcement assisted diversion programme
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the programme for written proof that you completed it, or, on the assessment path, for the assessment together with a written status update showing six months of substantial compliance with the recommended treatment or services and progress toward your recovery goals. This documentation is the whole evidentiary basis of the mandatory outcome, so it goes with the petition.

Every Washington waiting period runs from one of those dates and none of them is reliably on the $11 WATCH check.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of tribal membership
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The tribe of which the person was a member
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the tribe for written confirmation of membership. The court must find that the person is a member of a tribe that may exercise treaty Indian fishing rights at the location where the offence occurred, and the tribe is the only source for the first half of that.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of the applicant's authority where the subject has died
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The tribe, or family records
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where a family member or an official tribal representative applies on behalf of a deceased person.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Where you are applying for a relative who has died, bring proof of the family relationship, or, if you are applying as an official representative of the tribe, the tribe's written designation.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Death certificate or equivalent record of the homicide
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Washington State Department of Health, or the court or law enforcement agency that handled the homicide
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: A death certificate is usually the simplest proof. Where the homicide was prosecuted, the court file or the police report will also establish it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket for the prostitution conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case. If you do not have a cause number they can usually search by name and date of birth.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certificate of discharge under RCW 9.94A.637
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing superior court, on the Department of Corrections' or the participant's own motion
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the sentencing superior court whether a certificate of discharge has been entered, and if not, how to obtain one. WashingtonLawHelp states that a person usually needs the certificate before filing for felony vacation, and a participant who has completed their sentence but never obtained one is not ready to file.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Judgment and sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing superior court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the superior court clerk for the judgment and sentence. It carries the felony class, the exact RCW and any enhancement, none of which may be taken from the participant's description.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing superior court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the superior court clerk for the judgment and sentence, which carries the felony class the clean period depends on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Probation papers and the order of discharge from probation
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court, or the supervising probation office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or the probation office for the probation papers and any order discharging you from probation. RCW 9.95.240(1) says the probationer is to be informed of this right in their probation papers, so the papers themselves often say so.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Washington State Patrol non-conviction criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Washington State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: This route needs the non-conviction record, not the $11 WATCH check. The non-conviction record requires a fingerprint card plus $12, or an in-person record review at no fee with fingerprints and limited inspection time. Read the WSP fee table live rather than relying on a stored figure.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court record of the disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where charges were filed and a court disposed of them. Not applicable where no charges were ever filed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket or the order of dismissal, which fixes the favourable-disposition date the two-year period runs from.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Washington State Patrol criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Washington State Patrol
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The $11 WATCH name and date-of-birth check online gives conviction information immediately and is enough to start routing. participantFilingRequirements.name: Payment history for the case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court, or the collections agency the court used
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk, or the collections agency the court used, for a full payment history on the cause number. The refund is of what you actually paid plus accrued interest, so the payment history is what the claim is built on.
