It supplies the cause number, the exact RCW, the offence class, the sentencing date and the supervision and release dates. Every Washington waiting period runs from one of those dates and none of them is reliably on the $11 WATCH check.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Legal financial obligation balance and payment plan status
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court, or the collections agency the court used
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or the collections agency for the current balance and the payment plan status. RCW 9.97.010(1)(b) makes compliance an eligibility element, with three ways to satisfy it including good cause established with the court for non-compliance.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Judgment of conviction, or the sentencing transcript or minutes
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of circuit court for the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of circuit court for the judgment of conviction and, if the judgment is silent, the sentencing transcript or minutes. This is where the at-sentencing expungement order appears.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of discharge from probation or confinement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Department of Corrections or the detaining authority
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising agent or the detaining authority for the discharge documentation showing the sentence terms were completed and probation was not revoked.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Wisconsin DOJ criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Wisconsin Department of Justice, Crime Information Bureau
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended so the participant sees what remains after the court record clears.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a background check through the Wisconsin DOJ. There is a fee for the background check itself.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Judgment of conviction, or the sentencing transcript or minutes
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of circuit court for the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Useful to enclose so the authority can see that expungement was ordered at sentencing.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of circuit court for the judgment of conviction and, where it is silent, the sentencing transcript or minutes.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of discharge from probation or confinement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Department of Corrections or the detaining authority
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Useful to enclose where the participant already holds it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising agent or the detaining authority for the discharge documentation showing the sentence terms were completed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Judgment of conviction, or the sentencing transcript or minutes
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of circuit court for the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of circuit court for the judgment of conviction, and the sentencing transcript or minutes where the judgment is silent. This is the document that proves the expungement was ordered at sentencing.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that the sentence was completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of circuit court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for records showing any fine, costs or other sentence terms were satisfied.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Judgment of conviction, or the sentencing transcript or minutes
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of circuit court for the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of circuit court for the judgment of conviction and, where it is silent, the sentencing transcript or minutes. This establishes both the offence charged and whether the mandatory expungement order was entered.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified records of federal or state court proceedings
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the relevant court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Named because § 973.015(2m)(c) lists it as evidence the motion may include. The referral partner decides what is used.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Your attorney or legal aid provider will advise what to obtain. Do not send documents to LegalEase.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Approval notices, law enforcement certifications or similar documents from federal immigration proceedings
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The relevant federal agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Named because § 973.015(2m)(c)2 lists it as evidence the motion may include.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Your attorney or legal aid provider will advise. Do not send documents to LegalEase.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Wisconsin DOJ criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Wisconsin Department of Justice, Crime Information Bureau
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a background check through the Wisconsin DOJ system. This is the record that shows the arrest event and every charge tied to the fingerprint card, and it is the document the all-charges-cleared screen must be run against. The background check is fee-based.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Disposition or non-prosecution documentation for every charge in the arrest event
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of circuit court, or the district attorney's office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of circuit court for the dismissal order, judgment of acquittal or docket entry for each charge; where no charges were filed, ask the district attorney's office to confirm in writing.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Fingerprints taken by a fingerprint technician
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A law enforcement agency or commercial fingerprinting service
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: DJ-LE-250B requires fingerprints. Have them taken by a fingerprint technician and submit them with the request. LegalEase cannot complete this step.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Wisconsin DOJ criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Wisconsin Department of Justice, Crime Information Bureau
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a background check through the Wisconsin DOJ system. This is the record being challenged, so it must be in hand.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court record showing the correct disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of circuit court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of circuit court for the judgment, dismissal order or docket entry that shows what actually happened.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Form CR-214, Judgment Deferred Under 961.47, and the order of discharge and dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of circuit court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of circuit court for the deferred judgment record and the order discharging you and dismissing the case. These establish the non-conviction status that unlocks the DOJ removal route.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Wisconsin DOJ criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Wisconsin Department of Justice, Crime Information Bureau
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Needed before the DOJ fingerprint removal handoff, to map the arrest event.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a background check through the Wisconsin DOJ system.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the order of acquittal or dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit, magistrate or municipal clerk of the court that disposed of the charge
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for a certified copy of the order of acquittal or dismissal. The order carries the date the 60-day clock runs from and, usually, the stated reason for dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pretrial diversion agreement or deferred adjudication order and the order of completion
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit or magistrate clerk of the court that entered it, or the prosecuting attorney's office that signed the diversion agreement
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the case ended in completion of a § 61-11-22 diversion or a § 61-11-22a deferred adjudication.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the diversion agreement or deferred adjudication order and the order recording full and successful completion. Which of the two it was decides whether the family-or-household-member carve-out applies at all.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction on the inventory
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit or magistrate clerk of the county of disposition
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the county of disposition for a certified copy of the disposition, the judgment order and the sentencing order for each case. Most counties charge a per-copy fee. Ask for every case, not only the one you came in for, because the petition is once per lifetime.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of supervision completion
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising probation office, and the institution of confinement where applicable
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the probation office that supervised you for written confirmation of the date supervision ended, and the institution of confinement for the date of release. The waiting period runs from the later of conviction, release and end of supervision, so this date is usually the one that decides eligibility.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of any current restitution, protection, restraining or no-contact order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered the order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where such an order is currently in force. Section 61-11-26(d)(7) requires a current order to be attached to the petition.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered the order for a copy. The statute requires a current order to be attached to the petition; a past order is disclosed but not attached.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the order of acquittal or dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the circuit, magistrate or municipal court that disposed of the charge
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled your case for a certified copy of the order of acquittal or dismissal. Check the date on it against the date you gave us: the 60-day clock runs from that order, not from the day the case felt over.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the docket sheet or the plea agreement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that disposed of the charge
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the order does not make clear whether the dismissal was in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket sheet, and for the plea agreement if there was one. This is the record that shows whether the dismissal was traded for a plea to something else, which is the one fact that decides whether this route is open.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the order of dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the circuit or magistrate court that entered it
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order dismissing the charges after you completed the programme. Check its date against the date you gave us; the 60-day clock runs from that order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pretrial diversion agreement, or the deferred adjudication order, together with the record of full and successful completion
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered it, or the prosecuting attorney's office that signed the diversion agreement
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the deferred adjudication order, or the prosecuting attorney's office for the signed diversion agreement, and for whatever the court entered recording that you completed it. Which of the two it was decides whether the family-or-household-member carve-out applies at all, so bring the document rather than relying on memory.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit or magistrate clerk of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the county of conviction for certified copies of the disposition, the judgment order and the sentencing order. Check the conviction date and the sentence against the answers you gave us.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Written proof that supervision ended
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The probation office that supervised you, or the institution of confinement
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where a period of supervision was ordered or a sentence of incarceration was served.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising probation office for written confirmation of the date supervision ended, and the institution of confinement for the release date. This is usually the date that decides whether the one-year period has run.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of any current restitution, protection, restraining or no-contact order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered the order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where such an order is currently in force. Section 61-11-26(d)(7) requires a current order to be attached to the petition.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered it for a copy, and attach it to the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction in the group
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit or magistrate clerk of each county of disposition
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of each county of disposition for certified copies for every case in the group. Because this petition is once per lifetime, pull records for every conviction you might ever want cleared, not just the urgent one.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Written proof that supervision ended on the most recent conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The probation office that supervised you, or the institution of confinement
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising probation office for written confirmation of the date supervision ended on the most recent conviction, and the institution of confinement for the release date. The two-year clock runs from the later of those and the last conviction.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of any current restitution, protection, restraining or no-contact order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered the order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where such an order is currently in force.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered it for a copy, and attach it to the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit clerk of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the circuit clerk of the county of conviction for certified copies of the disposition, judgment order and sentencing order, and for the indictment or information. Check the conviction date and sentence against the answers you gave us.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Written proof of release and of supervision completion
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The institution of confinement and the supervising probation or parole office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the institution for the release date and the supervising office for written confirmation of the date supervision ended. On a felony the five-year clock almost always runs from one of these, not from the conviction date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of any current restitution, protection, restraining or no-contact order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered the order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where such an order is currently in force.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered it for a copy, and attach it to the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Documentation of compliance with an approved substance abuse treatment or recovery and counselling programme
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The treatment or recovery programme provider, which must be approved by the Secretary of the Department of Health
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the participant relies on treatment or recovery compliance under § 61-11-26a(a).
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the programme provider for written documentation of your compliance, covering the dates you were in the programme, and ask them to confirm in writing that the programme is approved by the Secretary of the Department of Health. Section 61-11-26a(b)(1) requires this to be included in the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certificate of graduation from an approved job readiness adult training course
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The course provider, under a West Virginia Department of Education approved course
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the participant relies on job readiness graduation under § 61-11-26a(a).
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the course provider for your certificate of graduation and for written confirmation that the course is approved by the West Virginia Department of Education. Section 61-11-26a(b)(2) requires the certificate to be included in the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Medical documentation of a history of substance abuse
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The treating clinician, treatment provider or medical records department
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only on the treatment branch, where § 61-11-26a(a)(1) requires a medically documented history of substance abuse alongside compliance.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask your treating clinician or the treatment provider for records documenting the history of substance abuse. LegalEase does not see, hold or assess these records; you attach them to the petition yourself.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit or magistrate clerk of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the county of conviction for certified copies for each case, and check the dates against the answers you gave us.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Conditional discharge order and the order of discharge and dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered them
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for certified copies of the order deferring proceedings and placing you on probation, and of the later order discharging you and dismissing the proceedings. Both dates matter and they are usually different.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Written confirmation of the date the probation term expired
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The probation office that supervised the participant
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising probation office for written confirmation of the date your probation term expired. The six-month clock runs from that date, not from the dismissal, and the two are often months apart.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Receipt or clerk's confirmation that court costs were paid
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that assessed them
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where court costs were assessed under § 60A-4-407(c) and the participant is unsure whether they are satisfied.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a payment history or a receipt showing the assessed costs are paid.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Division of Motor Vehicles record of Motor Vehicle Test and Lock Program completion
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Division of Motor Vehicles for the record showing you successfully completed the test and lock program, and the completion date. This is the fact the court's duty to dismiss and expunge turns on.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order of dismissal and the docket entry
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court in which the charge was pending
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the order dismissing the charge and for the docket entry. If the docket still shows the charge as open or convicted, that is the mismatch to raise with the clerk.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Division of Motor Vehicles certification of successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Division of Motor Vehicles for written certification that you successfully completed the test and lock program. Section 17C-5-2b(c) requires the motion to dismiss to be supported by this certification, so it must be attached before you file that motion.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order deferring proceedings and imposing probation
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered it
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order deferring the proceedings and placing you on probation. It carries the probation term the one-year expungement clock is measured from.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order of dismissal and discharge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered it
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the expungement stage, where the dismissal has already been entered.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order dismissing the charges and discharging you.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Written confirmation of the date the probation term expired
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The probation office that supervised the participant, or the clerk of the court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the expungement stage, because the one-year clock runs from the expiration of probation.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising probation office, or the clerk, for written confirmation of the date your probation term expired. This date, not the dismissal date, starts the one-year period.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The instrument of pardon
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Office of the Governor, or the Secretary of State
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a certified copy of the pardon. The court must verify the act of pardon, and whether it is full and unconditional is the threshold question on this route.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified judgment and sentencing orders for the pardoned conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit clerk of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the circuit clerk of the county of conviction for certified copies of the judgment and sentencing orders.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Record showing the date the sentence was discharged
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Division of Corrections and Rehabilitation, the supervising parole or probation office, or the circuit clerk
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the agency that supervised you, or the clerk, for written confirmation of the date the sentence was discharged. The five-year period runs from that date and it is usually later than the conviction date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Publisher's affidavit of publication of the Class I legal advertisement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The newspaper that publishes the notice
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: After the notice runs, ask the newspaper for its affidavit of publication and file it with the court. This is how the court is shown the publication requirement was met; LegalEase cannot arrange or prove publication for you.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Wyoming DCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation, Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended wherever the participant does not know whether the arrest reached the state central repository.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a personal criminal history record from the DCI Criminal Records Unit. A Wyoming record exists only where an arrest fingerprint card was submitted; if none was submitted the arrest will not appear on the state or FBI record, and DCI cannot create an arrest event from court documents alone.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket or case history for the underlying matter
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court in which the proceeding occurred
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where charges were filed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court for the docket and the order of dismissal or other disposition for the case.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified judgment and sentence for the misdemeanor conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting court for a certified copy of the judgment and sentence. Most clerks charge a per-copy fee.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that probation and any court-ordered program were completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising probation office, or the clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the probation office or the court for the discharge or completion documentation showing the date the terms of sentence expired. This is what establishes the start of the one-year or five-year clock.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Wyoming DCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation, Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended where the participant does not know what the state record shows, and where the court requests a DCI report.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a personal criminal history record from the DCI Criminal Records Unit.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified judgment and sentence for the felony conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting court for a certified copy of the judgment and sentence.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that probation and any court-ordered program were completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising probation office, or the clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the probation office or the court for the discharge or completion documentation showing the date the terms of sentence expired; the ten-year clock runs from that date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that court-ordered restitution was paid in full
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where restitution was ordered.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting court for a payoff or satisfaction record showing the restitution balance is zero.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Wyoming DCI criminal history record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation, Criminal Records Unit
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended because the other-felony bar looks at the entire record, and because the court may request a DCI report.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a personal criminal history record from the DCI Criminal Records Unit.
